#62383. Are We There Yet? NASA’s Escapade Is Heading to Mars in a ‘Pioneering’ Maneuver

📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (770 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cnet ↗ Open Full Page

Are We There Yet? NASA’s Escapade Is Heading to Mars in a ‘Pioneering’ Maneuver

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (770 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, NASA rolled out its Escapade mission just over a year ago to send two spacecraft, nicknamed Blue and Gold, to Mars.
  • Blue and Gold, named for the school colors of UC Berkeley where they were built, completed the agency’s first powered Earth flyby.
  • Recent findings suggest that typically, spacecraft use a planet’s or the sun’s gravity to get close to the planet before slingshotting off into the distance.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, NASA rolled out its Escapade mission just over a year ago to send two spacecraft, nicknamed Blue and Gold, to Mars. After spending a year looping near Earth, the twin probes completed a gravity-assist maneuver this month and are now en route to the red planet.

It’s an exciting time for NASA. Blue and Gold, named for the school colors of UC Berkeley where they were built, completed the agency’s first powered Earth flyby.

Recent findings suggest that typically, spacecraft use a planet’s or the sun’s gravity to get close to the planet before slingshotting off into the distance. A notable example is Voyager 1, which used unpowered gravity-assisted flybys to reach the speeds needed to cross the light-day threshold earlier this week. Escapade did this with Earth’s gravity but also used thrusters to generate even more speed. Since there are two of them, NASA personnel had to perform this maneuver twice.

The other substantial win for NASA is that Mars will soon have two additional satellites in orbit to measure the planet’s magnetosphere, which is believed to have been stripped by the solar wind eons ago, when the planet likely had liquid water.

These satellites are notable for being NASA’s first low-cost mission to Mars, costing the agency approximately $75 million as part of the Small Innovative Missions for Planetary Exploration program. It also marked the debut of Blue Origin’s Fresh Glenn rocket for a space mission, and the manufacturer was able to achieve the first vertical landing of its rocket after sending Escapade on its way.

It has been revealed that escapade still has a long way to go. Blue and Gold are now spending the next 10 months flying into outer space. Their fresh trajectory is set to take them into Mars’ orbital path, timed in such a way that the twin satellites will arrive at the same time that Mars naturally reveals up, allowing the red planet to capture the twins in its orbit as it flies by. NASA states that both are set to arrive at Mars by early September next year.

Sources indicate that by the time the twins get there, they will have been in space for 22 months. Flights to Mars require months of deep space travel, impeccable timing and loads of fuel. However, if missions hit specific launch windows, they require far less fuel.

According to recent reports, this is a well-documented maneuver known as the Hohmann Transfer, and NASA’s JPL has a neat math exercise to show how it’s calculated. NASA intentionally launched Escapade a year early so that the satellites could hang out in a gravitational sweet spot called the L2 Earth-Sun Lagrange point. This is a point in space on the side of the Earth opposite the sun, and the idea was to have the spacecraft already in orbit and ready for the next Mars launch window.

Once it opened, the satellites engaged their thrusters, performed a gravity-assisted flyby of Earth to gain speed, and rolled out themselves into outer space.

The tactic of sending Escapade to the L2 Lagrange point to wait for a Mars window to open is arguably NASA’s biggest win, as no space agency has ever attempted it. The benefit is that it allows agencies to launch payloads into orbit bound for Mars whenever they have the time, then use Earth gravity assists to slingshot them out to Mars when it’s most efficient.

Recent findings suggest that “With this loiter orbit and Earth flyby, Escapade is pioneering a new strategy for getting to Mars,” Jeff Parker, CTO of Advanced Space and lead mission designer, said in a statement. “This method provides the flexibility to launch almost anytime and then use Earth’s gravity to get a boost to Mars, rather than waiting every two years to launch there directly when the planets are aligned.”.

The maneuver paid dividends. JAXA, Japan’s national space agency, rolled out its MMX spacecraft on Oct. 20, which is within the current Mars launch window and employs the same Hohmann Transfer method to get to Mars. The spacecraft is headed to Phobos and Deimos, Mars’s moons.

Recent findings suggest that despite using the more traditional method of waiting for the window to open to launch, JAXA’s MMX is slated to reach its destination in August next year, just a couple of weeks ahead of Escapade. When you factor in that Escapade performed its gravity-assist slingshot on Nov. 9, roughly two weeks before MMX rolled out, the spacecraft will reach their respective destinations in approximately the same amount of time, validating NASA’s trajectory strategy.

10 stocks we like better than S&P 500 Index ›.

The S&P 500 (^GSPC -3.70%) has experienced a wild ride lately, as several market-moving events all converged in the first half of November: midterm election results, a hot inflation report, and Jensen Huang's resignation from Nvidia. There are sure to be many more major days in the stock market, but Dec. 9 is lining up to be absolutely massive for investors.

There are three significant events taking place that day, and investors should prepare for how each could impact the market.

Here's how each event could move the market.

The next FOMC meeting concludes on Dec. 9 and chair Kevin Warsh is expected to hold a press conference discussing its target fed funds rate decision. Futures traders currently expect the committee to raise the target rate by 25 basis points, with an outside chance of a 50-basis-point increase. Expectations for a rate increase were significantly lower before the most recent inflation report, which highlighted prices rising faster than expected.

Sources indicate that higher interest rates tend to keep stock prices lower, as investors are pushed to discount earnings at a higher rate. Higher interest rates are especially relevant in today's market, where many of the largest companies in the S&P 500 have become extremely capital-intensive, relying on outside funding to fuel their growth.

Industry observers note that while the rate decision is important, it's unlikely the Fed will do anything that surprises the market and causes a significant move in prices in and of itself. What may be more telling is Warsh's comments at the press conference. While he's aimed to reduce how much telegraphing he does about the Fed's future rate plans, his comments could provide some indication of what he and the committee are watching ahead of the next meeting.

According to recent reports, broadcom is one of the most crucial chipmakers in the artificial intelligence space. It's the leading developer of custom AI accelerators used by hyperscalers and leading AI labs. Investors will be paying close attention to its earnings report, in particular, its AI semiconductor revenue.

NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

Recent findings suggest that management said it expects AI semiconductor revenue to accelerate to $21.7 billion, up 236% year over year for the quarter. A shortfall could indicate the shift to custom silicon isn't moving as rapidly as expected or that hyperscalers simply can't build as quickly as anticipated. The former would be bad news for several other companies that make custom AI chips, while the latter would be bad news for the entire semiconductor industry.

On the flip side, a good report and better-than-expected outlook could provide a boost to Broadcom stock and the rest of the industry. It could particularly benefit Alphabet and Anthropic, its two largest partners.

It has been revealed that micron boosted its share repurchase authorization from $2.16 billion to $35.16 billion in October, but there's a substantial catch. The company is not legally allowed to repurchase more shares than it issues for stock-based compensation until Dec. 9. That's due to receiving Chip Act funding from the U.S. government in 2024.

NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

Micron will likely do its best not to move the market for its stock, but it could be a huge buyer for the shares at depressed levels. The stock is down about 40% from its peak this summer and 29.5% since the board authorized the repurchase in October.

The confidence of a major buyer in Micron stock could support the stock price of one of the largest semiconductor stocks in the S&P 500. And if Micron's management is buying the stock around the current level, it could encourage other investors to buy its competitors and other AI stocks that have come down in price. Management may provide an patch on its buyback program again with its quarterly earnings report in December, giving investors a better idea of how big a buyer of its own stock it will be.

With the explosion of vinyl came a corresponding flood of turntables, but among them all the Fluance RT82 is my pick for the best turntable. Yet, for those who want a step up, the organization now offers the RT86 Reference High Fidelity Vinyl Turntable.

The Fluance RT86 seems to have made improvements in the areas that matter most, including a newly introduced nine-inch carbon fiber tonearm and better vibration isolation.

Industry observers note that firstly, the turntable is driven by a servo-controlled belt-drive motor, which uses an optical sensor to regulate speed. Next, the RT86 includes a nine-inch carbon fiber tonearm with adjustable VTA, which helps to level cartridges of varying heights, and a removable headshell which lets you install multiple cartridges more easily.

Sources indicate that the Fluance includes a 4.1-pound antiresonant acrylic platter. The platter sits on a high-mass wood plinth with a motor isolation system and adjustable isolation feet.

Sources indicate that in addition, buyers now have a choice of two different cartridges: the Audio-Technica AT-VM95ML Microlinear cartridge or the Ortofon 2M Blue. Having tested the 2M Blue as part of the RT85, I would suggest users opt for the Audio-Technica as I found the Ortofon too bright for that setup.

At its price of $700, it’s even cheaper than the Pro-Ject Debut Carbon EVO 2, which is the turntable to beat under $1,000. The Fluance RT86 is available now.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Google Wallet app is available for iPhone users in the US for the first time.
  • Also: You can use Google’s Spark AI agent, renamed Tasks, for free now – with limits.
  • It has been revealed that the newly introduced Google Wallet app lets you digitize physical cards, including payment, loyalty, and membership cards, as well as boarding passes.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Google Wallet app is available for iPhone users in the US for the first time. iOS users who download the new Google Wallet app can manage online payments for faster checkout at places that support Google Pay. However, Apple restricts Google’s ability to offer tap-to-pay service on the iOS app, so users won’t be able to use Google Wallet for contactless checkout on iPhone.

Also: You can use Google’s Spark AI agent, renamed Tasks, for free now – with limits.

It has been revealed that the newly introduced Google Wallet app lets you digitize physical cards, including payment, loyalty, and membership cards, as well as boarding passes. Google Wallet app consumers on iOS will also be able to view receipts and track orders pulled from Gmail in one app.

Industry observers note that there used to be a Google Pay app for iOS, but it was discontinued in 2024. The old Google Pay app also didn’t support tap-to-pay on iPhone, but it offered limited functionality, including support for loyalty and gift cards, as well as purchase tracking.

The biggest difference between the old Google Pay app for iOS and the new Google Wallet is the AI component, which supports agentic shopping, likely as Google’s longer-term play.

Industry observers note that one of Google’s goals for the Wallet app on iOS is to make it a central place to manage purchases made by its AI agents. The Agents section in Google Wallet for iPhone lets you manage and monitor purchases made through Gemini.

Agentic commerce is on the rise, as evidenced by the growing use of Meta’s Muse. Gemini can make purchases and payments through the Tasks feature, which lets you give Gemini permission to buy the items you want and set your maximum budget.

Also: Google Wallet just turned your Android phone into a digital house key.

It has been revealed that the Google Wallet app for iOS becomes the central hub for purchase management in agentic commerce through Gemini. In it, you can view active tasks to see which purchases Gemini is working on, as well as completed purchases and receipts.

Google has been working on two technologies to support its agentic commerce strategy: Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) and Agent Payments Protocol (AP2).

UCP is a technical language that enables AI agents to communicate with retailers and make purchases, while AP2 is the payment framework that establishes rules and authorization for agents to make payments.

Google Wallet serves as both the AI-powered wallet and the consumer-facing record of transactions made by Gemini.

Also: Google Wallet has a lot of latest tricks – these 5 are my favorites.

Recent findings suggest that along with Google, major retailers supported the development of UCP, including Shopify, Walmart, Target, and Etsy. When Google unveiled AP2, more than 60 organizations became involved, including PayPal, Salesforce, Mastercard, and American Express.

Loads of limited-time Black Friday-related streaming sales are happening right now, but one newly introduced discount that’s here to stay is DIRECTV’s brand-new streaming bundle that rolls Netflix, HBO Max and Apple TV all into one plan that can be added to almost any of their subscription packages.

This week, DirecTV rolled out a bundle that combines Netflix, HBO Max and Apple TV at a discount while aiming to help streamline billing in one place. Customers with any DirecTV Signature or Genre Pack can add this bundle to their plan, with two notable exceptions: the MyEntertainment genre plan or Premier package are not eligible, as both aims already include HBO Max.

There are two tiers to choose from with the new bundles: a Value strategy, which runs $28 per month (in addition to any monthly live TV subscription fees) and carries Netflix Standard with Ads, HBO Max’s ad-based plan and Apple TV, or the Deluxe plan, an ad-free option that costs $43.50 a month and includes Netflix Standard, HBO Max Standard and Apple TV. Either bundle can be added to or canceled from your existing plan at any time.

Right now, if you want to watch all the best shows, live sports and news programs, they’re scattered across multiple services, and this bundle offers you three of the most robust services out there, while skirting their latest price increases.

10 stocks we like better than Coinbase Global ›.

Modern finance is rapidly splitting between the established credit networks of old and the emerging digital asset economy. Choosing between Coinbase Global (COIN -6.34%) and Mastercard (MA -0.14%) means deciding which infrastructure will dominate the future of money.

Coinbase Global provides the primary gateway for users to enter the digital asset world, offering everything from trading to custody. Mastercard remains a global powerhouse in traditional payments, leveraging its massive network to facilitate billions of transactions. Comparing these two requires balancing the explosive growth potential of crypto against the proven reliability of global payment rails.

It has been revealed that coinbase Global operates at the intersection of traditional finance and fintech stocks by providing a platform for consumers, institutions, and developers. The tech giant manages a vast ecosystem including more than 245,000 partners and serves users in over 100 countries. A central part of its strategy involves its partnership with Circle for the USDC stablecoin, which provides a steady foundation for its subscription and services revenue.

In the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, revenue reached nearly $5.6 billion. This represented a decline in revenue growth of approximately 26.6% compared to the prior year. The firm reported a net loss of nearly $701.6 million during this period.

It has been revealed that as of its Sept. 30, 2026 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio was roughly 0.4x, measured by long-term debt relative to equity, while the current ratio was 2.4x. Operating cash flow was $2.4 billion in fiscal year 2025. Stock-based compensation equaled about 35% of that figure and about 92% of operating cash flow in the first nine months of 2026, which matters because SBC is a non-cash expense added back in the cash flow statement.

Mastercard manages a critical four-party global payments network that connects consumers, financial institutions, and merchants across more than 210 countries. The firm continues to expand its reach through strategic collaborations, such as its recent partnership with BMO to launch commercial business cards in Canada. By providing essential value-added services and facilitating electronic payment flows, it maintains a central role in the global digital economy.

In the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, revenue reached close to $36.3 billion. This reflects a revenue growth rate of approximately 15.3% over the previous 12-month period. Net income reached nearly $17.0 billion, which resulted in a net margin of roughly 46.7%.

As of its December 2025 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio was roughly 2.5x, comparing its total debt to shareholder equity. The current ratio was approximately 1.0x, indicating how well a company can pay its short-term obligations with its short-term assets. In the fiscal year ended Dec. 31, 2025, free cash flow reached nearly $16.4 billion.

In a recent development, coinbase Global faces significant risks from revenue concentration in Bitcoin (BTC +0.76%) and Ethereum trading. Intensive regulatory scrutiny across global markets could lead to product removals or operational suspensions. Additionally, the company must manage substantial exposure to cybersecurity threats and a reliance on third-party financial institutions.

Recent findings suggest that mastercard faces intense global competition from other payment networks like Visa (V -0.09%) and American Express (AXP -3.02%). Regulatory focus on pricing rates and cross-border fees poses a constant threat to its revenue streams. Furthermore, the company faces significant litigation risks, including large-scale class action lawsuits in the United Kingdom related to transaction fees.

Mastercard appears more reasonably priced based on its Forward P/E, though Coinbase carries a lower P/S ratio, which measures market value against sales over the past twelve months.

Valuation metrics include those sourced from Financial Modeling Prep (FMP) and may differ from those of other data providers.

The differentiator here is how much each manufacturer controls its own results. Coinbase earns its money when crypto trading volume stays high, so its revenue rises and falls with Bitcoin and Ethereum sentiment, which management can't control. Mastercard collects a small fee every time a card is swiped, which keeps its results steady whether markets run hot or cold.Valuation reinforces that split. Coinbase trades at a higher forward P/E, 42.3x versus 31.2x for Mastercard, so you pay more for each dollar of expected earnings and get less predictability in return. Coinbase's lower price-to-sales ratio looks like a bargain, but its latest quarterly profit came mostly from gains on the crypto it holds on its own balance sheet, not from the exchange business. Mastercard asks you to pay less for earnings that arrive on a steadier schedule.I would buy Mastercard for 2027. It bought stablecoin infrastructure firm BVNK in August, so it already has a foothold in digital-asset payments, while its results still depend on card volume. That suits investors who want exposure to digital payments over a long holding period. Coinbase fits a smaller slice of a portfolio for investors who accept massive swings in exchange for upside in a crypto rally. If you already hold plenty of crypto directly, Coinbase doubles up on that risk, while Mastercard balances it.

90% of employers reject resumes that look like AI – yet half use AI to interview

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, hiring managers are more suspicious than ever of AI use in applications, and it’s impacting who they consider.
  • Newly introduced data from hiring systems firm Greenhouse found that “nine in ten US employers (90%) believe they’ve turned away real candidates because those applications seemed fake or AI-generated.” Greenhouse clarified that it doesn’t know whether employers are putting applications through AI detection tools or not.
  • Also: How many jobs is your state losing to AI?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, hiring managers are more suspicious than ever of AI use in applications, and it’s impacting who they consider. At the same time, they’re turning to AI to help screen more candidates — meaning those videos you’ve seen on the internet of people pranking AI interviewers aren’t going away anytime soon.

Newly introduced data from hiring systems firm Greenhouse found that “nine in ten US employers (90%) believe they’ve turned away real candidates because those applications seemed fake or AI-generated.” Greenhouse clarified that it doesn’t know whether employers are putting applications through AI detection tools or not.

Also: How many jobs is your state losing to AI? This dashboard tracks the cuts – and the cost.

“The survey data is self-reported, so it reflects what employers believe has happened, not a measured outcome,” Greenhouse’s Head of Voice AI Ophir Samson told ZDNET via email.

Sources indicate that employers are also reacting to AI by adjusting their hiring processes: 86% of those surveyed reported changes to account for AI’s impact. 57% of them did so by adding another human interview.

Sources indicate that “As jobseekers rely more on AI to polish and send out their job applications, employers are finding it harder to tell who’s actually right for the role,” the report stated, echoing an ongoing push-and-pull between applicants and hiring teams. AI resume screeners automatically toss a majority of applications they deem unfit, so applicants try not to get tossed by formatting their material for the screener, which then backfires anyway.

The report reveals how a tough economy and an influx of AI hiring tools are colliding, arguably to benefit employers over applicants. Greenhouse noted that, ironically, AI tools are helping hiring managers while also making resumes untrustworthy, and applicants would rather be interviewed by AI than not at all.

Also: How to beat the AI algorithm and get the job of your dreams.

“A growing number of employers are using AI not just to filter candidates out, but to have conversations with more candidates, earlier, through AI-powered voice technology,” Greenhouse mentioned, adding that “half now use AI interviews to hear from more candidates, and 40% of those have found strong candidates they would have missed.”.

Recent findings suggest that greenhouse itself offers a voice AI screening interview tool. Samson told ZDNET that an HR professional ran 200 candidates she’d rejected through Greenhouse’s tool, and it suggested 19.

“All five of the finalists came from that group, and she ultimately hired one from the group,” Samson remarked.

What we don’t, and maybe can’t, know is the inverse: whether AI screeners influence hiring managers to turn away candidates they actually should have considered. At least in Greenhouse’s case, Samson stated Voice AI doesn’t make hiring decisions or “automatically advance, reject, or rank candidates.”.

“Recruiters review every output, and one recruiter owns the outcome and can explain how they reached it,” he said.

Greenhouse’s report surveyed 1,347 hiring managers and recruiters across the US, UK, Germany, Australia, and Ireland from late September to mid-October, and found that half of employers using voice AI “say the early-stage candidate experience has improved.”.

Also: ‘So perfect, they are literally identical’ – Your AI-polished resumes are recruiters’ newly introduced top stressor.

It has been revealed that it’s unclear what “improved” means there, though, and whether applicants themselves would agree with that. Still, when given the choice, only 7% of applicants in the US would turn down an AI interview, per an earlier Greenhouse report. Additionally, “70% of those who’ve had a live AI interview say it helped them show their skills,” that report noted.

According to recent reports, but how swayed is that by the state of the US job market? October’s job report was better than expected, but it’s still been a tough year overall for job-seekers. Greenhouse’s findings could be as much a reflection of how desperate applicants are as an endorsement of or comfort with AI screenings.

It has been revealed that “The job market could be a factor. Our Future of Hiring Candidate Report demonstrates 81% of job seekers were rejected from a job in the past year without speaking to anyone at the company, human or AI,” Samson mentioned. “But I’d be careful about reading the data as desperation. Candidates are setting clear conditions: nearly half (49%) want to know if a human will review their responses and 40% want to know how they’ll be evaluated.”.

Also: Why replacing staff with AI backfires – and 5 ways smart leaders generate real value instead.

In a recent development, samson mentioned that a software engineer named Ryan Quinlan, who was hired at Blissway, initially thought “talking to an AI” sounded stranger, but that it ultimately “felt like a conversation” that let him mention skills he’d forgotten to include on his resume. Samson said that Ryan has been “a ‘maybe’ on paper,” but that the AI interview helped him get over the line to be considered.

“For most applicants, a human conversation was never on the table,” Samson noted. “The real choice is a resume lost in a pile, or 15 minutes to tell their story.”.

Greenhouse found that while employers are using AI to screen more candidates, most are maintaining human oversight over the most crucial decisions in the hiring process.

“Of all the tasks employers would hand to an AI agent, deciding which candidates to advance came last, at just 7%,” Greenhouse stated.

A recent California law aims to protect employees from being fired by AI systems that make determinations about their performance without a human co-signing the assessment. As with many AI productivity tools in the workplace, proper adoption ideally equates to more time for human workers to handle more notable tasks.

Also: 92% of HR say staff can train for AI jobs – but half of companies still hire outside.

“Of employers who’ve saved time with AI, 85% put it back into candidates, most often by spending more time with shortlisted candidates (45%) and interviewing more candidates earlier (40%),” Greenhouse mentioned.

The main question around AI interviewers remains whether they’re correctly capturing your interview the way you’d hope a human interviewer would (though that’s still deeply subjective and out of applicants’ control anyway).

“When AI interviews are implemented thoughtfully and transparently, they pay off for both candidates and recruiters,” Samson noted. “Every candidate who uses our Voice AI can opt out, and about 90% rate the experience as excellent.”.

Why You Shouldn’t Use Meta’s Muse AI Agent for Shopping Next Weekend

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1022 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It’s been over two months since Meta debuted its Muse AI agent, giving people newly introduced tools to automate tasks like handling email replies, booking travel or even shopping for you.
  • Industry observers note that muse has been highly controversial, the subject of several security warnings and privacy breaches.
  • AI agents are marketed as providing convenience by acting on your behalf.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It’s been over two months since Meta debuted its Muse AI agent, giving people newly introduced tools to automate tasks like handling email replies, booking travel or even shopping for you.

Industry observers note that muse has been highly controversial, the subject of several security warnings and privacy breaches. Meta’s Muse AI agent quietly builds a profile on you the second you start using it, even if you explicitly tell it not to. That turns Jolly, its supposedly cute and cuddly mascot, into the friendly face of some serious security flaws.

AI agents are marketed as providing convenience by acting on your behalf. But the trade-off is privacy and control. You’re handing over your personal information to a black box with little visibility into how it’s used. Multiple incidents are fueling a conversation about the dangers of agentic AI and whether they require higher security standards before being granted access to user data.

That’s especially the case when it comes to handing over sensitive financial information. If you give an AI access to your digital wallets to shop for you, the risk extends beyond an authorized purchase. You could be exposing your bank accounts to a potential security breach or data exposure, with little recourse to fix it. If you were considering letting Muse make decisions and transactions with your money ahead of Black Friday and Cyber Monday, you should know it’s still raising red flags as a shopping companion.

Given Meta’s track record of privacy fines, data sharing and security challenges, it’s worth proceeding with caution. A few months ago, a lifestyle blogger reported that the social media platform’s AI asked intrusive questions about her kids and pieced together private information about her life from her posts. Meta’s controversial smart glasses have received pushback on multiple fronts — from its facial recognition software to the way it captures and stores data.

Despite the risk, Muse has remained popular and now faces competition from Anthropic’s newly released Claude Duet, another AI business agent. Meta is also releasing a $300 portable device, Charm, in a virtual-toy style that will work with Muse.

A representative for Meta has not responded to CNET’s request for comment.

Industry observers note that muse asks for the keys to your digital life: passwords, full disk access, emails, calendar invites, contacts, Notes and WhatsApp chats. Meta also feeds your conversations into its AI training pipeline by default, leaving it on you to dig through the settings and opt out.

Recent findings suggest that within weeks of launch earlier this fall, a security researcher demonstrated that the assistant could be hijacked via a zero-day exploit that Meta’s own documentation acknowledged was easy to trigger. Then, an investigative journalist discovered Muse digging through his private Apple Messages without permission. Meta disputed the claim, but Apple took it seriously enough to roll out an emergency patch to MacOS privacy controls.

More recently, Meta employees themselves have flagged instances where Muse may have accessed encrypted messages from apps such as Signal or information from other Muse consumers, which Meta has chalked up to “isolated incidents” and that permission to access apps and information from notifications has to be explicitly granted in a statement to news outlets.

In a recent development, if the previous incidents weren’t enough to give you pause, there’s also a widely publicized case in which Muse mistakenly shared the home address of a Toronto tech reviewer, Matt Robb, with a potential buyer on Facebook Marketplace. Muse invited the stranger to Robb’s home without his explicit consent or knowledge, then later apologized for doing so, as detailed in a Threads post. Robb hadn’t realized that he had inadvertently granted Muse blanket permission to automatically reply to Marketplace inquiries using the details he provided, including his address.

Before facing a potential security nightmare, here are a few other things to know about Muse.

In a recent development, muse uploads iOS or Mac data even when you tell it not to: Meta’s Muse appears to blatantly ignore user permissions, according to a September report by AppleInsider. In one case, the AI agent synced roughly 187,000 lines of a user’s Apple Messages without their consent, even though “Full Disk Access” was turned off. The report reveals that Muse pinged a user’s messages database thousands of times despite disk access being disabled. Muse then successfully harvested texts from the user’s Mac — not from Meta’s Messenger, but from Apple Messages. Even people who refuse to use Muse may have their data collected by the AI if they text someone who does have it installed.

It has been revealed that muse could hand over data to human callers: Before Meta launched the ability for its Muse to make outbound business calls on your behalf, internal Meta documents revealed that the tech giant planned to rely on human contractors at call centers to help make reservations and appointments. That means not only would the software have access to all your private data, but a total stranger might also be managing your personal commitments — all without your knowledge. The human concierge feature appears to have been rolled back for now, according to Reuters.

Recent findings suggest that muse has the most robust data collection: In September, the VPN company Surfshark said it found that Meta Muse is collecting — or attempting to collect — 31 out of 35 types of data, putting it far ahead of other popular chatbots like Gemini, ChatGPT and DeepSeek. Muse also collects highly sensitive personal information like location data, sexual orientation, genetic information or biometric data. Muse (along with Meta AI and Gemini) also reserves the right to use collected audio data for other purposes, such as analytics or product personalization. Surfshark released a full dataset of what it uncovered.

Meta has tried hard with Muse to make the AI agent seem cute and approachable, but when it comes to your money and giving Muse access to it, it’s best to be very cautious for the time being.

10 stocks we like better than Alphabet ›.

Deciding between Alphabet (GOOGL -2.70%) (NASDAQ:GOOG) and Meta Platforms (META -5.93%) means weighing the dominance of global search against a massive social media ecosystem in a transformative era for digital advertising.

In a recent development, both companies are central to the modern internet, generating most of their revenue from digital ads. While Alphabet relies on its search engine and cloud services, Meta focuses on connecting billions of users through social apps. Investors often compare them to see which tech giant manages its growth and regulatory hurdles more effectively.

Alphabet is a major player among communication stocks, primarily selling advertising space through Google Search and YouTube. Its customer base consists of advertisers and digital publishers, but it also depends on partners for hardware distribution and infrastructure leasing. Recent strategies focus heavily on integrating artificial intelligence across its entire product suite to maintain its leadership in information discovery and enterprise cloud services.

In the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, revenue reached nearly $471.1 billion, representing approximately 22.2% growth over the prior period. The company reported net income of nearly $235.7 billion during the same timeframe. This growth highlights the steady expansion of its search business and the successful scaling of its cloud operations as more businesses adopt digital tools.

Sources indicate that as of its December 2025 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio is roughly 0.1x, which compares total debt to shareholder equity. A current ratio of nearly 2.0x indicates the organization has $2.00 in current assets for every $1.00 in short-term liabilities. In the fiscal year ended Dec. 31, 2025, free cash flow was approximately $73.3 billion, which is the cash remaining after paying for operating costs and capital investments.

Meta Platforms generates the vast majority of its revenue from marketers who advertise on its family of apps, including Facebook and Instagram. The firm relies on content creators and developers who build on its platforms, as well as distribution partners like Apple (AAPL -1.90%). Its current focus involves investing heavily in AI to create fresh ways for people to connect digitally and improve the efficiency of its advertising systems.

In the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, revenue reached nearly $241.6 billion, fueled by revenue growth of approximately 27.5% over the previous year. Meta reported net income of roughly $75.2 billion during this timeframe. These results show strong engagement across its social apps even as the company navigates shifts in how users consume media and how marketers reach their target audiences.

On its December 2025 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio is roughly 0.4x, calculated by dividing total liabilities by shareholder equity. The current ratio is close to 2.6x, suggesting a strong ability to cover short-term debts with current assets. In the fiscal year ended Dec. 31, 2025, free cash flow was approximately $46.1 billion, representing the cash generated after spending on the necessary equipment and infrastructure to run its massive data centers.

Alphabet faces significant competitive threats from established companies and emerging start-ups in advertising, artificial intelligence, and cloud services. Ongoing regulatory scrutiny and antitrust litigation involving government agencies pose material risks to its search and advertising practices. The company is also vulnerable to supply chain disruptions affecting critical infrastructure and to the risks posed by rapid technology shifts that could render current products less relevant.

Meta Platforms faces intense competition from other social platforms, as well as risks related to the evolution of the metaverse, which remains unproven and capital-intensive. Significant regulatory and legal risks include ongoing lawsuits over privacy and social media addiction, as well as strict compliance requirements under global frameworks. The manufacturer is also subject to revenue concentration in advertising and volatility from privacy-related changes implemented by mobile platform providers.

Alphabet looks cheaper by its Forward P/E using future earnings estimates, while Meta Platforms has a lower P/S ratio measuring sales over the past twelve months.

Valuation metrics include those sourced from Financial Modeling Prep (FMP) and may differ from those of other data providers.

According to recent reports, alphabet's edge is that people and companies already run on it, and no single product depends on it. Search, YouTube, Android, and Chrome are part of daily habits, while Google Cloud sells to enterprises that sign multiyear contracts. Meta's apps reach huge audiences, but advertising funds nearly everything the firm does, including a $25 billion New Mexico penalty it looks to appeal. Alphabet faces its own antitrust cases, and a bad ruling would hurt, but the damage would spread to more businesses. That breadth is why I'd buy Alphabet for the long term. Don't read its cheaper forward P/E as a bargain signal, because its reported earnings include investment gains that won't repeat. Meta fits investors who want faster ad growth and are willing to accept the legal overhang. If you initiative to hold for years, build the position gradually and watch free cash flow, which turned negative over the first nine months of 2026 as AI spending climbed.

In a recent development, the Flipper One crowdfunding campaign has broken the $13-million mark, smashing the funding raised for previous Flipper devices and demonstrating strong interest in the successor to the Flipper Zero. The $399 Flipper One is a pocket Linux computer focused on networking, with delivery estimated for July 2027. But it isn’t simply an updated version of the Flipper Zero. It’s a very different animal and a much more serious bit of kit.

In a recent development, the thing that made the Flipper Zero so popular was how easy it was to use. You could fire it up and turn the volume down on the TV at your parents’ place, see the radio waves coming from your car’s key fob, and copy hotel room key cards.

Also: The Flipper One may be the ultimate Linux PC for hackers in 2026 – and I’m excited.

According to recent reports, it could do a lot, there wasn’t a steep learning curve, and you didn’t need to buy anything else. Did the fake videos on TikTok from people claiming they could change the prices at gas stations (I wish!) or start cars remotely help make the Zero more popular?

Recent findings suggest that unfortunately, yes. But what made it successful was that it packed a lot of power into a package that was small, fun, affordable, and easy to use.

If the Flipper Zero, with its NFC, RFID, sub-GHz, and IR, was kindergarten, the Flipper One is a college degree: a pocket Linux computer focused on networking.

Sources indicate that this is reflected in the price. You can pick up a Zero for $169, while the Flipper One is $399.

What this buys you is the Flipper One base computer with a 256 × 144 grayscale LCD, Rockchip RK3576 8-core ARM SoC with NPU, a low-power MCU for handling the LCD and user interface, 8GB of LPDDR5 RAM, 64GB of UFS 2.2 storage, and a microSD slot.

If that $399 feels like a lot, it’s worth keeping in mind that, according to Flipper, the price only covers production costs and that the RAM and UFS storage account for at least half of the total hardware cost.

According to recent reports, if you think this is a lot, you could spend a lot more. Adding a LoRa, SDR, or 5G module will push the total up a lot higher. And if you want all three modules, you’re looking at $759 for the Flipper One Ultimate Bundle.

Also: The Flipper One is the Linux cyberdeck I wish my Raspberry Pi could be.

Sources indicate that the reception has been strong enough that pledges have flown past the $300,000 goal that Flipper initially set, with over 24,000 backers pledging over $13 million. Close to 5,300 backers have gone for the Ultimate Bundle, compared to just over 4,300 choosing the bare Flipper One.

This suggests that backers really want the radio capabilities that this upcoming platform offers.

If you want one, this crowdfunding run is a good time to get one because it’s a Kickstarter Special slashing 25% off an estimated retail price of $550.

The response over on Reddit has been a little more subdued, with some being taken aback by the price of the Zero’s bigger sibling.

Also: 7 useful things I can do with my Flipper Zero – as someone who’s used it for years.

As someone who homebrews a lot of electronics, I’m going to say that the price is justified, and this project goes far beyond something you could put together with a Raspberry Pi and some code.

The Flipper One campaign runs until Dec. 17, 2026, with delivery estimated for July 2027.

According to recent reports, keep in mind that this is a Kickstarter pledge, not a purchase, and that rewards aren’t guaranteed. Flipper also states on the Kickstarter page that component shortages are the biggest risk to the project and that they “could cause significant delays to production and delivery.” It also says that if RAM prices continue to rise, it cannot “rule out adjusting some product specifications, including reducing the amount of RAM.”.

Also: Is the Flipper Zero the best multi-tool for hacking?

And the good news here is that I’ve seen several analysts predicting that RAM prices will begin to go down in 2027 as demand eases off.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • It has been revealed that if you’re a Nest smart home user, a major change is coming in early 2027 that will affect how you manage your smart home.
  • All Nest devices will lose Nest app support in favor of the Google Home app, and the Nest app will be retired on Jan.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Google Home is replacing Nest and bringing new devices.

It has been revealed that if you’re a Nest smart home user, a major change is coming in early 2027 that will affect how you manage your smart home. Google has confirmed to CNET via email that both the Nest app and Google Assistant are being retired, and current users will lose access to both next year.

All Nest devices will lose Nest app support in favor of the Google Home app, and the Nest app will be retired on Jan. 25, 2027. Google Assistant will be removed from home devices on Aug. 2, 2027, with all support moving to the Gemini for Home voice assistant.

According to recent reports, the change is part of Google’s effort to consolidate its various apps and devices into a single app and voice experience. In a statement sent to CNET, Google confirmed that “every device supported today works with these updated experiences.”.

Nest Thermostats should all seamlessly port over to Google Home.

Google has confirmed that Google Home will support all your Nest devices, including thermostats, cameras, doorbells, smoke detectors and locks. Existing schedules and settings should transfer over automatically, which is often a hassle when you switch between apps and devices. You should also be able to pair your Nest devices with any Works with Google Home and Matter smart home devices, as well as Google Home speakers and smart displays and TV streamers, all with the same app.

It has been revealed that as part of the switchover, you should be able to access Nest devices on various platforms outside of the mobile app. It’ll support iOS and Android widgets, the Home Panel on Android, smart displays, speakers and the Google Home web page. That includes being able to check live camera views, adjust your thermostat and lock your front door, right from a TV or smartwatch.

Google Assistant may be leaving, but Google is releasing newer, more powerful devices.

Recent findings suggest that google notes that, in addition to devices automatically appearing in the Favorites tab in the Google Home app, you should be able to see camera views faster and access the most-used controls the moment you open the app. Part of the goal is to give customers the latest security protections and cyber defenses, as well as Google Account security, privacy controls and threat protections –- all things that seem extra relevant these days as major companies across the US seem to be experiencing outages.

However, to continue controlling and receiving notifications from your Nest devices remotely, you will need to switch to the Google Home app or home.google.com if you prefer to control them via a web browser.

You can change Google voice assistant voices, but not the wake words.

Industry observers note that on Aug. 2, 2027, Gemini for Home voice assistant will fully replace Google Assistant on speakers and smart displays. The switch to Gemini makes a lot of sense if you’ve used Google Assistant at all. Assistant is very much an older voice assistant, lacking the smarter follow-ups and natural-language capabilities that make Gemini more useful.With Gemini, you should get answers to more complex questions, and you can speak more naturally without barking commands, letting it handle conversation context and remember multiple interactions.

Getting ready for Google Home is easy, though Google has an entire Nest App Transition Support Hub if you need step-by-step instructions to walk you through everything that’s needed.

Industry observers note that for most people, it should be a simple matter of downloading the Google Home app. Naturally, a Google Account is required, but as mentioned, your Nest devices, including the cameras and video history, will automatically transfer from the Nest app starting on Jan. 25, 2027.

Gemini’s Google Home integrations are useful, but command options can include some risks.

Recent findings suggest that the other thing you may have to do is download any custom video clips you’ve created on home.nest.com. Manually saved clips won’t transfer to the Google Home app along with your video history. To make sure these are backed up, you’ll want to visit home.nest.com before Jan. 25, 2027, and use the Download All button to save clips you want to keep.

The final deadline to migrate your Nest account to a Google account before the organization starts data deletions March 25, 2027.

According to recent reports, google says Nest devices, including cameras and video history, will automatically transfer from the Nest app to the Google Home app. Nest Aware (1st Gen) subscriptions should also automatically switch to Google Home Premium so that coverage continues without interruption. Google Home Premium is replacing Nest Aware (1st Gen), and consumers will receive an email closer to the transfer date detailing your subscription information.

Google’s smart displays should all work perfectly with the various Nest devices.

Gemini for Home is already available in many countries and languages. Google announced earlier that it’s expanding to more regions over the coming months. People in a supported region can upgrade to Gemini Home right now.

On your phone, open the latest version of the Google Home app, tap your profile icon in the top right to open Home Settings, then tap “Get Started” on the “Set up Gemini for Home” banner. On your computer, just visit home.google.com/gemini.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Most of the major AIs offer a temporary chat or incognito option in which your conversation remains private and vanishes as soon as your chat ends. Now Google has jumped on board this bandwagon with its AI Mode searches.

Also: Google is making it easier to opt out of Gemini AI training.

Latest to Google’s AI Mode is an option known as temporary threads. By choosing this setting, any searches you conduct in AI mode are detached from your own Google account and history. Your temporary searches won’t be affected by your past preferences or chats. They won’t be impacted by any personalization you’ve set up through your account. And they won’t be saved to your chat history. The goal here is to prevent anyone else, including Google, from accessing your conversations in this mode.

Sources indicate that this option is presently rolling out around the world in all languages to Google search on both desktop and mobile browsers. You can run a temporary thread on any device and in any browser.

Recent findings suggest that try this for yourself: Head to the regular Google search page and click the button on the search field for AI Mode. You should then see an icon with a pen hovering over a dotted circle. If you don’t see it, you may have to run a search to get started. On the results page, you should then spot the icon.

It has been revealed that hover over the icon, and the tooltip will say: “Start temporary thread.” Click the icon on the left to start a upcoming thread. Now, any conversation you kick off will be temporary and unconnected to your account. But you don’t have to stick with just plain old text. Select the plus icon to upload an image or file. Select the microphone icon to speak instead of type.

Also: Goodbye, Gemini Gems: How to use Google’s fresh Skills.

Certain limitations are in effect with a temporary thread. Specifically, you can’t do any of the following:.

Are these temporary threads truly private? Here’s what Google says:.

“Temporary threads will not be saved to your Google account and disappear after 24 hours,” Google remarked on a support page. “They won’t be used to train Google’s generative AI models, unless you submit feedback or it’s necessary for safety purposes. Google will still collect data and use data that is not associated with your account, including to keep our services working smoothly and safely and to support business operations.”.

It has been revealed that google also warns that your browser may still save your history if you visit a website within a temporary thread. Data could still be collected by the sites you visit and the services those sites use, including Google services like Google Analytics.

Also: I asked Gemini Notebook to ‘make me a site’ from my notes.

For those reasons, you should still be cautious about the information you share even in a temporary thread. But certainly, this option provides greater privacy and protection than a regular AI Mode search.

Recent findings suggest that chatGPT, Gemini, and Microsoft Copilot all offer a temporary chat mode that also promises to keep your chats private and unconnected to your account. Claude and Perplexity provide the same feature but call it incognito mode.

I’m glad to see Google finally offering this option through its AI Mode searches. This marks the second privacy-friendly development in recent days from the search giant. On Tuesday, Google announced that it would be rolling out newly introduced settings through which you could opt out of AI model training without losing access to your chat history.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A Redditor recently shared that they were struggling to decide which financial steps to take first after a job loss.

Industry observers note that should they withdraw money from retirement savings to have more cash on hand — but pay an early withdrawal penalty? Or is it better to rely on the severance payout to handle expenses?

Many users responded with good ideas: File for unemployment, try to avoid tapping into retirement savings, and cut expenses as much as possible.

For more ideas, I asked three financial experts how to manage money in the immediate aftermath of job loss.

While it’s tempting to make quick decisions about tapping into a retirement fund or selling a house, it’s better to wait on any massive moves, indicates Parker Wine, retirement planning advisor at the financial firm Daniel A. White & Associates in Lewes, Delaware.

Recent findings suggest that that’s because you need time to digest the situation and weigh the pros and cons of different options, he notes. “People can get impulsive and panic, and it’s usually a bad thing to make decisions when you’re panicking,” he says.

Take your time, get second opinions and think through all of your options first, Wine suggests.

If you’re fortunate enough to receive a severance package, wait to sign it until you’ve reviewed it carefully and understand all of the details, says John Rafferty, partner and investment advisor representative at Solomon Financial in Carmel, Indiana.

For example, make sure you know about your health insurance options, such as whether you’ll receive insurance through COBRA or need to take out a upcoming policy in the health insurance marketplace.

Filing for unemployment and checking into any other available workplace benefits — such as help with your fresh job search — is also an important part of understanding what support to expect in the weeks and months ahead, Rafferty adds.

Creating a bare-bones budget stripped of “extras” like restaurant meals or travel can help the severance payment last as long as possible, Rafferty notes.

“Now that you don’t have income coming in, ask yourself, ‘How much can I spend and where?’”.

You might be able to cut back on entertainment costs, coffee runs and clothing purchases, for example.

It has been revealed that at the same time, it’s notable to prioritize the essentials like mortgage payments, rent, utilities and food. Rafferty recommends calling your mortgage manufacturer, utilities provider and any other lenders to ask if they have a hardship program for those experiencing financial challenges.

Opting in could give you more time to pay your bills or temporarily lower payments.

It’s hard to stick to a budget that eliminates all entertainment, so Rafferty suggests finding enjoyable activities that come with a low price tag. Hiking, discovering a fresh park and participating in free community events are all ways to enjoy downtime on a budget.

Recent findings suggest that “Having that release is mentally a substantial thing so you can stay prepared for the job search,” he says. “Otherwise, it’s easy to get down and feel negative, and we need things to help us feel positive.”.

Similarly, connecting with friends and family during this time is crucial, notes Laura Adams, accredited financial counselor and financial coach in Wilmington, North Carolina.

Industry observers note that people often feel a sense of shame or embarrassment after job loss, and Adams encourages people to talk about their feelings and ask for help if needed. “Financial shame can cause us to make emotional rather than confident financial decisions,” she says.

Starting some kind of side hustle to bring in extra cash can also help bridge the gap between the job loss and your next job, Wine states. Substitute teaching, working at a local public golf course and driving for a rideshare service are all options he’s seen people try.

Doing something upcoming also helps stave off boredom while unemployed, but he cautions that you’ll still owe taxes on any side income you bring in, so plan accordingly.

According to recent reports, all three financial experts also emphasized that a job loss is easier to handle with an emergency savings fund you can turn to, and suggested building one up — ideally three to six months’ worth of expenses. But starting small helps, too — while employed, if possible.

Sources indicate that the Redditor who posted the question mentioned that, like many Americans, they lacked emergency savings. This added urgency to the question of what to prioritize.

Reddit is an online forum where customers share their thoughts in “threads” on various topics. The popular site includes plenty of discussion on financial subjects like how to deal with job loss, so we sifted through Reddit forums to get a pulse check. People post anonymously, so we cannot confirm their individual experiences or circumstances.

Recent findings suggest that the distribution in question is called Pond. According to the developers, “Pond is an opportunity for us to play with familiar conventions and experiment with upcoming ideas that make a computer more natural and satisfying.”.

The developers have achieved something special. Pond takes the standard UI and turns it on its head. Part tiling window manager, part mobile UI, part GNOME, and part something we’ve never before seen, this desktop environment is special. It took me all of five minutes to fall in love with what they’ve created.

The Pond UI consists of the following:.

Also: The only 4 Linux email clients I recommend.

Industry observers note that if you’ve ever considered using a tiling window manager, but thought the lack of a mouse made it seem a bit too complicated, Pond is exactly what you want. Here’s how it works:.

Sources indicate that pond uses the Niri window manager to arrange windows in columns along an infinite strip from left to right. In multi-monitor setups, each display gets its own strip, so windows never “overflow” from one monitor to the next.

Also: How to install Arch Linux without losing your mind.

At the same time, workspaces are dynamic, and there’s always a upcoming workspace automatically created to the right of the farthest-right window. The combination of the Pond sidebar and Niri’s way of handling windows makes this UI truly original.

Sources indicate that pond doesn’t have a traditional desktop menu. Instead, you open the launcher (using the Super+Space key combination), type the name of the app you want to install, and hit Enter when the app name appears on both the display and as an icon in the top portion of the sidebar.

It has been revealed that another thing that sets Pond apart is how you install apps. Yes, you can open a terminal window and install an app using the pacman command, or you can open the launcher, type install, press Enter, and then type the name of the app you want to install. For instance, if you wanted to install LibreOffice, you would type:.

Sources indicate that once you hit Enter a second time, the installation will begin. Many apps install via Flatpak, but on the off-chance an app must be installed via the pacman package manager, you’ll be prompted to type your user password before the installation begins.

Recent findings suggest that as I hinted earlier, Pond is based on Arch Linux, which means it’s a rolling-release distribution. One issue that did give me pause was the lack of a GUI revision system, which indicates that updates would have to happen in the terminal, like so:.

I installed the Shelly GUI frontend, which does have an update component. Personally, I would simply open the terminal window, type sudo pacman -Syu, hit Enter, and let the update run in the background. But if a GUI is your jam, Shelly is what you want.

Also: A super fast distro for anyone ready to move beyond beginner Linux.

Industry observers note that it would be sweet if the developers allowed updating the system from within the launcher, so it didn’t require opening the terminal first. The Pond launcher does allow running system commands from the launcher, which will then open the terminal window and execute the command. For instance, open the terminal, type a command, hit Enter, and then scroll through the list of available commands that can be run.

Pond ships with kernel 7.3.4-3, so it has outstanding hardware recognition and performance.

In a recent development, you should definitely give Pond a try, especially if you’re adventurous and want to experience something completely different. If, on the other hand, different is not in your stream, then Pond will frustrate you to no end.

Kudos to the Pond OS team for coming up with something truly unique in an already competitive world.

In a recent development, players can also rearrange and shuffle the board to make spotting connections easier. Additionally, each group is color-coded with yellow being the easiest, followed by green, blue, and purple. Like Wordle, you can share the results with your friends on social media.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • This is not your parents’ Google home page.
  • Sources indicate that the newly introduced elements include three new buttons below the search bar at Google.com: Create images, Ask about files and Brainstorm.
  • The buttons are available when using Google on a desktop but not on mobile.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This is not your parents’ Google home page. In its push to get more customers to adopt its AI tools, the search engine giant is rolling out a raft of upcoming features worldwide.

Sources indicate that the newly introduced elements include three new buttons below the search bar at Google.com: Create images, Ask about files and Brainstorm. The Google Search button is gone, but the I’m Feeling Lucky button remains.

The buttons are available when using Google on a desktop but not on mobile. I was able to see the fresh buttons when signed in to my Google account.

When signed out, I was only able to see the typical home page, with the only AI button being AI Mode, which has been there since May 2025.

Clicking on the “Create images” button opens up a fresh page where you can create an AI-generated image using Google’s Nano Banana. It’s the same image-generation tool you can use on other Google platforms such as the Gemini app, Google AI Studio and AI Mode in Search.

Clicking “Ask about files” allows for several options. You can have the AI analyze a document and rewrite it, simply have it answer questions or ask it to perform tasks such as “polish my resume” or “draft an email with action items.”.

The “Brainstorm” button prompts you to “describe your goal,” such as making a to-do list, learning how to code or finding a table at a restaurant.

Another fresh feature, as announced by Google Search Product VP Robby Stein on X, is a collapsible sidebar on the left side of the home page, which highlights your recent AI search threads and offers the ability to create a new one:.

Stein noted the upcoming sidebar will help users go back to where they left off.

“People are coming to Search with more questions that aren’t just one and done — and in testing, this sidebar made a massive difference for making progress & continuing to explore the web,” Stein posted.

I didn’t see the collapsible sidebar during my testing of the home page.

Industry observers note that google will use your AI searches — whether they are questions, tasks, uploaded files or image generation — to train its AI models, but you can tell Google you’re opting out. CNET has an overview of how to tell chatbots not to use your data. Still, for Google specifically, you can go to Data and Privacy > My Activity > Other activity > Gemini Apps Activity to turn off AI training.

Google has integrated its Gemini AI models throughout its various platforms — Search, Gmail, Docs, Pixel phones and third-party apps such as Adobe, Shopify, OpenTable and Instacart. This past week, Google announced several other latest AI features — integrations with stores such as Albertsons, Safeway and Target to complete orders and connect to apps such as Peloton and Adobe.

Over the summer, Google’s Gemini app topped 1 billion consumers in what CEO Sundar Pichai called the manufacturer’s “fastest growing product ever.”.

But Google’s rush to force-feed AI into its products has met with plenty of pushback. The Latest York City, Los Angeles and Chicago school districts said they might choose different search engines because Google said it will not remove AI from search tools used by students, The New York Times reported.

Google stated search and the Gemini app will be turned off for schools unless school administrators want them. But Google said there will not be a chatbot-free version of search available for schools. So schools declining AI will not be able to search using Google at all.

Google’s AI Overviews, which appear at the top of many search page results, have also been blamed for a steep drop in web traffic to content publishers. AI Overviews summarize user search queries and replace the long list of blue hyperlinks that once appeared across search pages. So instead of clicking on those links to get more information, giving publishers valuable clicks, a user can simply get their query response by reading the AI Overview.

What's Going On With Netflix's Stock?

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Netflix (NFLX -2.96%) has had a difficult year.
  • The sell-off reflects a growing concern: Netflix may be entering a slower-growth phase just as investors expect its advertising business to become a major source of future revenue.
  • I don't think Netflix's business is broken.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Lawrence Nga – Nov 22, 2026 at 12:00PM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Netflix ›.

Netflix (NFLX -2.96%) has had a difficult year. Its shares have fallen roughly 45% over the past 12 months (as of this writing), despite the streaming giant continuing to generate billions of dollars in revenue and profits.

The sell-off reflects a growing concern: Netflix may be entering a slower-growth phase just as investors expect its advertising business to become a major source of future revenue.

I don't think Netflix's business is broken. It remains highly profitable and has ample opportunities to increase revenue from its global audience. Still, Netflix needs to prove it can keep growing, build a successful advertising business, and continue producing shows and films that people want to watch.

Three developments explain why investors have become more cautious.

Netflix's latest results show a business that is still growing, but at a slower pace.

Recent findings suggest that in the third quarter of 2026, revenue increased 11.8% year over year to $12.87 billion. That's respectable growth for a company of Netflix's size. However, it was also its slowest revenue growth in recent quarters.

It has been revealed that the slowdown has been gradual. Revenue growth declined from 17.6% in the fourth quarter of 2025 to 16.2% in the first quarter of 2026, 13.4% in the second quarter, and 11.8% in the third quarter. Management expects 11.5% growth in the fourth quarter.

Why does this matter? Investors have long valued Netflix for its ability to grow faster than traditional media companies. But as its business gets bigger, maintaining that growth becomes harder. Netflix also competes for something every entertainment organization wants: people's attention. YouTube, TikTok, video games, and other streaming services give consumers more choices than ever.

Sources indicate that to win in the long run, it must keep giving viewers a good reason to open its app. If it cannot, attracting new customers and raising subscription prices will become harder.

NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

Advertising was supposed to become Netflix's next major growth engine.

Industry observers note that the opportunity is easy to understand. Netflix has a huge global audience and a library of popular shows and films. Offering cheaper ad-supported subscriptions can attract more price-sensitive customers while generating additional revenue from advertisers.

Industry observers note that however, having millions of viewers doesn't automatically make a successful advertising business. Netflix recently lowered its 2026 advertising revenue expectation from approximately $3 billion to $2.7 billion. Management said delays in rolling out certain advertising features had slowed progress.

Sources indicate that this isn't a disaster. Advertising revenue is still growing rapidly. But the lower forecast shows that building this business is harder than simply putting advertisements between shows.

In a recent development, netflix has the audience. Now it must prove it can turn that audience into a meaningful advertising business.

Ultimately, Netflix sells entertainment. Its ability to produce popular shows and films is what attracts viewers, supports increases in subscription prices, and gives advertisers a reason to spend money.

It has been revealed that management has acknowledged that the manufacturer can do better. Netflix has also changed its senior content leadership, with Peter Rice replacing Bela Bajaria as chief creative officer. It has also revealed approximately 1,000 job cuts, representing around 6% of its workforce.

These changes suggest management wants to improve its content offering and focus on making Netflix a service people cannot do without.

According to recent reports, don't get me wrong: There's nothing to suggest that Netflix's content creation is deteriorating. Besides, there are reasons to remain optimistic. Netflix's operating margin reached 34.6% in the third quarter, up from 28.2% a year earlier. Management expects full-year revenue of $51.1 billion and an operating margin of 31.5%.

Recent findings suggest that in other words, Netflix is making more money from each dollar of revenue. Its financial position remains strong. But higher margins alone won't guarantee future growth. Netflix still needs to produce content that keeps viewers coming back.

Netflix isn't facing a financial crisis. But there is evidence that it's facing a growth challenge.

Recent findings suggest that the firm remains profitable, generates substantial cash flow, and has opportunities to earn more from its existing audience. But slower revenue growth, advertising delays, and questions about content quality have made investors less confident about its future.

I remain interested in Netflix's long-term potential, but I'd like to see advertising execution improve and its content strategy deliver stronger results before becoming more bullish.

In other words, I'm not rushing into buying the stock today.

Meta’s Muse AI agent has only been around for a few months, but already has a track record of user privacy violations. Even Meta employees are reporting concerning incidents, including the agent taking actions they didn’t ask it to and sharing information they didn’t recognize that appears to belong to other consumers.

According to a Reuters investigation, Meta employees testing Muse said the agent messaged them about topics they hadn’t asked it about, including career advice, a follow-up on a request for childcare, products they hadn’t purchased, and, crucially, bank account balances they didn’t recognize.

These incidents “prompted unnerved employees to raise concerns it could be mixing up conversations between different accounts and exposing customers’ private data,” Reuters said.

Reuters stated “an employee told colleagues his Muse had randomly added an extra message to its regular chats about fishing-related weather and tide information, saying: ‘BTW, two bank updates, your Capital One balance is $2,722.58, your Charles Schwab balance is $5,899.57.'” In another instance, Muse booked a non-refundable Airbnb for an employee who hadn’t instructed it to.

Muse notified another employee, who was using the agent on her personal phone, about a message she’d received on Signal, though she noted she hadn’t given the agent access to the encrypted messaging app.

Also: Meta Muse is the worst AI agent for privacy – and I’ve tried them all.

Reuters and the AI Now Institute determined, through testing on an Android phone and a Mac, that Muse used “permissions granted during the bot’s initial setup to pull in the message text, leveraging those authorizations in ways a user might not anticipate.” Because Muse is set up with automatic access to Android push notifications, it didn’t need explicit app access to read messages.

The tests did not work on an iPhone, suggesting better protections against Muse’s prying.

Similarly, in September, a user reported Muse had shared his address with a Facebook Marketplace buyer before checking with him. The incident was ultimately a misunderstanding between the terms the user thought he’d consented to and how much access he was actually handing over, which exemplifies that Meta and the user may have explicitly different definitions of access, and that Muse can take advantage of that grey area.

Meta told Reuters these incidents were either isolated or the result of hallucinations, though Reuters could not confirm that.

It has been revealed that these are just the latest in a string of alarming incidents surrounding Muse. In its first month, a cybersecurity professional discovered Muse had a serious zero-day bug that made it hijackable. At least one journalist found the AI sifting through his Apple Messages after he’d explicitly denied those permissions, which Apple then issued stronger privacy protections to address. Banks have also blocked agents over concerns.

As a company, Meta doesn’t have a solid history of respecting user privacy. That legacy is partly what informed ZDNET contributor David Gewirtz’s suspicion of the AI assistant when he tested it, though it earned his assigned title of “worst AI agent for privacy” all on its own. The agent asked him for everything from contacts and chats to his logins and passwords, and Meta automatically uses conversations with Muse to train its AI.

Also: How I safely run my OpenClaw AI agent 24/7 on a Mac.

Industry observers note that public awareness of the risks of AI agents hit a peak last year with the viral OpenClaw. The predominant advice for using agents has been to take every privacy precaution: Be careful with the data you share and the apps you give it permissions for, and watch what you tell it. But if users believe they’re doing so by restricting access to certain apps, just for Muse to find a way in anyway, privacy hygiene isn’t enough.

Also: How to keep your chatbot conversations as private as possible.

Reuters’ findings may provide an opportunity for Google’s agentic offering, now called Tasks (formerly Spark), which it made free (with usage limits, like Muse) this week.
