  • The humble Hyundai Elantra hasn’t historically been a sexy car, but it remains an crucial one for the brand.
  • It has been revealed that the updated hybrid powertrain pairs a 1.6-liter four-cylinder gasoline engine with a 6-speed dual-clutch automatic gearbox.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that hyundai pulled back the cover on the latest 2027 Elantra sedan and 2028 Elantra Hybrid this week at the LA Auto Show, and, wow, it looks like nothing else in its class. The bold styling may not be for everyone — though, personally, I dig it — but economy car shoppers will certainly be interested in the compact hybrid sedan’s targeted 53 mpg and Gleo, Hyundai’s new AI voice assistant that controls the automaker’s new Android Automotive OS-based dashboard tech.

The humble Hyundai Elantra hasn’t historically been a sexy car, but it remains an crucial one for the brand. It’s the automaker’s second-bestselling vehicle, behind only the Tucson. More importantly, the Elantra is one of the stalwarts of the affordable compact sedan class, a segment that many US automakers have abandoned in favor of more profitable SUVs. At a time when buyers are more sensitive than ever to inflated fuel costs and sticker prices, economy car options like the Elantra and its second-generation hybrid powertrain are worth our attention.

It has been revealed that the updated hybrid powertrain pairs a 1.6-liter four-cylinder gasoline engine with a 6-speed dual-clutch automatic gearbox. Combined output at the front wheels rises to 155 horsepower (up from 139 hp in the current car), thanks to a more powerful 45-kilowatt electric-assist motor (up from 32kW).

Recent findings suggest that an updated regenerative braking system recaptures energy when slowing and now offers an “EV-like one-pedal driving experience” that can bring the car to a complete stop at its maximum setting. Additionally, the hybrid now features a newly introduced Stay mode that lets the climate control and infotainment systems run while parked for up to 30 minutes without firing up the gas engine.

Sharing the stage in LA, the new nonhybrid Elantra arrives with the same 2.0-liter four-cylinder engine and continuously variable transmission as the current generation. At 147 hp with a target of 35 mpg combined, it’s no more powerful than before, but it should also be no less efficient, despite the sedan’s increased size. I’d say the hybrid is the better choice, though it will likely also be the more expensive powertrain option.

Inside, a newly introduced cockpit design moves the now-hoodless digital instrument cluster, a 9.9-inch “Slim Information Display,” away from the driver and toward the windshield on the dashboard. The new placement, similar to what I’ve seen on recent Toyota models, puts vehicle information closer to the driver’s line of sight.

Recent findings suggest that pleos Connect, Hyundai’s new Android Automotive OS-based infotainment suite, lives on a 12.9-inch center display. Despite being based on Android, it still features the automaker’s bespoke navigation and media software, rather than Google Maps. The system is said to be over-the-air updatable and features standard wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto for drivers who’d rather bring their own apps on the road.

The Pleos dashboard OS is matched with Gleo AI (who names these things?!), which is Hyundai’s newly introduced AI voice assistant that lets drivers and passengers talk to the car rather than occupy a hand on the touchscreen. Hyundai claims the system features “contextual language support, multi-command capability and zone-specific recognition,” which basically means the car knows who’s talking to it and which seat they’re in and can assign context to voice prompts based on the situation.

“Affordable doesn’t have to be anonymous,” stated Olabisi Boyle, Hyundai’s senior vice president of product, at the unveiling. I agree: Hyundai’s designers clearly aren’t afraid to push the design envelope, and the new Elantra is anything but bland.

Recent findings suggest that the sedan introduces the automaker’s Art of Steel design language, with chunky flared fenders that feel inspired by the brand’s recent new SUVs. The tall greenhouse looks a bit cartoonish if you catch it at the wrong angle, but it provides increased headroom inside. From certain angles, the sedan’s beefy fenders remind me of an angular Korean take on the Subaru WRX. From other viewpoints, I can see inspiration from Hyundai’s N Vision 74 concept and the hydrogen-fueled Nexo, particularly in the triangular rear windows.

The sedan measures 188.8 inches bumper-to-bumper on a 108.3-inch wheelbase that is 1.2 inches longer than the current model’s. Hyundai states the stretch for this generation improves rear-passenger space, now rated at 39.1 inches of legroom on the second row. The Elantra, according to its designers, now approaches the interior volume of a midsize car, a claim I’d take with a grain of salt had I not watched multiple six-foot-plus attendees slip into the back seat with relative ease.

Hyundai did not announce pricing or detailed specs at the auto show debut, and availability is still vague. However, based on the stated model years, which are usually slightly offset from calendar years, I expect the 2027 Elantra sedan to arrive in early 2027, with the 2028 Elantra Hybrid following in late 2027.

Editors’ note: Antuan Goodwin’s travel costs were covered by Genesis. The judgments and opinions of CNET are our own.

Signal to restrict screenshots over AI agent concerns – again

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, privacy concerns around AI agents have prompted encrypted messaging app Signal to set fresh limits on screenshots.
  • According to recent reports, whittaker noted that Google and Apple’s agentic features, including Gemini Intelligence and Siri AI’s Onscreen Awareness, compromise the privacy missions of third-party developers.
  • Also: My 5 favorite Siri AI ‘onscreen awareness’ tricks – and why.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, privacy concerns around AI agents have prompted encrypted messaging app Signal to set fresh limits on screenshots. The tech giant will prevent screenshotting in its iOS 27 app and “when AI assistants attempt to capture screen data on Android,” Signal President Meredith Whittaker wrote in a blog post Friday.

According to recent reports, whittaker noted that Google and Apple’s agentic features, including Gemini Intelligence and Siri AI’s Onscreen Awareness, compromise the privacy missions of third-party developers. These features observe what’s on a user’s screen as context for completing requests.

Also: My 5 favorite Siri AI ‘onscreen awareness’ tricks – and why.

“Your sensitive data is being captured, stored, and made accessible to whatever local database or remote server an OS-level AI agent is using at that moment,” Whittaker said. “All of this is outside of Signal’s control once the data has been captured, and imperils the privacy of all the participants in a conversation.”.

Signal also blocked screenshots last year in response to Microsoft’s controversial Recall AI feature, which could capture screenshots of Signal chats on devices running Windows 11.

According to recent reports, signal’s move is another reminder of how Massive Tech’s AI strategy trickles downstream. As AI features have moved from services external to the OS (like chatbots from OpenAI or Anthropic) to further inside of it, third-party apps have to adapt to conditions that undermine their hard-won privacy infrastructure.

Also: How I use Meta Muse safely to stretch my AI budget – and what I never let it do.

It has been revealed that just last week, researchers at Google DeepMind used AI agents to formally verify Signal’s code, building on Signal’s own work to essentially prove the app’s encryption works. That’s a high bar for a security guarantee within the app, but it becomes meaningless if an agent can simply grab messages off a screen.

Samsung is reportedly working on its own agent, Galaxy Claw, and Apple is developing a rival for Claude and ChatGPT as well.

Whittaker noted Signal’s screenshot restriction isn’t perfect, saying that AI agents can still access app data through other means, “such as retrieving content already present on a user’s device via the filesystem.” Earlier this week, a Reuters investigation supported by Signal and the AI Now Institute found that Meta’s Muse AI agent was using permissions from its initial setup in unexpected ways to access apps and data that a user had not explicitly connected it to.

Signal remarked its protections don’t presently work on MacOS.

It has been revealed that “It is a serious problem that Signal – and application developers beyond – lack robust tools to prevent AI agents from undermining application-level privacy,” she added. “Even where we are able to detect and block AI data access, Google, Apple, Microsoft, and others do not provide ways for developers to easily restrict such AI data access without making drastic compromises to the core user experience.”.

If you’d still like to take screenshots, you can simply disable the setting, though Signal’s announcement strongly advised against it.

“Doing so will potentially expose your (and your contacts’) Signal content to these AI agents, and break our privacy guarantees,” Whittaker stated.

With Mortgage Rates Rising, Should You Hibernate Until Spring?

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Mortgage rates are back up this week, wiping out modest relief from a monthlong drop that began in mid-October.
  • The average rate on a 30-year fixed-rate mortgage shot up 29 basis points to 7.28% APR in the week ending Nov.
  • It has been revealed that A mortgage is a big ol’ loan, so when rates go up, those fractions of a percentage point add up fast.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mortgage rates are back up this week, wiping out modest relief from a monthlong drop that began in mid-October.

The average rate on a 30-year fixed-rate mortgage shot up 29 basis points to 7.28% APR in the week ending Nov. 19, according to rates provided to NerdWallet by Zillow. (A basis point is one one-hundredth of a percentage point.) We calculate our weekly average using daily APRs recorded over the past five business days.

It has been revealed that A mortgage is a big ol’ loan, so when rates go up, those fractions of a percentage point add up fast. Say you’re borrowing $400,000 on a 30-year fixed-rate mortgage. Compared with last week, your monthly principal and interest payment would be about $78 higher today.

Recent findings suggest that one bad week doesn't make a trend, but a jump like this can make putting your house hunt on hold until spring feel like a safer bet. So … is it?

Before deciding whether to buy a house now or wait, it helps to know what's pushing mortgage rates higher.

It has been revealed that right now, mortgage rates are still feeling the aftershocks from two major inflation reports last week. First, the Consumer Price Index (CPI) showed consumer prices rose more than expected in October. Then, the Producer Price Index (PPI) showed wholesale inflation climbed 6.5% over the past year — its biggest annual increase in nearly four years.

It has been revealed that while CPI shows how prices have changed, PPI can offer clues about what's coming next. Faced with higher costs, businesses may raise their own prices to compensate, keeping inflation elevated. Federal Reserve policymakers aren't expecting much relief anytime soon, either. According to meeting minutes released Nov. 18, they expect inflation to remain elevated above their 2% target for a while.

In a recent development, to cool rising prices, the Fed can raise the federal funds rate, which is the benchmark interest rate banks charge each other for overnight loans. The Fed doesn't set mortgage rates, but lenders anticipate its decisions, so mortgage rates often move before the Fed acts. A rate hike is widely expected at the Fed's Dec. 8-9 meeting.

Even after a Fed rate hike, there’s no telling how promptly inflation will cool — or whether mortgage rates will follow. (Inflation is just one of many forces that affect mortgage rates, after all.) So if you do wait until spring to buy a house, don't do it just because you're betting on a cheaper mortgage.

If you're not in a rush to move, winter can be a good time to regroup. Fewer homes typically go up for sale from November through February, so waiting until spring could give you more options.

But new data from the National Association of Realtors suggests this year's slowdown goes beyond the usual seasonal lull. High mortgage rates and home prices are making it tough for many buyers to make the numbers work. For some buyers, waiting isn't a strategy — it's the only option.

It has been revealed that pending home sales, a measure of homes under contract, fell 16.7% in October compared with a year earlier, NAR reports. All four U.S. regions saw declines. At this rate, NAR chief economist Lawrence Yun warned that annual home sales could fall to their lowest level since the mid-1990s.

“Either sizable housing demand is building in the background, or the dream of homeownership is increasingly out of reach for many Americans,” Yun said in a news release.

In a recent development, whether you're waiting by choice or necessity, you can use the time to strengthen your finances. Paying down debt, strengthening your credit score or saving for a bigger down payment could help you qualify for a better mortgage deal.

Every little bit helps when today’s mortgage rates are this high.

Mortgage preapprovals typically expire after 60 to 90 days. If you're already preapproved, why not keep an eye on listings this winter? (Hey, I’m an optimist. All it takes is one house.).

According to recent reports, think like a seller for a second. If you're listing your house in the dead of winter, you're probably not doing it just for fun. You might have a deadline, and you’re probably more willing to negotiate. In the winter, buyers have less competition — and more room to negotiate a lower price, closing cost credits or repairs. Those savings on the sticker price might help offset today's higher borrowing costs.

Industry observers note that spring typically brings more homes for sale, but it also brings more buyers competing for them. And if mortgage rates end up dropping this spring, you won't be the only one coming out of hibernation.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By David Dierking – Nov 22, 2026 at 12:26PM EST.

10 stocks we like better than S&P 500 Index ›.

It has been revealed that volatility in the S&P 500 (^GSPC -3.70%) has picked up since the midterm elections. That week was the index's worst since April 2025, and it now sits roughly 10% below its all-time high.

According to recent reports, that kind of volatility doesn't usually happen when the S&P 500 is near its all-time highs. It's often considered a sign that the conditions that lifted stock prices to records may no longer be in place. And investors are dealing with some real concerns about where the market heads from here.

While bounces like the one that took place the week ending Nov. 13 might feel like relief, history reveals that might not be the case.

I went back and looked at S&P 500 history since 1970. Specifically, I looked for periods of market swings that look just like the one we experienced. Over history, there were 19 instances in which the index fell by at least 2.5% one week and rebounded by more than 2.5% the next week, while still within reach of an all-time high.

The good news is that recent history has shown solid gains for the S&P 500 following these periods. Since 2018, all six occurrences produced positive returns six months later, with a median return of more than 11%.

Industry observers note that the bad news is that prior to that, the results are incredibly mixed. There are more instances of negative forward returns, and the gains six months later were often minimal. Plus, some of these examples came during some of history's worst bear markets.

It has been revealed that data source: Investing.com and author's analysis of S&P 500 daily closing prices, 1970 to Nov. 13, 2026. A case is a weekly drop of at least 2.5% followed immediately by a weekly gain of at least 2.5%, with the index finishing within 5% of its record close. Six months = 26 weeks; 12 months = 52 weeks.

Sources indicate that the one thing history has shown us is that the market's biggest moves, both up and down, tend to cluster. You'll find several of these days bunched up around the tech bubble, the financial crisis, and the COVID-19 pandemic.

That's why the bounces aren’t necessarily relief. They can be part of a high-volatility environment in which investors are trying to determine how assets should be priced. It's not a rally built on financial strength or confidence. It's typically built on uncertainty. And that's why volatile periods like this can be potential signs of longer-term trouble.

According to recent reports, but as the data shows, it may be just fine. There are several examples in this data set of the S&P 500 generating double-digit gains in the months following. That's why it's usually not advisable to trade in these kinds of markets. There's really no way of knowing if you'll be right or wrong. And that feels more like gambling than anything.

According to recent reports, honestly, I wouldn't make any radical changes to my asset allocation, such as selling stocks and moving to cash. I'd keep funneling money to my investment accounts regularly.

The reason I'd hold tight is that most of what happens in the short term is noise. Even over seemingly longer periods of six to 12 months, the S&P 500 could easily move in either direction. I won't need my money for 15 years, so I'm more than happy to ride it out and leave the guesswork to others.

According to recent reports, and it's notable to remember that volatile periods like this are normal when investing in stocks. It should be expected, and you should be prepared to ride it out, assuming you don't need the money for a decade or more as well. Keep a disciplined approach and focus more on your long-term goals.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that korean luxury automaker Genesis rolled out its first hybrid models this week, debuting latest powertrains for the G80 sedan and GV80 SUV at the 2026 LA Auto Show.
  • The hybridized versions of the brand’s most popular sedan and SUV arrive as American drivers show growing interest in energy-efficient cars, both battery electrics and hybrids, driven by high fuel costs and better understanding of the technologies.
  • The G80 Hybrid and GV80 Hybrid share a 2.5-liter turbocharged hybrid powertrain.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that korean luxury automaker Genesis rolled out its first hybrid models this week, debuting latest powertrains for the G80 sedan and GV80 SUV at the 2026 LA Auto Show. The organization indicates the electrified system is both more efficient and more powerful than the current nonhybrid versions. For buyers who want a more battery-focused experience, Genesis teased an upcoming 640-mile extended-range electric vehicle due to arrive in early 2027.

The hybridized versions of the brand’s most popular sedan and SUV arrive as American drivers show growing interest in energy-efficient cars, both battery electrics and hybrids, driven by high fuel costs and better understanding of the technologies. Hybrids, in particular, have attracted attention because they behave like traditional combustion cars: There’s no need to install home charging hardware or change familiar driving and refueling habits. Just get in and reap better fuel economy with every mile.

The G80 Hybrid and GV80 Hybrid share a 2.5-liter turbocharged hybrid powertrain. Genesis says the system is 16% more powerful than the gasoline-only version, outputting 347 horsepower and 391 pound-feet of torque. A new liquid-cooled battery pack improves thermal management and allows higher maximum discharge than Hyundai Motor Group’s previous air-cooled hybrid batteries, boosting performance. Both models use a seven-speed automatic transmission adapted to work with the electric motor’s regenerative braking.

According to recent reports, genesis hasn’t unveiled official fuel economy estimates, but indicates the G80 Hybrid is 30% more efficient than the standard model, while the GV80 Hybrid is 24% more efficient. Based on current EPA figures, my math puts them in the ballpark of 30 mpg and 27 mpg, respectively. Any improvement is good, but those aren’t exactly earth-shattering gains. We’ll have to wait for the official ratings to be sure.

According to recent reports, each hybrid can be toggled into a silent EV mode for short distances — good for gliding into a driveway, garage or parking deck without waking the neighbors. However, without a plug, all the energy in the battery ultimately comes from the gas tank.

A upcoming Stay Mode lets owners run the climate control and infotainment without starting the engine for around 30 minutes. I like to think of it as the “moment of zen in the driveway before you have to go inside and face responsibility” mode, or maybe the “eating lunch in your car” mode. It’s similar to Toyota’s My Room Mode on its hybrids.

Aside from the powertrain, the G80 and GV80 Hybrids are largely identical to their combustion counterparts. Hybrid-specific touches include a three-dimensional G-Matrix grille inlay redesigned for these models, as well as latest exterior colors.

Inside, a 27-inch OLED display combining the instrument cluster and navigation stretches halfway across the dashboard. Tech features include Digital Key 2 Premium, which lets owners use their phone instead of a key fob to unlock and start the car, and active road noise cancellation. Genesis’ driver-assistance suite is headlined by the Highway Drive Assist 2 steering assistance system and the Remote Smart Parking Assist 2, which enables automatic parking with the driver inside or just nearby the car.

Sources indicate that prices for the sedan and SUV haven’t been revealed. Final specifications and EPA fuel economy figures are expected closer to the early 2027 launch window.

According to recent reports, my cynical side says that these newly introduced models are just Genesis doing what Toyota has done since the RX 400h debuted in 2004. (To be fair, Genesis didn’t become an independent brand until 2015, so its rival has a bit of a head start.) In practical terms, the move brings Hyundai Motor Group’s luxury brand into parity with other group members and luxury car competitors that have rolled out updated hybrids over the last year, and meets customers’ increasing demand for more energy-efficient cars where they are.

In addition to its first hybrid sedan and SUV, Genesis executives declared that the brand will expand the availability of its wild-styled, high-performance GV60 Magma full-electric SUV to more states and markets to meet higher-than-expected demand.

Sources indicate that at the debut event in LA, the brand also teased an upcoming extended-range EV — an EV with an onboard gasoline generator, essentially a very advanced plug-in hybrid — set to launch in early 2027. The EREV model is targeting over 640 miles before its “all-new high-performance battery” and gas tank both run dry, but Genesis didn’t give further details about the upcoming model.

Editor’s note: Antuan Goodwin’s travel costs were covered by Genesis. The judgments and opinions of CNET are our own.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • It has been revealed that as of Saturday, Nov.
  • Recent findings suggest that if you don't have any visual aids, you can still see the Mares Imbrium and Vaporum, as well as the Kepler Crater.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If you look up at the sky tonight, you'll notice the Moon is looking noticeably fuller than it did earlier in the week. We're still in the Waxing Gibbous phase, which falls between the First Quarter and Full Moon, but we're getting closer to the Full Moon every night.

It has been revealed that as of Saturday, Nov. 21, the NASA's Daily Moon Guide tracker tells us the Moon is in the Waxing Gibbous phase, with 85% of its surface visible.

Recent findings suggest that if you don't have any visual aids, you can still see the Mares Imbrium and Vaporum, as well as the Kepler Crater. With binoculars, you'll also see the Mare Frigoris, the Clavius Crater, and the Mare Nectaris. And if you have a telescope, you'll get to see all this plus the Apollo 15 and 17 landing spots, and the Rima Hyginus.

The next Full Moon will take place on November 24.

According to NASA, the Moon goes through a complete cycle of phases roughly every 29.5 days. As it orbits Earth, the portion of its sunlit surface visible to us changes, giving rise to the different lunar phases. The cycle begins with a New Moon, progresses to a Full Moon, and then gradually returns to a New Moon before starting all over again.

Fresh Moon - The Moon is between Earth and the sun, so the side we see is dark (in other words, it's invisible to the eye).

Waxing Crescent - A small sliver of light appears on the right side (Northern Hemisphere).

It has been revealed that first Quarter - Half of the Moon is lit on the right side. It looks like a half-Moon.

Waxing Gibbous - More than half is lit up, but it's not quite full yet.

Full Moon - The whole face of the Moon is illuminated and fully visible.

Sources indicate that waning Gibbous - The Moon starts losing light on the right side. (Northern Hemisphere).

Third Quarter (or Last Quarter) - Another half-Moon, but now the left side is lit.

Waning Crescent - A thin sliver of light remains on the left side before going dark again.

Andrew Garfield on Becoming Sam Altman in ‘Artificial’: ‘I’m Dying to Understand This Person’

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1235 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It’s a tall order for an actor to embody any living person, but especially someone whom audiences may already have negative feelings about.
  • Sources indicate that rather than daunting, that challenge was “exciting” to actor Andrew Garfield, who plays OpenAI’s polarizing CEO Sam Altman in the film Artificial, slated for an initial Dec.
  • In a recent development, garfield’s perspective on Altman morphed as he worked to better understand him, the actor told me ahead of an early screening hosted by SFFilm in the heart of the city where the story is set.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It’s a tall order for an actor to embody any living person, but especially someone whom audiences may already have negative feelings about.

Sources indicate that rather than daunting, that challenge was “exciting” to actor Andrew Garfield, who plays OpenAI’s polarizing CEO Sam Altman in the film Artificial, slated for an initial Dec. 25 release. The biopic follows the rise of OpenAI, focusing on Altman’s relationships — particularly with his cofounder Ilya Sutskever (Yura Borisov) — as he relentlessly pursues success amid Silicon Valley’s artificial intelligence power struggle.

In a recent development, garfield’s perspective on Altman morphed as he worked to better understand him, the actor told me ahead of an early screening hosted by SFFilm in the heart of the city where the story is set. His mission as an actor is to get to the “central truths” of who a person is, he remarked, “and try to merge my soul with theirs. And like all of us, Sam has so many facets.”.

According to recent reports, that includes physical traits. Garfield says he had to lose weight and change his gait and voice to try to match Altman’s. The semblance is striking. From his bouncy stride to his clipped, gravelly speech, Garfield effortlessly emulates the Altman we’ve seen in interviews and Congressional testimonies. It’s a remarkable transformation — down to the sly, coaxing glint in his eyes — showcasing the breadth of Garfield’s acting talent.

But it goes beyond physicality. Garfield had to dig deep internally to find elements “that felt like they were a match” with Altman, he remarked. The result is an astonishingly believable portrayal of a multidimensional figure, at once pensive and inscrutable.

“There is a responsibility,” Garfield told me. “I take it very, very seriously to play any character, but particularly someone who’s alive, someone who’s pretty much my age. But also, maybe the greater responsibility is making sure that we interrogate these human beings that are leading our world into the next chapter, it seems.”.

“And it feels like our job as storytellers to reflect the times we’re in,” he added, “and no better way of doing that than by looking at the human beings — their personal relationships, their souls, all the diamond facets of their souls — and interrogate the people that have the power over our culture right now.”.

Artificial explores OpenAI’s rise through a rather bleak lens, with questions of moral responsibility and safety looming over the protagonists as they navigate the manufacturer’s success. The film is laced with dark satire, which offers moments of levity amid otherwise weighty meditations on the technology’s long-term impact.

In one scene, when Sutskever is asked about the difference between AI and artificial general intelligence, which can theoretically match or even surpass human ability, he plainly responds, “It’s like how rocket ships are different from scooters.” He goes on to tell his cohorts that this is achievable “in your lifetime — well, maybe not yours or yours or yours,” as he points to the less youthful figures in the room. Moments like these elicited generous laughter from the audience.

It has been revealed that director Luca Guadagnino, known for deeply character-driven stories, such as Challengers and Call Me by Your Name, stated he was following the news about Sam Altman’s temporary ousting from OpenAI in 2023 and was fascinated by the “Shakespearean feud” leading to that moment. Guadagnino applies his signature character-centric approach to OpenAI’s story, relying on slow, measured beats, piercing close-ups and suspenseful music to relay the stakes of each pivotal moment.

According to recent reports, “It’s never about the object; it’s always about the people,” Guadagnino stated during a panel discussion after the screening. “It’s not about AGI or AI. It’s about the conflict between worldview and way of being, embodied by people that clash or fight for the vision they have.”.

He also said, “The point for me was more about trying to understand: How did the possibility of an incredible technology that can help all of us turn into the opportunity to get power in your hands and to become self-entitled?”.

Garfield is no stranger to portraying prominent figures in the tech world, having played Eduardo Saverin, Facebook’s co-founder and former chief financial officer, in 2010’s The Social Network. On the surface, Artificial seems like a spiritual successor, recounting another defining moment in the tech industry. But the films differ in both tone and approach, with Artificial trading rapid-fire drama for a darker, more existential theme that occasionally ventures into more technical territory. What the films do share is a focus on bold, forceful personalities.

“From that experience, I suppose, I was very curious about what it takes to win in this particular late-stage capitalist world that we’re in with these emerging technologies,” Garfield stated during the panel discussion. “What does it take to hold Sauron’s Ring of Power and not be completely burnt up by it? Is it possible to not completely lose yourself to that overwhelming, exponentially growing possibility and power?”.

Industry observers note that comic relief also arrives in the form of Ike Barinholtz playing OpenAI cofounder and tech mogul Elon Musk. By portraying him as a brutish, aloof figure who saunters in and out of rooms on a whim, he effectively underscores the absurdity of perceived importance and status. Almost every on-screen moment generated a murmur of laughter in the audience.

In a recent development, “I think we’re all fascinated by these cultural, iconic figures who are leading us into this next stage of culture and society,” Garfield told the crowd. “They’re kind of kids. They’re kind of slightly stuck in an early developmental place, and that felt like a really crucial part of Luca’s telling of this story.”.

In fact, he added, “[Guadagnino] would say to us, ‘This is a John Hughes movie. This is a high school, screwball comedy, just with slightly higher stakes — mixed in with a little bit of Invasion of the Body Snatchers.’ A very vital part of this is that these are all kind of adolescent, high-school-minded people.”.

Even the way Garfield portrays Altman flippantly perching on couches and sitting cross-legged on tabletops while donning sunglasses — including during serious conversations about the future of OpenAI — was deeply researched.

According to recent reports, “We had amazing consultants and researchers that work with us that gave us lots of information that’s not quite in the public arena about our characters,” Garfield noted. “And Sam is someone who apparently would always sit like he was crisscross applesauce at play school, nursery school [or] kindergarten.”.

In a recent development, ultimately, Artificial poses an open question about where society is headed and whether those at the helm are equipped to lead the charge. Amid weighty explorations of AI’s ramifications, the film paints a haunting, revelatory portrait of the cunning, mercurial figures making decisions that shape our world.

For Garfield, this presented an opportunity to dive deep into a figure like Altman, who, despite his prominence, remains largely elusive in the public eye.

According to recent reports, “I just wanted to tell this story and actually uncover for myself, excavate for myself, who is this person?” Garfield told me. “I’m dying to understand this person, and I get to try to understand this person, maybe more than anyone else has ever really tried to. And it feels like a gift to me.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Dana George – Nov 22, 2026 at 12:30PM EST.

10 stocks we like better than iShares Core S&P 500 ETF ›.

Exchange-traded funds (ETFs) have been around since 1993 and have long been treated as a quick way to diversify. You buy one fund and immediately own a basket of investments.

Sources indicate that while that diversification remains a positive feature of ETFs, today's investors are increasingly asking about more than how many holdings a fund has. They're asking what those holdings are and how much an ETF's holdings overlap with the rest of their portfolio.

It has been revealed that let's say you invest in the iShares Core S&P 500 ETF (IVV -3.52%) for access to hundreds of large U.S. companies. For example, IVV's top holdings included giants such as Apple (AAPL -1.90%), Nvidia (NVDA -14.01%), Microsoft (MSFT -2.77%), Amazon (AMZN -4.10%), and Alphabet (GOOG -2.59%) (GOOGL -2.70%). You can't get much bigger than these companies, and IVV's largest positions give you the sense that you're betting on winners.

NYSEMKT · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

With its low expense ratio, broad market access, transparency, and flexible trading, you can't find anything you don't like about IVV. In fact, you're so happy with the fund that you decide to invest in another ETF. While it's easy to believe that another fund will help you create a more diversified portfolio, that may not be the case.

It has been revealed that for example, what if you added the Vanguard S&P 500 ETF (VOO -3.42%) to your portfolio alongside IVV? You'd add some fresh holdings, but you'd also end up with a lot of overlap. That's because IVV and VOO both track the S&P 500 (^GSPC -3.70%) index and are heavily weighted toward Apple, Nvidia, Microsoft, Amazon, and Alphabet.

NYSEMKT · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

Recent findings suggest that instead of branching out and diversifying, you end up owning more shares of the same companies. The Securities and Exchange Commission advises anyone who holds several ETFs to check the top holdings of the funds to make sure they're different and provide the diversification you seek.

Industry observers note that A truly diversified portfolio spreads risk across investments that don't all respond to market events at the same time or in the same way. One way to achieve that is to include different regions, firm sizes, sectors, and asset types.

Sources indicate that when investing in more than one ETF, look under the hood of each. Find out about underlying holdings, the percentage of each fund invested in the same companies, and how much of your total portfolio those shared holdings represent.

While you're there, compare sectors, countries, and investment styles, since funds that hold different stocks can still be concentrated in similar areas.

Industry observers note that one of the easiest ways to compare funds is to use the ETF Research Center's fund overlap calculator. The calculator shows not only how many holdings overlap, but also the overlap by weight. This is vital information when you're aiming for a truly diversified portfolio.

If you like playing daily word games like Wordle, then Hurdle is a great game to add to your routine.

Sources indicate that there are five rounds to the game. The first round sees you trying to guess the word, with correct, misplaced, and incorrect letters shown in each guess. If you guess the correct answer, it'll take you to the next hurdle, providing the answer to the last hurdle as your first guess. This can give you several clues or none, depending on the words. For the final hurdle, every correct answer from previous hurdles is shown, with correct and misplaced letters clearly shown.

An vital note is that the number of times a letter is highlighted from previous guesses does necessarily indicate the number of times that letter appears in the final hurdle.

This Oceanfront Hilton Resort in Florida Is Great for Groups

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1499 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nerdwallet

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, hilton is making a big play in South Florida with its Signia by Hilton Diplomat Beach Resort.
  • It has been revealed that the resort caters primarily to business and group travelers (it’s attached to a massive events space), but it’s also a strong option for vacationers looking for some R&R.
  • Industry observers note that room rates typically run $300 to $600 a night, depending on the season, but you can also use Hilton Honors benefits to make your stay more affordable.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, hilton is making a big play in South Florida with its Signia by Hilton Diplomat Beach Resort. The massive 1,000-room property — which underwent an $80 million renovation before opening under the Signia Hilton brand in May 2026 — sits on the beach in Hollywood, Florida, just outside of Fort Lauderdale.

It has been revealed that the resort caters primarily to business and group travelers (it’s attached to a massive events space), but it’s also a strong option for vacationers looking for some R&R. The main downside: The location isn’t great if your trip primarily revolves around off-property excursions, dining and nightlife.

Industry observers note that room rates typically run $300 to $600 a night, depending on the season, but you can also use Hilton Honors benefits to make your stay more affordable. There’s also a resort fee of $59 per night — but Hilton waives that when you book using Hilton points.

Hilton covered the cost of my stay for two nights, but the opinions in this review are my own. Here’s what guests can expect at this oceanfront resort.

Since the Signia by Hilton Diplomat Beach Resort is part of Hilton Honors, there are several ways to book a stay there.

If you’re using Hilton points, expect to pay 70,000 to 80,000 points a night when standard rooms are available. Hilton elite status — a benefit you can earn by holding any Hilton Honors credit card — gets you the fifth-night-free perk, where you stay for at least five nights but pay for four when booking with points.

For example, if you were to stay five nights at 80,000 points a night, you’d pay 320,000 points total, bringing down your average nightly rate to 64,000 points.

You can also book using Hilton’s generous free night certificates, which can be used at almost any property in the portfolio. If you hold the Hilton Honors American Express Aspire Card, you automatically get a certificate each year. It’s also possible to earn certificates through reaching spending thresholds on the card and on the Hilton Honors American Express Surpass® Card. Terms apply.

Make sure to check the cash rate against the points rate to make sure you’re getting good value from your redemption. NerdWallet values Hilton points at 0.4 cent apiece.

In a recent development, for cash bookings of two nights or more, you might consider using The Hotel Collection via American Express’ travel portal for eligible cardholders. Eligible bookings come with benefits like a $100 property credit and other amenities subject to availability, including a room upgrade, early check-in and late checkout.

Keep in mind that third-party bookings typically don’t earn Hilton points or count toward elite status qualification.

It’s hard to miss the Signia by Hilton Diplomat Beach Resort, with its signature H-shaped facade and sleek white-and-glass exterior.

Stepping into the hotel, I was immediately struck by the lush greenery filling the entrance and indoor courtyard. The grand lobby has soaring glass ceilings, giving the space a greenhouse feel, although the strong air conditioning keeps you cool.

Industry observers note that despite its massive size, it doesn’t have a sprawling layout, which I appreciated. Everything is close together, and you can walk from the check-in counter to any of the indoor restaurants in under a minute.

I stayed in an oceanfront suite with a balcony, which was spacious and had a fun beachy vibe. To get to the rooms, you’ll need to use either the north or south tower elevator banks.

In the living room, there was a large sitting area featuring a TV, a couch, an accent chair and a four-person high-top table.

Although I didn’t spend too much time on the balcony — the October balminess was a bit too much for me — I enjoyed stepping out each morning to admire the view.

The bedroom had a king bed with extremely comfortable bedding and an oversized chair that was a great spot to relax and read a book by the window.

The bathroom was spacious, featuring a shower and a separate tub (something every room has).

Even the standard room I toured felt roomy. I liked that it shared similar elements with the suite, including the oversized lounge chair.

This is what you’d normally get when booking a room at the cheapest points price.

According to recent reports, there are several dining venues on the property, ranging from a grab-and-go cafe to a high-end steakhouse. It is a luxury resort, so expect the prices to reflect that.

For breakfast, you can head to Palmea Kitchen, which is also open for lunch. I had the breakfast buffet, which offered a nice spread of classics, from hot food items and pastries to cold cuts and smoked salmon.

Industry observers note that if you don’t have time for a sit-down breakfast, you can head next door to The Press, which offers made-to-order and grab-and-go food options throughout the day. You can also get smoothies, juices, snacks, pastries and other sweet treats.

The Canteen is another grab-and-go option that also sells snacks, drinks, souvenirs and sundries, similar to a convenience store.

For lunch and dinner, try Solara. It doesn’t have a traditional restaurant feel, as it’s mostly an indoor-outdoor bar space. One side connects to the lobby, while the other side faces the Solara adults-only pool.

It serves a lunch menu, as well as a substantial bar food menu that’s available late into the night.

Recent findings suggest that you can also eat at Playa Beach Bar & Grill, a beachside restaurant serving Latin-inspired cuisine. I enjoyed spending a lazy lunch there and watching the waves crash onto the shore.

In a recent development, for a fancy sit-down dinner, go to Diplomat Prime, the property’s steakhouse. We had a group dinner at the restaurant, and the meats were, of course, the highlight. But don’t sleep on the seafood, which was also delicious.

Recent findings suggest that one of the best parts of the Dip, as it’s affectionately known, is its location right on the beach. Guests can access the stretch of beach directly adjacent to the property. But it’s not a private beach, so you might encounter crowds.

I didn’t spend any time on the beach itself — it was extremely windy while I was there — but the hotel’s resort fee includes amenities like a beach lounge (umbrella not included), a daily one-hour kayak or paddleboard rental, and beachfront yoga classes.

If you don’t want to get sand everywhere, you can head to one of the three pool options: the adults-only Solara pool, the family-friendly lagoon pool and the Verandah Social Club for those 21 and older (requires paid access).

It has been revealed that the family-friendly lagoon spans the length of the property and runs beneath the Solara pool. It also has its own hot tub.

I spent an afternoon in a cabana at the Verandah Social Club, which has some smaller plunge pools and a hot tub.

I appreciated the attentive service from the staff there, who constantly checked on whether guests needed anything.

If you’re looking for other ways to stay active, head to the two-story fitness center, featuring a variety of equipment like free weights, exercise bikes, a rowing machine and treadmills.

Industry observers note that next door, you’ll find the spa and wellness center. I had a relaxing massage that incorporated hot stones and aromatherapy.

The locker rooms come with a sauna and steam room, although I wished there were more amenities like a hot tub and cold plunge.

It has been revealed that one of the resort fee inclusions is complimentary high-intensity interval training workout classes at the gym across the street. I signed up for an early morning class. The instructor was friendly, and it was a great way to start my day.

Other amenities include a complimentary one-hour e-bike rental each day, as well as a kids’ club with various activities (but drop-off fees apply).

I had a fantastic stay at this resort, but I’d recommend it for a specific traveler.

If you’re planning to stay on-property your entire trip, it’s a great option. That’s probably why it’s such a popular convention hotel, since everything you need is easily accessible.

I loved the hotel’s design, including the jungle-like atmosphere in the lobby, and I found the dining options to be tasty, albeit pricey.

But if your trip revolves around visiting Miami attractions, you’ll likely want to stay closer to the action.

Industry observers note that chelsea cruised to victory over Ruben Amorim’s AC Milan in Jakarta, Indonesia, on Saturday. Goals from Moises Caicedo and a double from João Pedro either side of half-time led Xabi Alonso’s side to their second win on their Far East tour.

The game was fairly even in the first half and looked set to head into the break level at 0-0 but Pedro’s header from Moises Caicedo’s corner put Chelsea in front.

The west London side then doubled their advantage seconds into the second half as Pedro scored his second, assisted by Pedro Neto.

Sources indicate that just minutes later, Chelsea had their third courtesy of a well-worked corner routine. Romeo Lavia’s delivery was met by Caicedo on the volley, with the Ecuadorian’s finish with the outside of the boot finding the bottom corner.

AC Milan take on Amorim’s former club Manchester United next Saturday before they kick off their Serie A campaign at Torino on August 23.

The trophies won by Franco Baresi, who has died at the age of 66, are their own monument to the AC Milan and Italy defender’s greatness. Six times a Serie A champion, five as captain, three European Cup-winning campaigns, 10 other winners’ medals and the distinction of being a member of Italy squads that finished in first, second and third places at World Cup tournaments demonstrate that his career, in a significantly more meritocratic era, stand alongside the giants even if the bias towards attacking virtuosos denied him the Ballon d’Or his talent deserved.

Sources indicate that yet they do not tell us why the grief, so tangible in Milan and beyond today, transcends tribal rivalry. It would be unfair to say that he transformed the art of Italian defending. Gaetano Scirea, the elegant Juventus sweeper who kept the 21-year-old Baresi confined to the bench when Italy won their third World Cup in 1982, had a surplus of natural ability, composure and intelligence. He did not need the raw-elbowed brutality of Claudio Gentile, heir to generations of Italian defenders influenced by the post-war influx of players brought up in the traditions of Argentina and Uruguay.

It has been revealed that chelsea’s pre-season continues out in the Far East as they take on AC Milan in the Gelora Bung Karno Stadium in Jakarta, Indonesia. Both clubs now have fresh managers, with Xabi Alonso taking over at Chelsea and former Manchester United boss Ruben Amorim now at the helm at AC Milan. These sides met in pre-season last year, with Chelsea winning 4-1 at Stamford Bridge. At that time, now-Manchester City boss Enzo Maresca was in charge whilst Max Allegri, who is now at Napoli, was leading AC Milan. The last time they met competitively was during the 2022/23 Champions League season, with Chelsea winning both games.

Chelsea lost 1-0 to AC Milan’s Serie A rivals Juventus on Wednesday in Hong Kong, in which Danny Welbeck made his first Chelsea appearance after joining from Brighton in the last week.

Industry observers note that “We want to have a great team spirit and that is built on a daily basis with a great culture in the building,” Alonso said in his pre-match press conference. “That helps in the moment you have to compete. You feel better having that togetherness, trust, and the bonds between the players are so vital to ultimately building a winning mentality, and a team that can compete anywhere. So the football side is so important, but the mental side is as important. And the strength of the team is the most important. We have been able to train and prepare [during pre-season] and I am very happy with the attitude and personality, we know that it is a very important part of this tour.”.

It has been another busy week on the transfer front for Chelsea; not only has Welbeck arrived over the last week but so too have Jordan Henderson and Valentin Barco. Alonso’s men have two more games after this against Johor Darul Ta’zim and Real Sociedad before getting their Premier League campaign under way with a derby against Fulham at Craven Cottage.

AC Milan finished fifth in Serie A last season to earn a spot in the Europa League last season. Their big-money acquisition this summer as been Portuguese striker Goncalo Ramos from PSG. They have played two pre-season friendlies so far, which have both ended in draws; 2-2 against Celtic and then 1-1 against city rivals Inter. They kick off their Serie A campaign at Torino on August 23.

Secondo quanto riportato da Il Messaggero, Il tecnico ha ricevuto garanzie: nessuno partirà. Sources indicate that la garanzia sulle partenze tutela il gruppo attuale. Resta da stabilire, nel confronto con il club, quali scelte di mercato siano compatibili con i bilanci.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Daniel Foelber – Nov 22, 2026 at 12:30PM EST.

10 stocks we like better than NASDAQ Composite Index ›.

The stock market sell-off has gone from bad to worse, with ripple effects extending to the major indexes.

The Nasdaq Composite (^IXIC -5.28%) is now firmly in a correction, which is a drop of at least 10% from this high. As of Nov. 19 market close, the Dow Jones Industrial Average (^DJI -1.93%) is down 9.7% from its high, while the S&P 500 (^GSPC -3.70%) has proven more resilient but is still down 8.2% from its highs. It's worth mentioning that the Nasdaq and S&P 500 were both at all-time highs in early October -- showcasing the speed and severity of the sell-off.

Here's the level that the Nasdaq would need to reach to be in bear market territory, the differences between a stock market crash and a bear market, and how to navigate further volatility.

Sources indicate that the Nasdaq Composite closed at 23,879.20 on Nov. 19 -- putting it 13.5% off its all-time high.

Industry observers note that if the Nasdaq fell to 22,178.20, that would put the index down 20% from its all-time high of 27,722.75, set on Oct. 6.

A bear market is defined as a prolonged downturn of at least 20% from a high. So, for example, the rapid sell-off during the outbreak of the COVID-19 pandemic in March 2020 and the tariff-induced sell-off in April 2025 both saw the Nasdaq down over 20% from its high, but those levels were very short-lived. In contrast, the broader sell-off in growth stocks during 2022, when the Nasdaq fell 33%, was a legitimate bear market.

A stock market crash is typically defined as a sudden drop in a major index. Exact definitions vary based on speed and severity. For example, a 10% drop in a week can feel more crash-like than a 20% drop over six months, even if the 20% drop is more damaging to your portfolio. However, if the Nasdaq does fall to that 20% drawdown level over the next few weeks, I think it's fair to call it a crash, given that the all-time high occurred just six weeks ago. And the speed of the sell-off, especially over the last couple of weeks, has been rapid. Especially in certain sectors.

It has been revealed that there are already pockets of the stock market that have undergone crash-like sell-offs. In just three weeks, the Nasdaq Composite is down 10.1%. Even gold and Bitcoin (BTC +0.76%) have undergone rapid declines. Nvidia (NVDA -14.01%), which was the world's most valuable company for most of this year, has lost roughly a third of its value in three weeks -- accelerated by the sudden resignation of its founder and CEO of over 33 years, Jensen Huang.

Gold Price in US Dollars data by YCharts.

For investors with outsize exposure to Nvidia and other artificial intelligence (AI) stocks, the sell-off feels like a crash -- even if the major indexes don't reflect as much damage.

According to recent reports, history says that stock market sell-offs present excellent buying opportunities in hindsight. After all, the major indexes have still delivered excellent medium- and long-term returns, even when factoring in current drawdowns. But that doesn't mean investors should assume that every stock that is down is cheap just because the price is lower.

I've been bullish on Nvidia for years. But even I think Jensen Huang's departure negatively impacts the long-term investment thesis on Nvidia. So much so that I shifted my stance from a buy to hold until we get more clarity on the extent of the national security risk, how Nvidia will be restructured without Huang, how the manufacturer will fare under upcoming leadership, whether Nvidia can retain its top talent, if the fundamentals remain intact, and if Nvidia can continue operating with the financial muscle of a large company paired with the flexibility and innovation of a start-up. So while there's a fair argument that the Nvidia sell-off may have gone a bit too far, the business is definitely weaker without Huang, and earnings growth may slow under a more operations-oriented leader like Colette Kress.

It has been revealed that I think there are far more clear-cut buying opportunities in today's market than Nvidia. One example is ASML (ASML -6.63%), which is a leader in the semiconductor equipment industry. Its machines are used by top chip fabs like those operated by Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (TSM -9.48%), Samsung Electronics (SSNLF +0.00%), and Intel (INTC -7.97%). These machines are needed to manufacture next-generation AI chips at commercial scale, making ASML an excellent long-term buy for investors who believe that AI sophistication and use cases will continue to evolve.

Another approach is to buy a beaten-down growth stock exchange-traded fund (ETF) for a basket of top companies. For example, the Vanguard Growth ETF (VUG -5.32%) and Vanguard Mega Cap Growth ETF (MGK -5.58%) both have ultra-low fees and provide exposure to many top companies.

It has been revealed that stock market sell-offs are excellent times to update your watch list with latest opportunities and buy stocks whose values have become more reasonable. However, investors should expect volatility to be swifter and more severe due to widespread access to information, the ability to act on it easily through high-frequency trading, and, at the retail level, mobile trading and zero-fee brokerage services.

Sources indicate that index concentration is another factor driving volatility. At its peak, Nvidia alone made up around 8% of the S&P 500 (still 5.4%). But as the current sell-off proves, the impact of Nvidia on the broader market extends far beyond its own weighting, through the companies that directly or indirectly depend on, compete with, or transact with Nvidia.

Therefore, it's best to only buy stocks you are OK with holding even if volatility continues to intensify.

Here's when a Raspberry Pi 5 could be considered overkill

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (830 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Engadget

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The ongoing memory shortage has led to price increases across the tech industry, even affecting historically affordable computers like the Raspberry Pi.
  • Recent findings suggest that but if you're looking to buy a Raspberry Pi today, you don't have to limit yourself to the newest Pi 5 board.
  • According to recent reports, the Raspberry Pi 5 is more than twice as powerful as the previous-generation Pi 4, but you'll only notice that difference in the real world if you use it as your sole computer.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that powerful? Yes. Necessary? Maybe not.

The ongoing memory shortage has led to price increases across the tech industry, even affecting historically affordable computers like the Raspberry Pi. In early November 2026, Raspberry Pi CEO Eben Upton confirmed that the latest Raspberry Pi 5's 16GB variant was getting an $80 price hike. At $385 for the 16GB Pi 5, it's safe to say that the platform is no longer as affordable as it once was. The Pi 5's 2GB, 4GB and 8GB models saw price increases earlier in 2026 too.

Recent findings suggest that but if you're looking to buy a Raspberry Pi today, you don't have to limit yourself to the newest Pi 5 board. Depending on your intended use case, you could save significant money by buying an older model. The Pi 4, in particular, is still a capable platform with plenty of power for both light desktop use and the typical projects you would run on a Pi. And you're not just saving on the board itself — the Pi 4 has more modest power and cooling requirements than the latest model.

According to recent reports, the Raspberry Pi 5 is more than twice as powerful as the previous-generation Pi 4, but you'll only notice that difference in the real world if you use it as your sole computer. The Raspberry Pi 4's slower CPU means it's not as well-suited for web browsing or heavy workloads. But if you're planning to use the board as a springboard for hobbies like self-hosting, home automation or robotics, you're unlikely to find the Pi 4's performance lacking.

Unfortunately, the higher-end Raspberry Pi 4 models have also seen substantial price increases over the past year or so. Still, they remain slightly cheaper than the Pi 5 and more widely available. The Pi 4's official starting price is just $35 for the 1GB model, the same as the original Raspberry Pi that was released in 2012.

It has been revealed that the Pi 4's less performant CPU also saves you money on power and cooling. It only needs a 15W USB adapter, which is far more common than the 27W USB-C PD adapter that the Pi 5 required. Additionally, the older Pi 4 runs cooler, and you don't need to add a cooling fan to the bill of materials for most projects. However, the Raspberry Pi 5 tends to exceed 176 degrees Fahrenheit (80 degrees Celsius) after a minute of heavy load. Without a cooling fan, the board then throttles the CPU to bring temperatures under control.

In a recent development, when you factor in the cost of a more capable power adapter and cooling hardware, the Pi 5 ends up costing more than the $45 starting price would have you believe. The Pi 4's CPU also benefits from cooling hardware, but it doesn't get hot as quickly and you can get away with a cheap, passive aluminum heatsink.

According to recent reports, if you're willing to stomach the extra initial cost of a Raspberry Pi 5 and hunt for available stock, it's definitely the more future-proof option. The Pi 5's 1GB and 2GB RAM variants, in particular, are only slightly more expensive than the Pi 4, but whether those work for you depends on how much RAM you need from your Pi.

That remarked, the advantage to buying an older Raspberry Pi is availability. Many official retailers simply cannot keep the affordable Pi 5 models in stock, while you can easily buy a Pi 4 or 3B+ without waiting for a restock. The $35 Pi 4 is also available at Micro Center locations in the US, while you'd have to order the base model Pi 5 online and pay for shipping.

According to recent reports, the used market is also flooded with older Pi 4 boards as people upgrade to either the latest model or a more powerful computer altogether. In my city, I see dozens of listings for Raspberry Pi 4 and 3B+ boards on Facebook Marketplace, all selling well below the current retail price. These deals often include power supplies, cases and other necessary accessories too.

In a recent development, raspberry Pi boards are safe to buy second-hand as they're surprisingly durable. They don't have any moving parts and most people use them for relatively lightweight loads. Even if you use a Raspberry Pi as a media server, for instance, the board remains idle most of the time. With minimal power draw and heat generation, a Pi can easily last several years if not a decade. So buying a used Raspberry Pi isn't as much of a gamble as a pre-owned desktop.

Raspberry Pi's CEO has called the recent price increases a "difficult, but temporary" phase and committed to lowering prices when memory costs fall. However, memory manufacturers have warned of supply shortages extending into 2028 and beyond. Put simply, the latest Raspberry Pi may come down in cost anytime soon.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • As scary as the past few weeks have been, from peak to trough the S&P 500 (^GSPC -3.70%) has only tumbled about 7%, leaving it shy of the minimum sell-off of 10% just to qualify as an ordinary correction.
  • Nevertheless, I've been in and around this business long enough to know there are just some things I and every other investor should make a point of doing no matter how scary things get.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By James Brumley – Nov 22, 2026 at 12:45PM EST.

10 stocks we like better than S&P 500 Index ›.

It remains to be seen whether the market's due for any further downside. But there's certainly no denying it's possible.

As scary as the past few weeks have been, from peak to trough the S&P 500 (^GSPC -3.70%) has only tumbled about 7%, leaving it shy of the minimum sell-off of 10% just to qualify as an ordinary correction. Given that we're overdue for such a move, the pullback from October's peak so far still feels like it could continue unfurling. Plenty of investors, including me, are understandably concerned.

Nevertheless, I've been in and around this business long enough to know there are just some things I and every other investor should make a point of doing no matter how scary things get. Here's a rundown of my four non-negotiable rules for surviving market setbacks, and for that matter, thriving during bullish periods.

It has been revealed that it will come as no surprise that all four are so well-preached that they've almost become cliché. There's a good reason for that, however.

As legendary investor Warren Buffett put it, "it's far better to buy a wonderful company at a fair price than a fair company at a wonderful price." This simply means that your priority should be owning quality investments even if it means paying a premium for them. In the long run, quality ends up paying for itself. Or as the antithesis adage goes, "cheap stocks are cheap for a reason.".

This idea is likely to give many investors more than a little pause here. Now three years into a bull market that's been led by AI-mania (which has also in turn drawn out some very speculative IPOs), it's going to be tough for most people to admit they've taken on some risk that's more rooted in hope than actual opportunity. It happens.

The good news is that any major reset for the market should jolt everyone -- and valuations -- back to more historically sustainable norms.

Most everyone has a basic time frame in mind when they're investing. For most of us, it ends with retirement, when we're all likely to dramatically reshape our portfolios for reliable income rather than growth.

According to recent reports, if we're being intellectually honest with ourselves, however, all of us are probably at least a little bit guilty of scooping up the occasional name that's not actually aligned with our target time frame. We're attracted by the buzzy bullish rhetoric, and dive in expecting above-average gains in a below-average amount of time. And that's OK. Again, it happens.

With the risk of a correction (and even a slim chance that it could turn into a full-blown bear market), however, I'm going through each of my remaining positions and asking myself if this is a stock I'm actually interested in holding through the next bear market just so I own it at the beginning of the next bull market. If not, I'm likely letting it go.

After 27 years in this business (which includes the dot-com mania of the late-90s followed by its implosion in the early-2000s), I've learned a thing or two about the boom and bust patterns that play out over and over again.

Sources indicate that the VIX soars to a wildly-high level? By that point, most everyone who was thinking about getting out has already gotten out. Are the pundits (literally) laughing at anyone that's cautiously concerned? Then buying has likely run its full course. No two scenarios are exactly the same, but all of the market's major turning points look pretty darn similar.

The thing is, exceptions to these seemingly predictable norms aren't particularly unusual, and even when they are more or less materializing when and where expected, being just a few days early or a few days late can cost you more than it's worth.

According to recent reports, numbers from mutual fund manufacturer Hartford put things in perspective. The company points out that the S&P 500 gains an average of 13.6% in just the first month of a new bull market, and during its first three months the index soars an average of 25.3%. As much as I'd like to sidestep marketwide weakness, the biggest risk and my biggest fear is missing out on those early moves just by being a few days late to the party.

Recent findings suggest that to be a successful market timer, you have to be perfect 100% of the time. I'm not. So, I'm not even going to try. I'll just improve my odds and scope of success by waiting out short-term weakness with long-term winners.

Finally, while most investors understand the benefits of diversification -- and many of them even make a tentative strategic allocation plan -- too many of us also forget to put these plans into real practice when and to the degree we need to.

Industry observers note that it's not just a matter of sector diversification either. After a long dry spell, small-cap stocks have finally come alive again to outperform large caps. International, precious metals, and real estate are also opportunities to keep on your radar even when they're not performing and everything else is.

Your allocation will never be picture-perfect. If you don't proactively make a point of strategically diversifying for both offensive and defensive reasons, though, you'll obviously never enjoy any of the very real net performance benefit of doing so.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • 10 stocks we like better than iShares Trust - iShares Russell 1000 Value ETF ›.
  • I'm guessing few investors expected this heading into 2026: Large-cap growth stocks beat large-cap value by wide margins in 2023 and 2024.
  • Earnings have thus far delivered, but market leadership has sharply reversed.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By David Dierking – Nov 22, 2026 at 1:00PM EST.

10 stocks we like better than iShares Trust - iShares Russell 1000 Value ETF ›.

I'm guessing few investors expected this heading into 2026: Large-cap growth stocks beat large-cap value by wide margins in 2023 and 2024. They led by a narrower margin in 2025, but the assumption was that the artificial intelligence (AI) trade would continue to lead as long as earnings growth remained strong.

Earnings have thus far delivered, but market leadership has sharply reversed. Year to date, the Russell 1000 Value Index now leads the Russell 1000 Growth Index by nearly 28% in 2026, which would be its widest margin for a calendar year since 2000.

It's been a major rotation away from what's worked in 2023-2025. But can value continue to lead in 2027?

What we see in almost every boom is an eventual normalization. Investors drive prices up beyond what fundamentals can support. Then when growth rates start to slow, stock prices experience a sharp pullback.

Sources indicate that we saw it with internet stocks during the early 2000s and cybersecurity stocks around 2015. And we may be in the early stages of seeing it with AI stocks.

Industry observers note that the key to the growth-to-value rotation centers around AI spending and data centers. Concerns that tech companies will see a requisite return on their investments, coupled with a wave of negative sentiment around building data centers and the possibility of a coordinated effort to slow AI development, are finally pushing investors out of tech and growth.

But they're not abandoning equities altogether. S&P 500 (^GSPC -3.70%) earnings growth is helping to ensure that. Instead, they're rotating into value and defensive equities. Whereas the biggest earnings growth before was concentrated in tech, it's now beginning to spread to other sectors that may be second-order beneficiaries of the AI build-out.

NYSEMKT · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

Industry observers note that the Fed Funds futures market is currently pricing in about three rate hikes by the June meeting. Environments where rates are steadily rising generally don't coincide with growth stock outperformance. Investors tend to be a little more discerning about how much they pay for stocks as rates rise. Currently, that's looking like what could happen in 2027.

Goldman Sachs also sees S&P 500 earnings growth slowing rapidly in 2027. It's expecting 11% growth next year compared to an estimated 36% in 2026. That's still more than enough to allow stock prices to keep rising, but slowing growth tends to work better for value overall.

One catalyst that may not work for value stocks, however, would be an end to the Iran war. That would likely begin bringing inflationary pressures down as well as long-term interest rates. In that scenario, the Federal Reserve might be less compelled to raise rates, which could lead to another stretch of growth-stock leadership.

Taken together, I think conditions are leaning more toward value than growth in 2027. I wouldn't expect such a large gap between the two styles, but I believe a significant slowdown in the theme that has driven the S&P 500 over the past few years would be the biggest catalyst for value stocks next year.

Mortgage rates are constantly changing, since a major part of how rates are set depends on reactions to upcoming inflation reports, job numbers, Fed meetings, global news ... you name it. For example, even tiny changes in the bond market can shift mortgage pricing.

Sources indicate that next week, the Nerds are waiting for the Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) price index, due out Wednesday. It's the Federal Reserve's preferred measure of inflation, so investors will be watching closely. The Fed doesn't set mortgage rates, but lenders anticipate its decisions, so mortgage rates often move before the Fed acts. Stubbornly high inflation is a substantial reason why we’re seeing upward pressure on mortgage rates right now.

It has been revealed that if PCE demonstrates inflation comes in hotter than expected, mortgage rates could climb as markets anticipate further Fed rate hikes. (An increase to the federal funds rate is already widely expected at the Fed’s Dec. 8-9 meeting.) A cooler reading could ease some pressure on mortgage rates for now.

I’m not getting my hopes up too high for meaningfully lower inflation, though. Last week's Producer Price Index revealed wholesale inflation climbed 6.5% over the past year — its fastest pace in four years. Wholesale inflation measures the price businesses pay for things. When businesses’ costs go up, they could pass those along to consumers in the form of higher prices — keeping the flames of inflation alive.

Whether Wednesday's PCE brings relief or another helping of bad inflation news, we'll know before the turkey hits the table on Thursday.

  • Industry observers note that "I am confident that the government's financial condition is at an inflection point," Dalio wrote in a LinkedIn post published Friday.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent's debt buyback announcement this week fits into a broader pattern that can signal a forthcoming crisis, according to billionaire investor Ray Dalio.

According to recent reports, the Bridgewater Associates founder stated Bessent's plan to increase government debt purchases may portend trouble for the U.S. economy. Coupled with the Japanese government reducing its U.S. bond market exposure and surging long-dated American bond yields, Dalio said investors may want to prepare their portfolios for increased risk by owning cryptocurrencies and gold.

Industry observers note that "I am confident that the government's financial condition is at an inflection point," Dalio wrote in a LinkedIn post published Friday. "If this is not dealt with now, the debts will build up to levels where they can't be managed without great trauma.".

Dalio noted that the Treasury Department has "only limited capacity" to buy back bonds. Bessent told CNBC on Thursday that his team was going to "make a market" and that the purchases would likely top $4 billion.

The U.S. is spending about 40% more than it's bringing in, resulting in the burgeoning budget deficit, Dalio noted. The U.S. budget deficit topped $432 billion in July, but Bessent told CNBC that it's likely peaked under President Donald Trump's administration.

Bessent stated in the interview that a team was looking at ways to shrink spending by hundreds of billions of dollars. But Dalio said there is "very little ability" to do so given that it is either committed or considered essential.

After years of overspending, Dalio stated total debt now dwarfs what the U.S. brings in each year. If the U.S. government was a business, Dalio said debt service payments would come in at roughly $11 trillion — about 200% of annual revenue.

Dalio, 77, warned the cost of repaying principal and servicing the debt will only grow over time.

In a recent development, to solve this, Dalio noted the U.S. needs to carefully employ a three-part strategy to get the budget deficit down to 3% of gross domestic product.

First, Dalio said the U.S. government needs to reduce its spending. Second, he said tax revenue needs to be raised. Finally, the Newly introduced York native and Harvard Business School alumni said lower interest rates were needed.

According to recent reports, "All three need to happen concurrently so as to prevent any one from being too large," Dalio mentioned. "If any one is too large, the adjustment will be traumatic.".

Dalio cautioned against ramming through these adjustments by "force." For instance, "it would be very bad if the Federal Reserve unnaturally forced interest rates down," he remarked.

Dalio noted it's vital to to take steps now, while the economy is healthy. An economy in recession requires increased government spending, he said.

Industry observers note that dalio noted the exact timing of a debt crisis can be swayed by variables ranging from military conflict to political change. On its current trajectory, the U.S. could enter such a crisis in as early as one year or as late as five. "My guess, which I suppose will be a bad one, is that it will come in three years, give or take two, if the course we're on is not changed.".

To prepare, Dalio recommended investors are underweight debt assets, such as bonds.

As much as 10% to 15% of a portfolio could land in gold, as well as "a bit" of bitcoin, the hedge fund founder remarked.

In a recent development, dalio's post came at the tail end of a volatile week for U.S. financial markets. Rising long-term Treasury yields have pressured stocks, leading the S&P 500 to snap a a three-week-long advance.
