📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Prosper Junior Bakiny – Nov 22, 2026 at 1:03PM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Eli Lilly ›.

The weight loss drug market is one of the hottest areas in the pharmaceutical industry right now, and according to projections, it will continue growing rapidly over the medium term. Eli Lilly (LLY -0.30%) is currently a leader in this space.

Its financial results in recent quarters have been excellent, partly thanks to its obesity franchise. Even though some investors worry that increased competition will erode Eli Lilly's market share, the company's pipeline appears strong enough to withstand the challenge. Here's more on why Eli Lilly is well positioned to remain the top player in the anti-obesity space over the next five years.

Sources indicate that eli Lilly's approved weight loss portfolio right now includes injectable tirzepatide, sold under the brand name Zepbound in this market, and Foundayo, an oral anti-obesity treatment. Zepbound was first approved about three years ago, and it is posting outstanding sales growth. In the third quarter, Zepbound's revenue increased by 49% year over year to $5.4 billion.

Sources indicate that foundayo earned approval in April, and it has had a fairly strong commercial ramp-up so far. In the third quarter, it generated $184 million in revenue. Competitors might launch treatments that rival -- or perhaps even exceed -- Zepbound and Foundayo in efficacy. But Eli Lilly will do the same, which may help the firm defend, or even improve, its market share. Below are some of Eli Lilly's most crucial pipeline candidates.

Data from Eli Lilly. Chat by the author.

In a recent development, note that two of these candidates, retatrutide and EloraTZP, achieved greater weight loss than Zepbound, although head-to-head comparisons remain somewhat limited. This does raise a potential problem, however.

Will these latest medicines cannibalize Zepbound sales? Some of that will happen, and for what it's worth, it's better if Eli Lilly's own products capture sales from older ones rather than other pharmaceutical giants taking market share away from the company. However, newer products will also help Eli Lilly expand the market.

First, medicines with greater weight-loss efficacy will help the organization attract patients who haven't lost enough weight on Zepbound alone.

NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

In fact, Lilly has already made retatrutide available to some patients, despite it not yet being approved. Eligible patients must have failed to respond to standard obesity interventions, among other criteria.

Sources indicate that second, eloralintide isn't a GLP-1 product. It mimics the amylin hormone, a differentiated approach that could yield improved tolerability. Eloralintide demonstrated weight-loss efficacy comparable to GLP-1 products in Phase 2 studies, with strong tolerability.

Further, Eli Lilly's expanding portfolio could help it maintain strong pricing power, even as more weight-loss options enter the market. Treatments with stronger efficacy than Zepbound could command a premium price. That may allow the organization to keep revenue growing fast while also preserving its margins and profits. Here's the most important point.

While an increasingly competitive weight-loss market is often cited as one reason Eli Lilly isn't worth investing in right now, the tech giant's pipeline suggests it could perform just fine despite the challenge.

Eli Lilly's revenue and earnings have grown at much higher rates than the industry averages in recent years.

LLY Revenue (Quarterly YoY Growth) data by YCharts.

For context, a pharmaceutical leader with a double-digit year-over-year revenue rate is already pretty impressive. Eli Lilly's growth rate will eventually slow. But given its work in the weight loss market, the drop might not be that dramatic, especially when we also factor in the clinical and commercial progress it is making in other areas, such as diabetes, oncology, immunology, and neuroscience.

Recent findings suggest that an earnings per share (EPS) growth rate of about 20% to 25% over the next five years seems reasonable for the tech giant, and considering the progress it is still making across various areas, the market may continue to price the stock at a premium. Given all that, Eli Lilly's forward price-to-earnings ratio of 27.2 doesn't seem unreasonable, even though it’s much higher than the 18.9 average for healthcare stocks. The stock is a buy.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Michael Carrick remarked he had to be careful with Mason Mount after the England midfielder handed Manchester United an injury scare in their friendly draw with Paris St Germain.

Mount has had a torrid time with injuries since signing from Chelsea in a £55m-deal three years ago, starting only 25 Premier League games for United in that time.

The 27-year-old has been successfully deployed by Carrick in a central midfield role during pre-season, leading to speculation that United may not make another expected signing in that department.

But Mount played only 18 minutes of Saturday’s 1-1 draw against the European champions in Gothenburg before being replaced by Scotland international Tyler Fletcher.

“He [Mount] got kicked. We just wanted to be careful and look after him,” Carrick, the United head coach, told reporters in Sweden.

“We’ve been lucky with injuries so far, so we wanted to be careful.”.

Post-match video footage showed Mount walking freely on to the United bus without the aid of a protective boot or knee support.

Sources indicate that michael Carrick told VG Mason Mount was taken off as a precaution. Looked OK leaving stadium. pic.twitter.com/Uo0fBtgpAl.

United went behind within two minutes at the Ullevi Stadium when Liverpool target Ibrahim Mbaye punished slack marking to put PSG ahead.

Bryan Mbeumo fired United level after 32 minutes following good work from Amad Diallo, the Cameroon forward’s third goal in two games after his match-winning double against Atletico Madrid.

United meet Leeds in a Dublin friendly on Wednesday before coming up against AC Milan and their former manager Ruben Amorim next Saturday.

United open their Premier League campaign at Hull on August 22.

In a recent development, “It was good game. PSG is good so we had to keep building fitness. I am happy to have other [players] back and we have to keep going.”.

“It’s good for me. I enjoyed it. We need to build fitness, we have a big season ahead.”.

“It’s a good game PSG are tough to beat and we got a draw and now think about the next game [against Leeds in Dublin].”.

It has been revealed that “We have two more games against Leeds a and Milan. We need to have massive season and hope to win a trophy.”.

All over in Gothenburg and it’s been a good match for Michael Carrick’s team. They looked sharper and quicker than their win over Atletico Madrid last week (what the manager wanted) and things are moving in the right direction. Manchester United continue their Sweden sojourn with match against Paris St-Germain in Gothenburg.

Clearly a clash against the back-to-back Champions League winners is a step up from their previous two pre-season friendlies (victories against Rosenborg and Atletico Madrid), but at the same time this is more a chance for players to get miles in the legs and see how fresh signings and possibly some young guns fit in.

One of those latest signings is Youri Tielemans, and the Belgian international is in line to make his debut after his move from Aston Villa. Other team news is that Bruno Fernandes is back and ready to captain the team.

Michael Carrick has also been boosted by the returns of Matheus Cunha, Diogo Dalot and Noussair Mazraoui after their post-World Cup breaks.

Cunha, however, will not play a part in today’s match because of a “minor illness” according to the MUTV website. He is expected to link up with the squad in Ireland, where they face Leeds United at Croke Park, after the match.

This will be Man Utd’s first outing since the 2-1 win over Atletico, a performance and result that pleased Carrick.

Sources indicate that “I enjoyed it, I thought there was a lot of good in things that we are looking to improve on,” the United manager said. “Building on what we did for the last seven months, I think there is a lot of good signs for us, it’s never going to be the exact stage we want to be at. But I thought there was really a lot of positives to take out of the game, individual, collectively as a team, senior players looking strong and fit, and the younger players doing really well.

“The spirit and the camaraderie is so crucial for the team, it’s great to see the boys getting on so naturally and enjoying each other’s company. Collectively we looked strong as a team, which is always the most important thing, and individual performances seeing the young players come on to have an impact.”.

College Scholarship Breakdown: Types, Sponsors and Eligibility at a Glance

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1397 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nerdwallet

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Scholarships have become a standard part of applying for college.
  • It has been revealed that before you go searching for a scholarship, it's important to understand the types of scholarships available and how to identify the ones that give you the best chance of winning, which can save you time and potentially earn you more funding.
  • It has been revealed that scholarships are often funded by three groups: private organizations, institutions like universities, and government agencies.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Scholarships have become a standard part of applying for college. You can learn about scholarships in a variety of ways, but looking through an online database of available scholarships — the most common way — can be overwhelming.

It has been revealed that before you go searching for a scholarship, it's important to understand the types of scholarships available and how to identify the ones that give you the best chance of winning, which can save you time and potentially earn you more funding. Here’s what you need to know about scholarships to decide which ones are best for you.

It has been revealed that scholarships are often funded by three groups: private organizations, institutions like universities, and government agencies. None is better than the other when it comes to awarding funds.

Nonprofit organizations and clubs that are looking for students either majoring in or researching certain fields, or who have experience volunteering in a specific field.

Companies that want to support all students or only fund those majoring in a field that relates to the companies’ industries.

Financial institutions, such as banks or credit unions, that want to support their community or their members.

Individuals or families that are funding private scholarships, usually in memory of a loved one.

Universities and colleges that are offering funds to students who attend their campuses.

Research organizations that want to fund students who will research in their areas of interest and further their causes.

These scholarships generally are provided by local, state or federal government agencies for a variety of reasons. Despite being funded by a government agency, the scholarships do not require you to pay back the money — unlike federal student loans.

Some scholarships pay for anything related to college expenses, including tuition, room and board, books and supplies, and more. Other scholarships limit what you can pay for with the funds, such as only tuition or tuition along with books. It’s crucial to look at this restriction when applying for scholarships to ensure the funds will go toward what you need to cover.

Merit scholarships require you to show excellence or achievements in your schoolwork, through talents and abilities, and even leadership or service work. Because these types of awards can be highly competitive, merit scholarships might require more than just achievements, such as volunteer or leadership experience. This means merit-based scholarships can overlap with other types of scholarship categories. Here are some examples of merit-based scholarships:.

Merit scholarships often require you to have earned a minimum grade point average (GPA). The minimum GPA depends on the scholarship but often ranges from 2.0 to 4.0, with more competitive scholarships usually requiring higher GPAs. Scholarships with lower GPA minimums are more likely to consider additional factors, such as financial need.

Some merit scholarships might require a minimum ACT or SAT score instead of a GPA — or in addition to a minimum GPA.

It has been revealed that merit scholarships might also require applicants to have participated in activities outside of their schoolwork. This is common for scholarships that require membership in a certain group or organization. For example, membership in agricultural clubs, such as 4-H or FFA, and scouting groups, such as the National Eagle Scout Association, appear in scholarship requirements.

Sources indicate that some scholarships emphasize volunteering or community service and only consider applicants who have that experience. Applications vary in how detailed their requirements can be. Some scholarships want only a general description of where and how you’ve volunteered, and others might require experience with a service project that demonstrates more leadership experience or time volunteering with a certain type of organization.

Scholarships that are awarded to students who can’t afford college are called need-based scholarships.

Unmet financial need is the difference between what it will cost you to attend college and what you can afford to pay. Because calculating how much you can afford is a complicated process, many scholarships refer to your FAFSA to document your financial need.

Sources indicate that some scholarship requirements may be as straightforward as demonstrating that you have financial need, but some scholarships might have income limits. However, income restrictions are less common.

According to recent reports, athletic scholarships are for — you guessed it — athletes. They are usually offered by colleges and universities to recruit athletes onto their collegiate teams and can be competitive. Which sports have scholarships available and the scholarship amounts vary by college.

Even though the main criterion for an athletic scholarship is being good at your sport, you’ll likely still need to show that you can keep up with your schoolwork. Most athletic scholarships require students to earn a minimum GPA or test scores to remain eligible while they’re in college.

It has been revealed that some scholarships are designated for students majoring in a general field, such as science or education, but others can be for very specific areas of study. For example, a scholarship for students majoring in a natural resource field could include majors in biology, ecology, wildlife biology, conservation education, forestry, soils and hydrology. However, a stricter scholarship might state that students have to major in more specific topics, such as biochemistry or microbial ecology.

It has been revealed that scholarships are available for active and former members of the military and members of their families. In addition to federal funds available for veterans to attend college, private organizations and some universities have scholarships for veterans to offset the cost of a degree.

Industry observers note that which family members can apply for funds depends on the individual scholarship. For example, some scholarships extend to children or spouses of veterans, but some go as far in a family tree as great-grandchildren.

Veteran- and military-focused scholarships might require that applicants or their family members enlisted in a certain branch, served during a particular time or conflict, or meet a certain rank or status such as receiving disability. Scholarships might also require that the applicant be a wartime veteran or family member of a wartime veteran; not all veterans meet this status.

Recent findings suggest that scholarships are also awarded to people who identify with a certain group. Common examples of identity-based scholarships include those for people who have disabilities, belong to certain ethnic or religious groups, identify as LGBTQIA+ or are first-generation students. Some identity-based scholarships require applicants to meet several criteria, such as belonging to more than one identity group.

Outside of what would be considered standard DEI groups, there are scholarships for applicants who identify with less common groups, such as veganism, homelessness and model railroad builders.

In a recent development, the best scholarships for you depend on your situation. For example, if you are a skilled athlete with a good academic record, going for an athletic scholarship might give you the most funding. On the other hand, if you’re going to research a topic that isn’t common, looking for scholarships that support your research topic might be your best bet because competition could be lower.

Good tactics to figure out which scholarships are worth your time include:.

Industry observers note that think of the skills, talents, experience and identities that are unique to you. For example, being a child of a veteran immediately qualifies you for scholarships with fewer applicants than scholarships open to everyone. Likewise, if you embrace a certain ethnicity, identify with a specific group or have experience with a type of work, you might qualify for scholarships that appreciate and recognize those attributes more than the average scholarship.

In a recent development, apply if you think you're eligible. Don’t apply to just a few scholarships and hope you get them. Instead, apply for as many scholarships as you can and for which you’re eligible. This increases your chances of receiving funds. Even small scholarships can make a significant impact when you add several of them together.

In a recent development, understand how you can use the money. If you already have a scholarship that covers only books, applying for the same type of scholarship isn’t helpful if you don’t need the extra funds. Instead, look for scholarships that cover the costs you have remaining.

It has been revealed that not sure where to look? Our sister site Scholarships360.org provides students with vetted scholarship opportunities. That would be a good place to start.

Addas a preferred source on Google.

However, the company continues to expand its reach through joint ventures and global system integrators.

In the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, revenue reached about $7.3 billion. This reflects a revenue growth of approximately 87% over the preceding year. During this time, the company generated a net income of about $3.7 billion, yielding a net margin of around 50%.

It has been revealed that as of its December 2025 balance sheet, the current ratio stands at approximately 7.1x. This metric measures a firm's ability to cover its short-term debts with assets that can be converted to cash within a year. The company has a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.0x, which measures total debt relative to shareholders' equity. In the fiscal year ended Dec. 31, 2025, free cash flow was close to $2.1 billion. Note that stock-based compensation accounted for roughly 32% of operating cash flow, inflating reported cash generation, since SBC is a non-cash expense added back in the cash flow statement.

UiPath faces risks from its heavy reliance on a single automation platform and potential customer concentration. It competes against large cloud providers like Salesforce.com Inc. (CRM -1.47%) and newly introduced start-ups focused on artificial intelligence. The firm also navigates complex international regulations and operational challenges from rapid global scaling.

Palantir Technologies deals with long and unpredictable sales cycles and a high concentration of revenue among a few large customers. The firm also faces risks related to the ethical use of its software and evolving data privacy laws. It relies heavily on third-party cloud providers like Amazon.com Inc. (AMZN -4.10%) and Microsoft Corp. (MSFT -2.77%) for its infrastructure.

UiPath appears to be the more value-oriented choice with a much lower sales multiple, whereas Palantir trades at a substantial premium reflecting its faster growth.

Valuation metrics include those sourced from Financial Modeling Prep (FMP) and may differ from those of other data providers.

The Forward P/E is a valuation based on future earnings estimates. The P/S ratio measures market cap divided by sales over the past twelve months.

Recent findings suggest that AI is becoming a dominant theme in UiPath's business, with 18 of its 20 largest deals in its most recently reported quarter involving AI. The business raised its annual recurring revenue to more than $1.9 billion in its second quarter of fiscal 2027, up 13% year over year. Revenue in the quarter rose 13% to $410 million. For the full-year fiscal 2027, Wall Street analysts project revenue to rise 11% to $1.79 billion. Net income is expected to drop 30% to $200 million, while free cash flow is set to rise about 16% to $425 million, according to consensus estimates.

Recent findings suggest that uiPath notes that in the age of AI, its platform is about orchestration of enterprisewide software and systems to enable companies to find the efficiencies that AI promises while providing guardrails around AI and also working to ensure exactness--the idea being that even if AI is accurate 99.9% of the time, businesses like banks and medical providers need 100% accuracy. UiPath management says many businesses are deploying AI agents, but few have the connective tissue to link these single-task agents to the larger enterprise and to the multiple other software platforms they have deployed. UiPath says its software provides all that in a vendor-agnostic manner. That is its path to long-term growth.

Palantir started out as a tech contractor to the U.S. military, and the federal government still accounts for half of its revenue. But the business has been successfully expanding beyond government work, with about a quarter of sales coming from international customers and a significant minority of revenue from the private sector. For the first time in it smost recently reported quarter, private sector revenue exceeded U.S. government revenue.

Industry observers note that palantir states customers are drawn to its sovereign AI--its term for systems that can help build themselves while protecting what makes each system the AI is refining, so it is not commoditized. Companies like Nvidia Corp. (NVDA -14.01%) and L3Harris Technologies (LHX -2.59%) are notable customers of Palantir's sovereign AI.

According to recent reports, the boom in private-sector AI business should double Palantir's 2026 sales to $8.6 billion, with a $2.7 billion jump in net income to $4.4 billion. 2027 should see continued rapid growth, with consensus estimates projecting revenue of $13.1 billion and net income exceeding $6 billion.

Recent findings suggest that palantir has the fastest-growing business, but its shares come at an exceptional premium. Still, the expected drop in UiPath net income is a bit of a concern. Yet, UiPath shares are priced below the average S&P 500 stock (which trades at around 19x forward earnings), making UiPath shares the better risk relative to pricey Palantir.

By Courtney Carlsen – Nov 22, 2026 at 1:15PM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Archer Aviation ›.

In a recent development, air taxis may attract headlines, but Archer Aviation's (ACHR -9.06%) biggest opportunity could lie beyond commercial passenger flights. The electric vertical take-off and landing (eVTOL) aircraft developer has teamed up with defense technology company Anduril to develop hybrid-electric VTOL aircraft, with Thunder's first flight planned for 2027.

Sources indicate that for investors, Thunder's debut reveals another side of the Archer story: a defense business that could eventually outgrow its commercial air-taxi operation. Here's why Archer's military push is worth a closer look.

Archer Aviation develops the Midnight aircraft, its flagship aircraft for its commercial air taxi business. The company is currently working through a multi-year Type Certification process with the Federal Aviation Administration and is in the final phase of the four-stage process. It has conducted piloted flights in Northern California, and CEO Adam Goldstein hopes to begin passenger flights in 2027.

NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

While commercial air taxis get the attention, Archer is making a wise decision to diversify into defense with a hybrid-electric variant of its Midnight aircraft in collaboration with Anduril. Because military procurement operates under the Department of Defense airworthiness standards, Archer could generate revenue and validate its hardware with real-world flight hours before its commercial air taxis scale.

In July, Archer and Anduril unveiled the hybrid-electric VTOL military variant, Thunder, and a commercial cargo variant, Halo. What makes these VTOLs intriguing is that they give the military an aircraft that falls somewhere between small tactical drones and expensive helicopters.

Unlike helicopters, these aircraft can fly uncrewed into contested airspace without risking the lives of highly trained military pilots or the expensive Viper and Apache helicopters. Meanwhile, like helicopters, these vehicles can take off and land vertically, operating from small airfields, operating bases, or small naval decks without needing traditional runways.

According to recent reports, it will take time for Archer Aviation's consumer air taxi business to take off and reach commercial scale, especially since it's an entirely new form of transportation. By expanding into defense, the firm can get its aircraft flying and open itself to the potential to win major government contracts, which could provide long-term revenue visibility and stability.

Earnings from Thunder and Halo will likely be limited in the near term, as Archer ramps up test flights in 2027. However, Archer has expanded its defense footprint by acquiring Insitu, Wisk Aero, and SkyGrid from Boeing. Insitu adds $200 million in defense revenue immediately, and Archer also inherits its customer relationships and offices in the U.S., Australia, the U.K., and the United Arab Emirates.

Archer Aviation's air taxis could change how we travel across cities, and passenger flights will begin on a limited basis in 2027, with full commercial operation projected for 2028. That said, some experts think 2028 is overly ambitious, so in the near term, defense provides a financial bridge that will keep the organization growing even if commercial air taxi rollouts slip past 2028.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • The conventional wisdom behind the trade is that perceived hard assets, like cryptocurrencies and precious metals, gain as investors try to hedge against a weaker U.S.
  • "The size of the Treasury purchases announced so far by Bessent are trivial in comparison to the size of the overall market, but the [signaling] effect was very powerful," said Stephen Coltman, head of macro at 21Shares, a crypto-focused creator of exchange-traded funds.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The debasement trade is gaining latest traction on Wall Street as concern over the size and cost of the budget deficit mounts.

The conventional wisdom behind the trade is that perceived hard assets, like cryptocurrencies and precious metals, gain as investors try to hedge against a weaker U.S. dollar and Treasury debt in the face of ballooning government spending. Those fears reached a fever pitch last week before, and after, the Treasury Department's unusual step of increasing debt buybacks under Secretary Scott Bessent.

"The size of the Treasury purchases announced so far by Bessent are trivial in comparison to the size of the overall market, but the [signaling] effect was very powerful," said Stephen Coltman, head of macro at 21Shares, a crypto-focused creator of exchange-traded funds.

Gold touched three-month highs Monday, building on last week's advance of more than 5%. The yellow metal has climbed for five straight weeks and in August is on track for its biggest monthly rise since 1999.

In a recent development, bitcoin added 2% Monday, to the highest since May. Last week, the digital currency soared 22%, its biggest three-day rally since 2023. Overnight Tuesday, the crypto touched $80,000.

Conversely, investors fled the dollar.

The U.S. dollar index, which tracks the dollar against six other leading currencies, hit three-month lows last week and recorded its third down week in the last four. The index was little changed on Monday as investors expressed little appetite to bid up the greenback.

According to recent reports, the Treasury Department mentioned last week that it would double the maximum size of its bond buyback, to at least $4 billion from $2 billion. Two senior Treasury officials told CNBC Monday that the department could use its General Account to help fund the plans.

Sources indicate that last week's announcement followed news that the monthly U.S. budget deficit in July reached a five-year high and came at the same time as total federal government debt topped $40 trillion. Bessent told CNBC last week that he wields a "big toolkit" to calm the government bond market amid concerns about the government's financial health.

Industry observers note that long-dated U.S. Treasury yields surged last week, at one point sending the 30-year yield to almost a 20-year high of 5.34%, up from 4.82% in late June. Yields dipped and then rebounded in the wake of the Treasury buyback move, a signal that bond investors believed Bessent's moves were inadequate.

"Markets are saying something," the billionaire philanthropist and former energy trader John Arnold said in a Friday post on X. The weaker dollar, lower Treasury prices and strengthening hard assets, are "all part of the debasement trade," he wrote.

The Treasury's moves could aid the bond market, but also translate into outsized pain for the dollar, according to Nohshad Shah, Citadel Securities' head of fixed income sales for Europe, the Middle East and Africa.

Sources indicate that the stakes are high for monetary policymakers, as a weaker greenback can ease financial conditions, Shah mentioned. U.S. inflation — above the Federal Reserve's 2% target for five years — could worsen.

The Fed might need to hike interest rates in response, Shah said. Fed funds futures reflect about a 56% chance the central bank raises borrowing costs at its October meeting, up more than seven percentage points from a week ago, according to CME's FedWatch tool.

"The bond market's message is straightforward: fiscal or monetary policy should be tighter," Shah said in a Monday note. "Households may ultimately pay for policymakers' unwillingness to fix the roof whilst the sun is shining.".

Coltman at 21Shares stated the appetite for alternative stores of value also stems from mounting geopolitical tension. The U.S. on Monday rolled out a global sanctions program focused on segregating Iran from the global economy, days after slapping 50% tariffs on billions of dollars in Canadian exports.

Still, assets that would benefit from a debasement trade have recently received votes of confidence on Wall Street.

According to recent reports, deutsche Bank analyst Michael Hsueh said in a Monday note that gold could surpass his target price of $4,800 an ounce. Already, that level suggests the precious metal only need to rise another 3% or so from where it closed on Friday. "We see the Treasury policy change as underlining the gold constructive view," Hsueh said.

Recent findings suggest that billionaire investor Ray Dalio recommended investors remain overweight gold and bitcoin ahead of what he warned could become a debt crisis in the U.S. as a result of unchecked government spending. Gold could account for as much as 15% of a model portfolio, the Bridgewater Associates founder said.

"The government's financial condition is at an inflection point," Dalio wrote on LinkedIn Friday. "If this is not dealt with now, the debts will build up to levels where they can't be managed without great trauma.".

Others are less sure, devaluing the notion of a debasement trade.

It's probably too early to endorse the idea unless it's clear that the Fed will go along with the Treasury Department, said Alexander Lis, investing chief at Social Discovery Ventures.

For the first time, SpaceX successfully caught the upper stage of its Starship rocket using mechanical arms attached to its launch tower. It was a major milestone for the manufacturer, setting the stage for its future space ambitions.

According to recent reports, also this weekend, rival United Launch Alliance (ULA), a joint venture between Boeing (BA -2.88%) and Lockheed Martin (LMT -1.11%), had a major setback. Its Vulcan rocket failed, destroying 40 Amazon (AMZN -4.10%) Leo satellites in the process.

NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

Recent findings suggest that this weekend's results show the growing distance that SpaceX is gaining over its competitors in the space sector. Its achievement also comes months after Blue Origin's New Glenn rocket exploded on the ground in May, destroying the manufacturer's only launch pad. Space competitors are clearly struggling with releases, which is also hurting Amazon's efforts to get its Leo satellite internet service, which will compete with Amazon's Starlink, off the ground.

It has been revealed that still, not everything went well for SpaceX this weekend. It decided to abandon trying to catch Starship's Super Heavy booster, which it diverted to the Gulf of Mexico, where it exploded before reaching the water.

The Super Heavy Booster is the much more expensive part of Starship. According to PayLoad Research, a Starship rocket costs around $90 million, with the Super Heavy booster making up about $63 million of the total. However, the Super Heavy Booster is the easier part of the rocket to catch, and SpaceX has already caught it on its own multiple times.

Sources indicate that having a fully reusable rocket is paramount for SpaceX to achieve some of its loftier goals, like orbital data centers and Earth-to-Earth cargo transport. By rapidly reusing a $90 million rocket multiple times rather than just once, SpaceX not only saves a lot of money but also greatly increases the number of launches it can perform.

This completely changes the economics of space and sets the manufacturer up for strong growth and the ability to disrupt industries, essentially shifting SpaceX's space segment from being a low-margin launch business into a scalable logistics business, where fuel and maintenance are the main recurring costs.

Recent findings suggest that it also positions SpaceX as a monopoly in the orbital economy. By being the only tech giant with massive, rapidly reusable rockets, SpaceX would control the entire market. It could price its services below competitors to win deals and capture the bulk of the market, while its huge cost advantage would allow it to pocket strong margins. Meanwhile, it would have a huge structural advantage that would allow it to build out Starlink or orbital data centers at costs well below competitors that would have to pay retail launch prices.

Sources indicate that spaceX still faces obstacles to achieving some of its loftier goals. It doesn't matter if SpaceX can launch data centers into space at a cost much lower than competitors' if it can't overcome some crucial hurdles.

Industry observers note that one obstacle it will need to overcome is getting chips that can withstand cosmic radiation, which can flip bits and corrupt data. It is currently working with Nvidia (NVDA -14.01%) on a solution. It also needs to be able to develop a cooling solution, as currently there is no way to cool these systems in the vacuum of space. Meanwhile, with Earth-to-Earth transport, it will need to get past a lot of political red tape to launch rockets from places like China to the U.S.

Overall, this past weekend helped put SpaceX in the driver's seat and gave investors another reason to get excited about the stock. While it still has hurdles to overcome before entering some exciting new markets, its lead just keeps growing. That makes this growth stock a buy.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Investors have been grappling with stock market volatility, weighing elevated oil prices, persistent geopolitical tensions, the Federal Reserve's rate hike and a debate about AI safety. For all that, it helps to look beyond short-term noise and focus on stocks with strong long-term growth potential.

Top Wall Street analysts' recommendations can help investors gain clarity, as these experts conduct in-depth research to pick stocks with attractive growth prospects.

Here are three stocks favored by some of Wall Street's top pros, according to TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

Enterprise software and cloud infrastructure company Oracle (ORCL) recently unveiled better-than-expected results for the first quarter of fiscal 2027. The quarter benefited from solid growth in cloud infrastructure revenue.

It has been revealed that after hosting a series of investor meetings with Ken Bond, Oracle head of investor relations following Q1 earnings, Guggenheim analyst John DiFucci reiterated a buy rating on the stock with a price target of $400. Oracle remains a Guggenheim Best Idea, he mentioned.

"We continue to believe ORCL is a decade stock, driven by the massive (and profitable) opportunity ahead for AI training and inferencing," said DiFucci. He also cited the traditional Public Cloud business and additional AI-enabled cloud database and cloud applications for his bullish stance. DiFucci expects all the factors to drive revenue and profit acceleration over the next few years.

While Oracle delivered 850 MW of data center capacity in Q1 FY27, Bond cautioned that Infrastructure as a Service revenue in any quarter depends more on the timing of when that capacity comes online, than on the headline MW number. DiFucci expects IaaS growth to stay strong, with full-year growth expected above Q1 FY27's 120% constant currency rate. Management expects total revenue growth to accelerate sequentially throughout fiscal 2027, as the faster-growing infrastructure business makes up a larger share of the mix.

DiFucci addressed concerns regarding customer concentration, saying OpenAI's share of total remaining performance obligations has dropped from 80% last June to about 50% now, and is expected to keep falling as new contracts are signed with new and existing customers.

Recent findings suggest that diFucci ranks No. 263 among more than 12,490 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 62% of the time, delivering an average return of about 17.5%. See Oracle Insider Trading Activity on TipRanks.

Space systems and launch services provider Rocket Lab (RKLB) was recently initiated as a buy with an $80 price target by Raymond James analyst Brian Gesuale.

"RKLB has assembled launch, spacecraft, components, payloads and optical communications, with Neutron and Iridium completing medium-lift and applications/spectrum in 2027," said Gesuale.

In a recent development, the 5-star analyst highlighted that with the completion of the Iridium acquisition, Rocket Lab will become the only vertically integrated space manufacturer with positive free cash flow (FCF). The deal will add a deployed constellation valued at more than $3 billion, globally coordinated L-band spectrum and about $500 million in earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization (EBITDA) and $300 million in free cash flow (FCF).

Gesuale highlighted RKLB's strong revenue and backlog growth and progress toward positive EBITDA and FCF in 2027/2028. Rocket Lab is moving from a heavy investment phase into monetization, with estimated revenue growth of 59% in 2026, the analyst remarked, noting that RKLB's backlog has more than doubled to almost $2.4 billion from $1.1 billion in Q3 2025.

Given strong growth projections, the analyst expects RKLB's gross margins to expand from about a 35% trough in 2027 to about 47% by 2030, while R&D spending is estimated to decline from ~35% of sales in 2026 to about 10% in 2028, creating substantial operating leverage as the platform matures.

According to recent reports, gesuale ranks No. 369 among more than 12,490 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 63% of the time, delivering an average return of about 17%. See Rocket Lab Statistics on TipRanks.

J.P. Morgan analyst Doug Anmuth recently upgraded Meta Platforms (META) to buy from hold and raised his price target to $820 from $640. Despite the year-to-date underperformance of META, the 5-star analyst still sees significant upside, as Meta is in the early stages of launching frontier models and AI-powered offerings beyond advertising, particularly the Muse AI agent and Meta Model API access.

"Frontier models are at the core of Meta's product and monetization pipeline over a multi-year period, and its path toward superintelligence," mentioned Anmuth.

In the summer of 2025, Meta set a goal to rebuild its Meta Superintelligence Labs team and deliver frontier AI models within a year, the analyst mentioned. The team appears to have met its goal, rapidly advancing from the rollout of Muse Spark 1.1 in July to Muse Spark 1.3, which is competitive with Claude and GPT models, Anmuth said.

Industry observers note that meanwhile, Meta's Watermelon product will expand opportunities in consumer products, business intelligence, and Family of Apps engagement, the analyst said. The product will enhance internal operations and overall efficiency, said Anmuth, who's confident of Meta's ability to bring consumer-driven AI products to its extensive user base of 4 billion and views its distribution network as a competitive advantage.

While Meta has focused on frontier models and AI product development, Anmuth also sees solid opportunity in its AI infrastructure capacity, which he believes will support future compute needs.

Anmuth ranks No. 832 among more than 12,490 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been successful 57% of the time, delivering an average return of about 9.40%. See Meta Platforms Financials on TipRanks.

#62302. Palantir Stock Could Finish 2026 Lower. Its Only 2 Losing Years Ended Very Differently.

📖 Baca
Business & Policy ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Fool ↗ Open Full Page

Palantir Stock Could Finish 2026 Lower. Its Only 2 Losing Years Ended Very Differently.

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (862 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • 10 stocks we like better than Palantir Technologies ›.
  • Sources indicate that palantir Technologies (PLTR -6.63%) has finished only two calendar years in the red since it started trading in September 2020, and it might add a third.
  • The stock has already swung widely this year, closing as low as about $107 in late June before reaching a record close over $209 in October.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Daniel Sparks – Nov 22, 2026 at 1:37PM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Palantir Technologies ›.

Sources indicate that palantir Technologies (PLTR -6.63%) has finished only two calendar years in the red since it started trading in September 2020, and it might add a third. As I write, shares are near $160, about 10% under the $177.75 they closed at to end 2025, with less than six weeks of trading left in the year.

The stock has already swung widely this year, closing as low as about $107 in late June before reaching a record close over $209 in October.

Palantir's two losing years didn't end the same way, though. The stock dropped around 23% in 2021 and then shed another 65% in 2022. But the 2022 loss was followed by a 167% rise in 2023.

In a recent development, what separated the two? I think it mainly boiled down to the price investors were paying heading into the next year, and whether the business was getting stronger. On one of those two fronts, today looks more like the end of 2021 than the end of 2022.

Palantir's 2021 wasn't a bad year for the business. Revenue climbed 41% year over year to $1.54 billion, and the organization's net loss shrank to $520 million from $1.17 billion in 2020.

Sources indicate that but growth was cooling as the year ended. Fourth-quarter revenue grew 34% year over year, a slowdown from the full year's pace.

The stock wasn't cheap, either, even after its 2021 drop. Based on Palantir's share count at the end of 2021, its $18.21 closing price gave the organization a market cap of around $37 billion -- about 24 times its 2021 sales.

Sure, a high price can hold up if growth does, but Palantir's growth kept cooling. Full-year revenue grew 24% in 2022, and fourth-quarter revenue climbed just 18% year over year. The tech giant also lost $374 million that year, and the stock shed around two-thirds of its value.

Recent findings suggest that the end of 2022 set up something very different. At $6.42 a share, Palantir's market cap was around $13.5 billion. Put another way, investors were paying around 7 times sales, based on 2022 revenue of $1.91 billion.

Then, in February 2023, Palantir posted its first quarter of positive GAAP net income, earning $31 million in the fourth quarter of 2022. Management also stated it expected GAAP net income for all of 2023.

Sources indicate that interestingly, the business didn't speed up in 2023. Revenue rose just 17% to $2.23 billion, slower than in either losing year. But net income swung to $210 million, from the $374 million loss in 2022.

Because the stock began the year at around 7 times sales, the improvement was arguably enough to power a 167% gain.

Industry observers note that on the business side, today's Palantir resembles neither year. Its year-over-year revenue growth rate has risen three straight quarters, from 70% in the fourth quarter of 2025 to 85%, 93%, and 96% during the first three quarters of 2026. Third-quarter revenue hit $2.31 billion.

In a recent development, even more, profits are soaring. Third-quarter net income was $1.13 billion, or 49% of revenue, over twice the $476 million Palantir made a year before.

It has been revealed that the price, though, looks more like the end of 2021, just higher. At around $160 a share, Palantir is worth about $385 billion. Measured against its revenue for the last four quarters, that's about 53 times sales.

NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

Industry observers note that it's more than double the sales multiple the stock carried into 2022 and more than seven times what it carried into 2023. Measured against earnings, shares trade at more than 110 times earnings, a price that already bakes in years of rapid growth.

True, growth like this can lower a valuation fast. When 2026 started, shares cost around 95 times Palantir's 2025 revenue, and that sales multiple has since dropped by over 40%, mainly because revenue rose. But Palantir itself expects some cooling. Its fourth-quarter forecast of around $2.65 billion implies year-over-year growth of about 88%.

What made 2023 work was a low starting price meeting an improving business. Palantir has the improving business now, but it doesn't have the low price. So I don't think a losing 2026 would set up a 2023-style rebound. Any gains from here would probably need to come slowly, as revenue and profits rise faster than the share price for a while.

Sources indicate that I'd still be comfortable holding a small stake at this price, as the business has never looked stronger. I'd just expect the returns to take some patience.

By Seena Hassouna – Updated Nov 22, 2026 at 1:40PM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Micron Technology ›.

The explosion of artificial intelligence has sparked a fierce race for high-performance memory. Deciding between Micron Technology (MU -13.89%) and Sandisk (SNDK -16.05%) means choosing between two giants powering the next era of computing infrastructure.

Micron provides a massive range of memory and storage solutions across several high-growth markets. Sandisk focuses its expertise on advanced flash storage technologies for everything from mobile phones to massive server farms. Investors are comparing these companies as they look to capitalize on the sustained demand for data storage and processing power.

Recent findings suggest that micron Technology specializes in creating semiconductor memory and storage products like DRAM, NAND, and NOR. These components are essential for smartphones, data centers, and automotive electronics. The firm operates 15 manufacturing sites and 21 design centers globally to meet this demand. The business relies heavily on its top 10 customers, which account for over 50% of revenue, and it primarily serves the data center market. Customer concentration like this adds a layer of risk to the business.

In the 12 months ended Sept. 3, 2026, revenue reached nearly $133.2 billion, representing a significant 256.3% increase over the prior period. This represents a massive jump from the $37.4 billion in revenue reported just one year earlier. Net income for this timeframe was approximately $85.0 billion. The rapid revenue growth is indicative of the broader expansion occurring among semiconductor stocks tied to modern computing.

Sources indicate that as of its September 2026 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio was 0.0x. This ratio measures total debt relative to shareholders' equity, and a value of zero suggests a very conservative use of borrowed funds. The current ratio, which measures the ability to pay short-term obligations with current assets, was roughly 3.3x. In the fiscal year ended Sept. 3, 2026, free cash flow totaled nearly $59.0 billion. Free cash flow is the cash a tech giant generates after accounting for cash outflows to support operations and maintain its capital assets.

Sources indicate that sandisk designs and produces advanced flash storage solutions for businesses and consumers. Its products are found in cloud infrastructure, AI systems, and connected edge devices like tablets and wearables. The firm employs over 10,000 people and maintains a presence in more than 30 countries. Unlike many rivals, no single customer accounted for more than 10% of its revenue in 2026. This indicates a more diversified base of buyers compared to some industry peers.

In the 12 months ended Oct. 2, 2026, revenue reached approximately $29.0 billion. This marked a 272.4% increase compared to the previous 12-month period. The company also reported net income of nearly $19.4 billion during this time. This jump in profitability represents a significant recovery from the net losses the company reported in the previous two fiscal years. This turn toward profitability highlights the strong market reception for its latest storage technologies.

According to its July 2026 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio was 0.0x. This level indicates the company at the moment does not rely on debt to fund its operations relative to its equity. The current ratio was close to 2.3x, showing a healthy ability to cover short-term financial obligations with its current assets. In the fiscal year ended July 3, 2026, free cash flow was nearly $11.5 billion. This cash generation provides the business with the flexibility to reinvest in its flash storage research and development.

Recent findings suggest that micron Technology faces significant risks from the inherent cyclicality of the memory market, where selling prices can fluctuate wildly. The company is also highly dependent on a small group of large data center customers. Intense competition from firms like Samsung and SK hynix (SKHY -13.11%) keeps pressure on innovation and pricing. Furthermore, trade restrictions involving China, as well as the CAC's restrictions on purchasing its products, could disrupt its global operations or limit its market access.

Recent findings suggest that sandisk relies heavily on strategic joint ventures, specifically with Flash Ventures and Kioxia, which can limit its ability to make independent operational decisions. The tech giant also faces intense competition, which can lead to lower average selling prices for flash memory. Forecasting the specific needs of AI infrastructure remains difficult, creating a risk of supply imbalances. Additionally, its recent separation from Western Digital (WDC -12.02%) introduces ongoing regulatory and compliance complexities.

Sandisk carries a lower multiple relative to future earnings estimates, while Micron looks more attractive based on its current relationship with trailing sales.

Valuation metrics include sourcing from Financial Modeling Prep (FMP) and may differ from other data providers.

The Forward P/E uses future earnings estimates to gauge value, while the P/S ratio measures market cap against sales over the past twelve months.

Both stocks need the same thing to go right: AI data center spending has to keep growing. Last week's AI sell-off, which dragged chip stocks lower and gave the S&P 500 its worst week in more than a year and a half, indicated how rapidly investors can doubt that. It hit Micron and Sandisk alike, so the drop tells you little about which business is better built.What separates them is how each handles a slowdown. Micron runs its own fabs, sells across DRAM, HBM and NAND, and holds far more cash than debt, so it can keep investing through a rough patch. Sandisk runs leaner and spends little on capital, but it sells only NAND and relies on one joint venture partner for its wafers.For a long-term investor, that points to Micron. Last week lowered the price you pay, but it didn't make memory any less cyclical, and drops like this can run further. Build a position in stages rather than all at once, and size it so another leg down wouldn't force you to sell. If your timeline is 2027 and beyond, the real test is whether you can hold through the swings, not whether you catch the bottom.

Latest Update: Chelsea’s feisty friendly ends in penalty shoot-out confusion

📅 09 Aug 2026 | ⏱️ 15 min read (3079 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~15 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Chelsea’s Far East tour ended in farce and confusion with players waiting around for a penalty shoot-out that never happened.
  • The chaos came at the end of a hard-earned, bad-tempered draw against Malaysian champions Johor Darul Ta’zim, with an own-goal in the 89th minute sparring the west London side’s blushes.
  • That goal also was supposed to set up penalties.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Chelsea’s Far East tour ended in farce and confusion with players waiting around for a penalty shoot-out that never happened.

The chaos came at the end of a hard-earned, bad-tempered draw against Malaysian champions Johor Darul Ta’zim, with an own-goal in the 89th minute sparring the west London side’s blushes.

That goal also was supposed to set up penalties. But after minutes of waiting around – and Kevin Campello, Chelsea’s head of first-team operations, saying “it’s written in the contract” – the players walked off the pitch.

That confusion ended a feisty affair in which tensions threatened to boil over and that, at certain points, paid little attention to the “friendly” aspect of the clash with seven yellow cards shown. At one point the visitors’ upcoming set-piece coach Austin MacPhee exchanged angry words with some of Johor’s coaching staff. The CFC TV commentary team suggested that the spot-kicks were abandoned because of the match’s heated atmosphere.

Austin MacPhee was ready to throw hands😂 pic.twitter.com/CFDgTOwmxE.

Having played just 24 hours earlier in Jakarta – a 3-0 win over AC Milan – it was no surprise to see Xabi Alonso name a fresh XI, a mixture of players who may well be offloaded before the end of the transfer window, those needing to prove themselves, and youngsters given much-needed game time.

And considering Johor are one game away from setting a upcoming world record of 109 matches unbeaten in the top flight – a run that would surpass the current mark set by Ivorian side Asec Mimosas in the early 1990s – it was also no shock to see the Malaysian team offer a stern, pre-season test for the west Londoners.

After a good start Chelsea were second best in a first half in which Johor should have been at least two goals to the good. The Malaysian champions controlled the first 45 minutes and were 1-0 up after 14 minutes – a low cross from the left side-footed home by Arif Aiman.

The hosts gave the young, inexperienced Chelsea backline a torrid time, especially on the flanks and Óscar Arribas was guilty of not capitalising on a great chance to double Johor’s lead, his shot after cutting in from the right going wide.

While they looked vulnerable at the back, Chelsea also struggled to keep possession in attack. But they got an equaliser they scarcely deserved after Liam Delap was manhandled to the ground in the box by Kevin Medina. The striker, who may well leave Stamford Bridge before the transfer window slams shut, fired home the spot-kick allowing the visitors to go into the break on level terms.

For the most part, the second half followed a similar pattern to the first – Jofor having the better chances, while tensions on the pitch continued to run high.

It was, however, Chelsea who took the lead after the break, Delap once again scoring from the spot, this time after Jamie Gittens was brought down in the area.

Johor, though, kept on creating, thanks in part to a fairly porous visitors’ backline, and levelled through a deflected Arribas free kick, before going 3-2 up thanks thanks to a well-taken Bérgson strike.

Recent findings suggest that had it stayed that way Chelsea could have had few complaints. But as the clock approached 90 minutes, the visitors had one last attack. Mykhailo Mudryk, just on as a substitute, delivered a cross from the left that Antonio Glauder could only steer into his own net. That was supposed to set up the penalty shoot-out that did not take place and the chance for one of the sides to claim a hollow victory.

In a recent development, considering a raft of changes and that fact this was far from the first XI, it is hard to know what to make of this. But among the positive things Alonso could take from the game was the impressive form of Nicolas Jackson and good centre-forward play of Delap. The negative was, however, a poor defensive display.

Chelsea return to Stamford Bridge on Saturday for their last pre-season friendly, against Real Sociedad, before the Premier League season starts away at local rivals Fulham on August 24.

According to recent reports, johor Darul Ta’zim: Syihan Hazmi; Arribas, Israfilov (Carlos Akapo 82), Medina, Antonio Glauder, Silva (La’Vere Corbin-Ong 89); Arif Aiman, Petrovic, Méndez (Nené 78), Marcos Guilherme (Bérgson); Zahedi (Stoichkov 62). Substitutes: Abad, Davies, Hidalgo, Nahuel Leiva, Lowry, Mohamadou Sumareh, Stuart Wilkin.Booked: Israfilov, Antonio Glauder, Silva.Goals: Arif Aiman (14), Arribas (65), Bérgson (86).Chelsea: Sharman-Lowe (Slolina 46); Subuloye, Adarabioyo, Anselmino (Watson 29); Geovany Quenda, Dario Essugo, Nicoll-Jazuli, Gittens (Mudryk 87); Estêvão, Delap, Jacskon (Satpaev 86). Substitutes: Curd, Diakite, Kavuma-McQueen, Sarr, Walsh.Booked: Estêvão, Delap, Jackson, Geovany Quenda, Watson.Goals: Delap (42 pen, 62 pen), Antonio Glauder (89 og).

There will NOT be a penalty shootout. No one is quite sure why.

Anyway, that was an entertaining draw, plenty of good things for Chelsea (the play of Delap and Jackson) as well as worrying signs (open and vulnerable at the back).

The commentators on CFC TV are now not so sure!

That was an entertaining pre-season friendly. There was a bit of niggle and that added to the action.

There will be penalties, apparently, if it stays the same score...

Industry observers note that will there be a late winner? There will be four minutes of added time.

Mudryk just on picks up the ball on the left and, with four Chelsea players in the box, crosses into the danger area. It’s a good ball and asks too many questions of the hosts as Glauder diverts the ball into his own net.

It’s been an entertaining match.

It’s what the host have, on the balance of play, deserved, but it’s a gift from Chelsea. Essugo loses the ball in the final third and Bergson, on as sub pick it put driving at the box before hitting a low shot from outside the area, the ball nestling in the left corner of the net.

Chelsea have been better this half than the first 45, they’ve been able to control the pace of the game well since the break.

The pace has slowed down since the break, Chelsea seeing more of the ball. They work it right before Watson loses possession on the edge of the area.

The referee clearly forgot about the hydration break and the two teams are having a belated one now. Delightful...

I reckon there’s another goal left in this match. It’s been entertaining fare and the hosts have given as good as they’ve got, if not more.

Recent findings suggest that this has been a lively match, better than most run-of-the-mill pre-season friendlies. Chelsea seeing a fair bit of possession at the moment, can they fashion a chance?

Yes they can. But it’s a longish shot from Gittens that is easily saved by Hamzi in the JDT goal.

More niggle in this match that hasn’t really had many tough challenges. After a few handbags the referee takes control and the argy bargy peters out.

Recent findings suggest that it’s the least the hosts deserve. They have a free-kick 25 yards out, Arribas takes it with his right it’s at the wall but in turning away from the ball Delap deflects it into the far-right corner giving Slonina no chance.

Fluky goal but the hosts have deserved their bit of luck.

Delap again with the goal, this time he goes low, but still to the keeper’s right.

Penalty for Chelsea. Gittens cuts back in the box onto his right and is clipped by the defender. Clear-cut penalty.

Half-chance for Delap on the edge of the area. He playes a one-two with Jackson before opening up his body and letting fly, the shot going well wide.

Sources indicate that another good chance for the hosts and it’s not shock to write that it’s come from the industry of Arribas on the right. He fires in a low cross that evades everyone in the box.

Estevao goes down in the box, it looks as though it could well be a penalty but the referee waves play on. The Brazilian is the shown a yellow card for possibly lashing out having not got the decision he wanted.

The hosts have asserted themselves well this half, in much the same way as they did in the first 45 minutes.

Recent findings suggest that another good chance for the hosts and again it’s all too easy as Zahedi is one-on-one with the keeper. The striker, however, dithers a bit too long and Slonina makes a fine save. JDT have had plenty of chances to add to their sole goal...

Chelsea have had a ragged start to this half.

Good work from JDT who keep the ball well in midfield before a throughball is played to the on-rushing Zahedi but Slonina comes out well.

They’re back under way in Johor, and there’s an early chance for Jackson who gets the ball in the box, but the ball gets stuck underneath him and he cannot get in a good attempt in on goal.

And that is the last action of an entertaining half. Chelsea started well before the hosts opened the scoring. JDT then took control of the half and should, if truth be told, have extended their lead. But Delap did well to earn the penalty that he subsequently scored and should have made it 2-1 with the last kick of the 45.

Worrying signs at the back, however, for Alonso. Will Chelsea go to four at the back after the break?

The answer to that question (see last post) was so very nearly yes...

Jackson plays in a peach of a through ball with the outside of his right foot, Delap is one-on-one with the keeper and looks for all the world as though he has to score. BUT he scuffs his shot wide.

There will be three minutes of added time. Can Chelsea head into the break with an unexpected lead?

Industry observers note that free-kick for Chelsea on the JDT byline. The ball is put deep into the box, it’s headed back by Tosin before the ball is blazed over the bar.

A minute later Tosin then let’s fly form 25 yards, the ball goes well over the bar.

The hosts should have been more than 1-0 to the good and now they’re drawing. Goals change matches...

Having won the penalty Delap fires the spotkick home, sending the keeper the the wrong way.

Penalty to Chelsea and it’s all thanks to good centre-forward play by Delap. He gets the ball in the box and Medina manhands him to the ground. The referee doesn’t hesitate before pointing to the spot.

In a recent development, chelsea have struggled to create anything since the opening 15 minutes. They have no control at the front and none at the back at the moment.

As I type that JDT have another good chance to turn the 1-0 lead into a 2-0 lead. Arribas, whose been a menace all game, dances toward the Chelsea box before delaying the pass too long.

JDT are finding a lot of joy on the flanks, there are three at the back for Chelsea and on the outside are two youngsters. The hosts are working the space well.

Recent findings suggest that yet again Chelsea are made to look decidedly average. A simple ball over the top on the right opens up the visitors’ defence and Arribas is in on goal, he cuts in and lets fly with his left peg, the shot going wide.

That should have been 2-0 to the Malaysian powerhouses.

Worrying signs for Chelsea who have struggled to keep possession up top and looked vulnerable at the back.

In a recent development, yet more good work from JDT who are being given space by Chelsea. Marcos Guilherme slaloms into the west Londoners’ box and Tosin again doesn’t look the most assured but the JDT player cuts the ball back and the visitors can clear the danger.

Another good attack from the hosts who get in a shot in on goal, it’s deflected and loops into the grateful arms of Sharman-Lowe in the Chelsea goal.

There’s a break in play with Anselmino down and suffering what looks like a hamstring injury. He is eventually replaced by Reggie Watson.

Meanwhile, the home fans are in fine voice and waving several HUGE flags.

Industry observers note that yep, everyone’s least favourite part of the World Cup in the U, S of A is back. To be fair it’s humid in Johor so taking on fluids during the first 45 minutes is no bad idea.

There’s a bit of argy-bargy not really what you should get in a ‘friendly’. There hasn’t been a bad chellenge in the match so far so not sure where that came from...

Yet more good work from the hosts, this time it’s down the right, Arribas getting the better of Anselmino before shooting at the near post - the attempt hitting the side netting.

After a lively start Chelsea have been second best.

Poor defending from the visitors there but the chance was well snapped up by JDT.

Industry observers note that lovely break from the hosts. They break down the left at pace, before the ball is threaded through to the back post and Arif Aiman sidefoots into the back of the net with aplomb.

So very nearly an opener for Chelsea. They break at pace thanks to Estevao who drives down the middle before playing in Jackson. The striker cuts in from the left and shoots, the attempt is saved well by Hamzi and Estevao’s follow up is wide. Is a goal coming?

In a recent development, free-kick for Chelsea some 35 yards out. Too far fro a shot on goal? Of course it is. The ball is floated into the box and the visitors earn a corner.

Industry observers note that what can they create from this set piece? ‘Not much’ is the initial answer as the ball is cleared by JDT but Chelsea win possession back and the ball is fed to Estevao on the left, the Brazilian goes for go with his trusty left peg but the bal goes high and wide.

JDT attack down the left, it’s a lovely ball in that forces a fine header to clear the danger from Adarabioyo.

No sooner had I sent that last post than Chelsea break through the middle. The ball is fed through to Delap who gets a left-footed shot in on goal forcing a good save from the JDT keeper Hamzi.

Quiet, low-key start to the match. No real shock there, it is a pre-season friendly.

JDT give the ball away in their half and Chelsea have a half-decent platform to launch an attack from. They cannot fashion a chance and also lose possession.

According to recent reports, they’re under way in southern Malaysia, Chelsea are in their vibrant blue and the hosts are wearing a fetching pink number. There was a late change for the visitors, Mamadou Sarr has been replaced by Olutayo Subuloye.

We’re moments away from kick-off.

CHELSEA XI TO FACE JOHOR: Sharman-Lowe; Sarr, Tosin, Anselmino; Quenda, Nicoll-Jazuli, Essugo (c), Gittens; Estevao; Jackson, Delap; subs: Slonina, Curd, Subuloye, Diakite, Watson, Mudryk, Walsh, Kavuma-McQueen, Satpayev.

According to recent reports, ...Luis Garcia. The Spaniard has history with Chelsea, remember the ‘ghost goal’?

Arriving for duty! 🫡 pic.twitter.com/M2XEkLC18n.

Your Chelsea side today! 🔵 pic.twitter.com/0OvvGVmgpc.

A mixture of players who may well be offloaded before the end of the transfer window, those needing to prove themselves, and youngsters you may not have heard of.

In a recent development, johor Darul Ta’Zim – more commonly known as JDT – are the Man Utd of Malaysia (at least that’s according to a Malaysian friend of mine). In 2013, they were going nowhere and were the dictionary definition of a stagnant club, low on confidence and trophies. That was until the Crown Prince bought the club and, over the next 13 years, transformed it into the powerhouse it is today.

As if to underline JDT’s dominance over Malaysian football they are one game away from the world record unbeaten run in a top flight. The newly introduced season of the Malaysian Super League gets under way later this month and should they avoid defeat in their opening match they will extend their unbeaten run - which began in April 2021 - to 109 games and surpass the world record set by Ivorian side Asec Mimosas in the early 1990s.

Industry observers note that chelsea’s pre-season tour of South East Asia ends today with a match against Johor Darul Ta’zim in Malaysia. The clash comes barely 24 hours after the west Londoners beat AC Milan 3-0 in Jakarta, a much-needed win coming on the back of defeats against Juventus and Tottenham.

A fine volley from Moises Caicedo and a double from João Pedro either side of half-time led Xabi Alonso’s side to victory in the Indonesian capital.

The game was fairly even in the first half and looked set to head into the break level at 0-0 but Pedro’s header from Caicedo’s corner put Chelsea in front.

Alonso’s side then doubled their advantage seconds into the second half as Pedro scored his second, assisted by Pedro Neto.

According to recent reports, just minutes later, Chelsea had their third courtesy of a well-worked corner routine. Romeo Lavia’s delivery was met by Caicedo on the volley, with the Ecuadorian’s finish with the outside of the boot finding the bottom corner.

Today, the west London side face Malaysian powerhouses Johor at the Sultan Ibrahim Stadium, more on them later, but considering the tight turnaround from yesterday’s match today’s clash will provide a stern test.

“The idea, with the game against Milan and then one in Johor, was to arrive at this weekend with players not being ready for 90 minutes until now,” Alonso explained after the win in Jakarta.

“We wanted to have a logical progression in their loads; so we had our strategy and we’ve stuck to that.

“We have another idea [against Johor]; that was decided yesterday [Friday]. The idea is that many young players were coming to have chances to play tomorrow. If not, we’d have been short, as playing two games in two days is quite intense. So we will need them.”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Brendan Coffey – Updated Nov 22, 2026 at 1:43PM EST.
  • 10 stocks we like better than Advance Auto Parts ›.
