📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Brendan Coffey – Updated Nov 22, 2026 at 1:43PM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Advance Auto Parts ›.

Choosing between essential automotive services and niche digital commerce is a central question for investors today. As you strategy for 2027, should you buy Advance Auto Parts (AAP -0.40%) or Etsy (ETSY -2.88%)?

According to recent reports, advance Auto Parts is a veteran of the brick-and-mortar retail world, providing parts and maintenance supplies to a massive network of mechanics and hobbyists. Etsy represents the modern creator economy, providing a specialized platform for handmade and vintage items. Both companies operate within the consumer discretionary space but face very different growth drivers and competitive landscapes.

According to recent reports, advance Auto Parts focuses on providing automotive components to a diverse customer base, including professional garages, service stations, and auto dealerships. These professional installers account for approximately 50% of the total sales recorded by the tech giant. It also supports do-it-yourself customers through thousands of retail stores and a growing digital mobile application that allows for convenient part identification and ordering.

In the 12 months ended Oct. 10, 2026, revenue reached about $8.6 billion, which was a decrease of approximately 0.3% from the previous period. Net income for this time frame was approximately $100 million. This performance comes as the company navigates shifts in consumer spending habits while attempting to maintain its market share in a highly competitive automotive maintenance industry.

Sources indicate that as of its January 2026 balance sheet, the manufacturer maintained a current ratio of roughly 1.7x, which indicates its ability to pay short-term debts with current assets. The debt-to-equity ratio was close to 2.4x, which compares total debt to shareholder equity. In the fiscal year ended Jan. 3, 2026, free cash flow was negative $298 million, representing the cash remaining after accounting for capital expenditures.

Industry observers note that etsy operates a global marketplace that connects millions of creative entrepreneurs with buyers looking for specialized, handmade, or vintage items. This focus makes it a standout choice among retail stocks as it avoids the inventory risks and physical overhead of traditional stores. The platform serves approximately 86.5 million active buyers and over 5.6 million active sellers worldwide.

Industry observers note that in the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, revenue reached abour $2.9 billion, representing growth of approximately 2.1%. Net income for the same period was approximately $987.5 million, reflecting a net margin of roughly 34.4%. This highlights the efficiency of its marketplace model, in which the company earns fees and service revenue without having to manufacture or ship physical products itself.

As of its December 2025 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio was approximately -2.8x, which means that total liabilities exceed shareholder equity. The current ratio stands at approximately 1.4x, which measures the tech giant's ability to meet its short-term financial obligations. In the fiscal year ended Dec. 31, 2025, free cash flow was approximately $638.8 million, though note that stock-based compensation represented roughly 35.3% of operating cash flow, which inflates reported cash generation.

In a recent development, advance Auto Parts faces intensive competition from national and regional chains like AutoZone (AZO -0.67%), as well as mass merchandisers and internet retailers like Amazon.com Inc. (AMZN -4.10%). The organization is heavily reliant on its information technology systems and must successfully adopt latest tools like artificial intelligence to remain efficient. Furthermore, its significant indebtedness could restrict its operational flexibility if the automotive market faces a downturn.

According to recent reports, etsy is highly dependent on discretionary consumer spending, which can be volatile depending on macroeconomic conditions like inflation or interest rates. The company competes with a wide range of online marketplaces, including eBay Inc. (EBAY -1.39%) and specialized platforms like Pinterest (PINS -3.32%). Maintaining traffic to its platform is also a risk, as Etsy relies on third-party search engines and social media sites for marketing and customer discovery.

Advance Auto Parts offers a lower Forward P/E based on future earnings estimates and a lower P/S ratio relative to sales over the past twelve months.

Valuation metrics include those sourced from Financial Modeling Prep (FMP) and may differ from those of other data providers.

Industry observers note that advance Auto Parts is in the midst of turning around the struggles it has experienced over the past few years around sales growth, margins, and market share. The aftermarket auto parts business has been in a slump, due largely to a mix of factors: weak do-it-yourselfer demand, vehicle electrification, intense competition, and general pocketbook pressures on consumers.

It has been revealed that manufacturer management has been addressing the business' problems by rolling out a upcoming multi-year turnaround program. That started in late 2024, including closing stores, optimizing store footprints, and overhauling its supply chain. To date, the program has produced mixed results. First-quarter fiscal 2026 results were much better than expected, with revenue of $2.6 billion and net income of $25 million. But the second quarter disappointed the street, and shares plunged as revenue fell short of consensus at $2 billion, even as net income and other metrics beat expectations. The most recently reported quarter, Q3, also slightly missed analyst expectations on sales and fell well short of projections on net income, with about $15 million profit.

Analysts see full-year 2026 sales slightly lower at $8.49 billion, with net income improving to near $115 million, well more than 2025's $44 million profit.

Turnaround stories like Advance Auto Parts are tempting to buy when they are dirt cheap, as its P/S ratio suggests it is.

Turning to Etsy, individual sellers on the platform are passionate about what they sell and are known for their attention to detail and high customer service. A tech giant with passionate users often has passionate shareholders, too. Metrics such as active buyers and growth in gross merchandise sales per active buyer are improving as the company benefits from personalization and AI initiatives. Etsy's capital-light model means it doesn't need to allocate significant capital to manufacturing facilities or inventory.

Still, top-line growth isn't very strong. The manufacturer is expected to see a slight $12 million rise in revenue this fiscal year to $2.895 billion. Yet that will come with about a 550% rise in net income to about $1.059 billion, a level that Wall Street analysts see as sustainable in the year ahead.

In a recent development, even though Etsy is pricier than Advance Auto Parts, its shares are still reasonably priced, with ratios that are about average for a high-profile stock. Advance Auto Parts is tempting, but for 2027, go with Etsy.

Walmart Has Raised Its Dividend 53 Straight Years. I'd Buy It Before December and Never Sell.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that walmart (WMT +1.51%) had a good morning on Thursday, Nov.
  • I've learned to love earnings days like this.
  • CEO John Furner summed up the quarter in one line: "The strength of our omnichannel model gives us room to do even more.".
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Micah Zimmerman – Nov 22, 2026 at 1:45PM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Walmart ›.

Industry observers note that walmart (WMT +1.51%) had a good morning on Thursday, Nov. 19. Sales and profit topped Wall Street's estimates, and the manufacturer raised its full-year forecast. Then the stock fell about 2% in early trading anyway.

I've learned to love earnings days like this. A dip on good news is often the cheapest way into a tech giant that has raised its dividend for 53 straight years. This move of 50 consecutive dividend raises places Walmart in the coveted Dividend King category. These are companies that have raised their payouts for 50 years or more.

NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

CEO John Furner summed up the quarter in one line: "The strength of our omnichannel model gives us room to do even more.".

What he means is that Walmart's stores are no longer just places you walk into to make a purchase. They have become launchpads for online orders, and more than a third of the orders filled from stores reached shoppers in under three hours. That speed is winning new kinds of customers, too, as Walmart noted its share gains were led by upper-income households.

In a recent development, CFO John David Rainey remarked the quarter also brought Walmart's biggest market share gains in food in three years. "We continue to gain share while continuing to improve the profitability of our digital businesses," he told CNBC.

Industry observers note that the part I find most exciting doesn't involve a shopping cart at all. Walmart's U.S. advertising business grew 37%, its membership fee revenue rose 17% worldwide, and sales on its online marketplace, where outside sellers pay to reach Walmart's shoppers, jumped 49%.

According to recent reports, brands pay to show up where millions of people shop, and members pay a yearly fee whether they buy a TV or a gallon of milk. That's how Walmart can keep cutting prices and still grow profit, and it's what makes the dividend feel so durable to me.

Then there's Sparky, Walmart's AI shopping assistant. Its U.S. usage has more than doubled from a year ago, and Furner said shoppers who use it build baskets about 40% bigger on average. Shopping may increasingly start with a question typed into an app instead of a walk down an aisle, and Walmart wants to be the one answering it.

It has been revealed that the newest piece is a $120-a-year bundle of Walmart+ and Sam's Club Plus. Furner told CNBC it has brought about 2 million latest people into Sam's Club since it launched in late October, and Rainey mentioned bundle members are "spending appreciably more." There's a catch, though: Walmart expects the bundle to weigh on Sam's Club profit growth until late 2027.

My reason is a practical one. Walmart's next dividend goes to shareholders of record on Dec. 11, so you need to own shares by the ex-dividend date. Walmart has also repurchased $7.8 billion of its own stock so far this fiscal year, so the dividend isn't the only way it returns cash. The holiday season is arriving, too, and Rainey mentioned he's "optimistic" about holiday spending, adding that the fourth quarter is "off to a pretty good start.".

According to recent reports, here's what gives me pause. Diesel prices are climbing. "The reality is that increases in diesel fuel and transportation, they do work their way into the cost of goods," Furner told CNBC, adding that "we'll keep prices as low as we can.".

Industry observers note that U.S. same-store sales growth also slowed to 2.9%, from 4.5% a year ago. Rainey said Walmart is keeping "flexibility" in its forecast, and the stock already trades at about 46 times earnings with a dividend yield under 1%. That's a rich P/E ratio for a store, and the yield won't make anyone rich promptly.

Sources indicate that so why never sell the stock? Walmart has turned its stores into delivery hubs, its shoppers into an ad audience, and its customers into paying members. Each of those makes the others stronger, and that's the kind of economic moat that tends to widen with age.

The 53-year streak is the result of a business that keeps finding newly introduced ways to earn its customers' trust, and today's report highlighted it's still doing exactly that.

#62282. Tech Report: Junk bonds are 'flashing yellow.' Watch these warning signs

📅 09 Oct 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1036 w)
📖 Baca
Gadgets ⚠️ Warning 🌐 CNBC ↗ Open Full Page

Tech Report: Junk bonds are 'flashing yellow.' Watch these warning signs

📅 09 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1036 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Cracks are forming in the junk bond market as investors demand higher payouts for owning the market's riskiest debt.
  • High-yield bonds now yield 8.1%, up from 7.22% a month ago.
  • The high-yield market is also showing stress on the credit side with spreads recently widening to levels not seen since April, according to the Federal Reserve Bank of St.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Cracks are forming in the junk bond market as investors demand higher payouts for owning the market's riskiest debt. It isn't time to ditch high-yield bonds, but investors should pay attention to the warning signs.

High-yield bonds now yield 8.1%, up from 7.22% a month ago. The increase reflects a jump in yields across the curve as investors bake in more inflation from high energy prices and other pressures, including concern about the deficit — hitting nearly $2 trillion in the fiscal year that ended Sept. 30.

The high-yield market is also showing stress on the credit side with spreads recently widening to levels not seen since April, according to the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis. Credit spreads are the difference in yield between the bonds and Treasurys of similar maturities. Wider spreads mean investors are demanding higher yields for holding corporate debt, viewing it as riskier.

In a recent development, spreads are at 315 basis points in the overall high-yield market, higher than a year ago but still below levels in March when they reached 346 bps. One basis point equals one one-hundredth of a percent, or 0.01%.

The high-yield market consists of bonds rated BB+ by S&P and Fitch and Ba1 and under by Moody's. The lowest-rated cohort, CCC and below, has seen the most movement with spreads climbing dramatically over the past year to roughly 1,250 bps.

Right now, the high-yield market is "flashing yellow" but is "far from red," noted Michael Arone, chief investment strategist at State Street Investment Management.

It makes sense that investors are demanding more compensation for taking on additional credit risk as borrowing costs rise, he mentioned.

Yields are elevated across the board with the 10-year Treasury reaching its highest level since 2002 earlier in the week.

"The bigger question is whether this is simply a repricing of interest rate risk, or the beginning of a more fundamental reassessment of credit quality," Arone said.

He's in a wait-and-see mode since earnings are still growing, interest-coverage ratios remain good, and while default rates have ticked up some, he believes it is not concerning.

That said, the starting point in spreads is likely weighing on investors' psyche, since they are still low by historical standards.

Sources indicate that "There's a small margin of error here, which I also think raises the anxiety level," Arone explained. "The compensation that investors are receiving for taking on this credit risk isn't overwhelming relative to history, and therefore subtle changes in credit spreads can be concerning.".

While there may be concerns about part of the lower-rated market, the overall high-yield market is in good fundamental shape.

In fact, credit quality is at a record high, with BB bonds making up over 60% of the market compared with 38% prior to the global financial crisis, remarked Kelley Gerrity, a fixed income strategist at Morgan Stanley Investment Management.

It has been revealed that "We've had higher-quality companies coming in, and with higher rates now, you also have more discipline from companies that are more indebted ... just because of the higher cost of capital, so that actually is creating a bit of a healthier picture as well," she said.

According to recent reports, the lowest tier of high yield has always been more speculative, since the bonds have a higher default risk. Therefore, it's no surprise that they are the ones seeing the most widening in spreads, said Collin Martin, head of fixed income research and strategy at the Schwab Center for Financial Research.

It has been revealed that the overall move in high-yield spreads have been "orderly," he remarked. "Are there cracks forming? I think the cracks are logical cracks with the lowest-rated bonds and it's too early to say that it's spreading to the broad credit market.".

It has been revealed that in addition, fluctuations within the CCC-rated and lower spreads have been idiosyncratic, Gerrity added. Morgan Stanley recently broke down the spreads in the lowest cohort into two buckets: performing assets and non-performing assets, which are defined as spreads above 1,000 bps.

The non-performing spread to worst is 2,818 bps, while the performing bucket — the biggest piece of the CCC market — is 461 bps, she stated.

"It is isolated," she said. "I'm not necessarily sure that that will go away anytime soon, but it doesn't tell the story of overall concern and flashing caution for credit markets right now.".

For now, investors should remain selective within higher yield, Gerrity advised.

"We're looking for the best relative value opportunities, and we think that exists within that single-B cohort, and so we're leaning into that," she remarked.

Investors should be concerned if there is a steep widening in the broader high-yield market.

It has been revealed that but there's scant evidence of stress in the BB cohort. Spreads in that group are at 194 bps, up from 179 bps a year ago — although the move hasn't been in a straight line.

According to recent reports, "We're going to be focusing our attention on what are considered some stronger businesses," Martin noted. "If we start to see the markets demand higher spreads there also, that's what we'll be looking at to see if risks are really rising.".

It's also important to understand that the Federal Reserve is raising rates in a strong economic environment, mentioned R.J. Gallo, chief investment officer of global fixed income at Federated Hermes. The central bank is concerned about an inflation problem amid high fossil fuel prices due to the Iran war, while growth has been stronger than expected, he noted.

"With growth being good as the reason that the Fed is hiking, then you wouldn't expect high yield to blow out because growth means revenues stay up, means cash flow and profitability stays up," he explained.

High yield becomes a disaster when the economy is heading into a sharp economic downturn, Gallo said.

Recent findings suggest that "That's when spreads really widen out," he said. "But a recession is not the odds-on bet. Now, talk to me in six months if the Fed keeps hiking over and over, if oil prices stay high for longer, well, then maybe we will start to wonder.".

#62281. Industry News: Here's the Average Social Security Benefit in Your 60s vs. Your 70s

📅 22 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (648 w)

Industry News: Here's the Average Social Security Benefit in Your 60s vs. Your 70s

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (648 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Kailey Hagen, CFP® – Nov 22, 2026 at 2:00PM EST.
  • Most people view Social Security as a single choice made on a single birthday.
  • According to the Social Security Administration (SSA), the average benefit for retirees aged 62 to 69 was $1,877.82 per month as of December 2025, the most recent data available.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Kailey Hagen, CFP® – Nov 22, 2026 at 2:00PM EST.

Most people view Social Security as a single choice made on a single birthday. Looking at the benefits through a decade-long lens tells a more complete story about how timing and earnings history shape retirement income.

According to the Social Security Administration (SSA), the average benefit for retirees aged 62 to 69 was $1,877.82 per month as of December 2025, the most recent data available. By the time you reach the 70-to-79 age band, that average climbs to $2,194.02.

Industry observers note that this creates a monthly gap of $316.20 between the two decades. Over a full year, that difference adds up to about $3,794.40. These figures represent broad population snapshots rather than what any one person's check will do as they get older.

Industry observers note that the higher average in the 70s band likely reflects who's in that group. The 70-to-79 decade tends to include more workers who waited longer to claim. They earned delayed retirement credits, which increase your benefit by 8% for every year you wait past full retirement age (FRA).

Sources indicate that full retirement age ranges from 66 to 67, depending on your birth year, and it's 67 for everyone born in 1960 or later. If your FRA is 67, waiting until age 70 can increase your monthly check by 24% compared to your baseline amount. A worker with an FRA of 66 can earn up to a 32% increase by waiting until 70.

Conversely, the 60s band likely has more early claimers. If you claim at the earliest age of 62 and your FRA is 67, your benefit faces a permanent 30% reduction. For those with an FRA of 66, the maximum reduction at 62 is 25%.

In a recent development, the SSA calculates your benefit based on an inflation-adjusted average of your 35 highest-earning years. This system is designed to replace about 40% of your pre-retirement income. That share is well short of what most retirees need to cover their costs, so they rely on savings or other income sources.

A 3.6% cost-of-living adjustment (COLA) will take effect in 2027. These figures don't yet reflect that raise, but it will add about $51 per month to the age-62 average and $82 per month for 70-year-olds. These adjustments are designed to help checks keep pace with inflation.

Sources indicate that contrary to what some believe, when you claim Social Security, you're typically locking in your benefit amount at that rate, apart from annual COLAs. Your future checks usually will not increase otherwise, though there are a couple of exceptions.

It has been revealed that if you've lost money to the earnings test in years past, you will get a one-time benefit boost at your FRA to make up for the benefits you lost before. The size of the increase will depend upon how much you'd had withheld in years past.

Industry observers note that seniors who continue to work may also see their benefits tick upward slightly over time if their current income is higher than in years past. This reflects your changing average monthly income used to calculate your benefits.

That said, these changes are unlikely to be life-changing for most seniors. It's better to choose your claiming age carefully based on your finances and life expectancy rather than hoping your checks will grow later.

For more on how Social Security affects your retirement, see this guide.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Matt DiLallo – Nov 22, 2026 at 2:02PM EST.

10 stocks we like better than Broadcom ›.

Broadcom (AVGO -12.19%) has become one of the biggest winners of the artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure boom. Demand for its custom AI chips and networking gear is surging as tech giants pour billions of dollars into data centers. Last quarter, its AI semiconductor revenue rocketed 221% to $16.7 billion, and management expects that business to double in fiscal 2027 and again in fiscal 2028.

The stock, however, already prices in a lot of that success. While it currently trades about 30% below its 52-week high, it's still up nearly 250% over the past three years. Here's a look at what a $1,000 investment in Broadcom could be worth by 2035.

Sources indicate that broadcom's fiscal 2026 third quarter was its best yet. Total revenue rose 86% to $29.6 billion, and AI semiconductor revenue climbed 221% to $16.7 billion. For the fourth quarter, the manufacturer guided to $21.7 billion in AI revenue, up 236%. Management has also laid out a path to roughly $58 billion of AI semiconductor revenue in fiscal 2026, $115 billion in fiscal 2027, and $230 billion in fiscal 2028. Custom accelerators for customers such as Anthropic and OpenAI drive that growth, along with the Ethernet switching and optical connections that link those chips together.

Industry observers note that broadcom isn't just an AI chip story. Its infrastructure software business, anchored by VMware, recorded nearly $8.8 billion in revenue last quarter, up 29%. That high-margin business generates growing recurring revenue for the company.

NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

Investor expectations are as massive as the AI opportunity. So are the risks. Broadcom depends on a small group of AI infrastructure customers, so a spending pullback by even one could hurt. AI spending could also cool once the current build-out peaks, and some customers may struggle to finance or monetize their data centers. Worries about AI financing and customer concentration have already driven a sell-off in chip stocks.

Margins are another watch item. As lower-margin custom accelerators account for a larger share of sales, margins could shrink. Competition from rivals and in-house chip designs also adds margin risk.

The question isn't whether AI infrastructure spending will grow over time. It's whether Broadcom can deliver the profits that investors already assume.

According to recent reports, broadcom recently traded around $325 per share. Analysts expect about $19.39 in adjusted earnings per share (EPS) for fiscal 2027, which puts the stock at roughly 17 times that estimate. Wall Street is bullish: none of the 50 analysts covering the tech giant rate it a sell, and the average price target is over $525 a share. That estimate already assumes more than 60% upside from the recent price.

To cover all the bases, I modeled three scenarios to 2035:.

Here's what a $1,000 investment in Broadcom stock would be worth in 2035 under those scenarios:.

Industry observers note that all three scenarios include estimated cash dividends, without reinvestment, and assume a purchase at today's price. The base case is conservative next to management's own goal: CEO Hock Tan has said Broadcom is on target to exceed $30 of EPS in fiscal 2028, while my base case implies about $21 that year. However, even in a conservative base case, Broadcom could deliver a nearly 150% return. Meanwhile, the bull case is even stronger.

Broadcom has a compelling opportunity in custom AI chips and networking, and its software business adds another source of profitable growth. Under my base case, a $1,000 investment in the semiconductor stock could grow to about $2,500 by 2035, a nearly 11% annualized total return. That's an attractive return, and it doesn't require Broadcom to sustain its extraordinary near-term growth indefinitely. While the outcome depends on the manufacturer meeting very ambitious earnings expectations, Broadcom looks like a compelling AI stock to buy right now.

Health insurer UnitedHealth delivered better-than-expected results for the third quarter of 2026. The tech giant also raised its full-year earnings outlook, reflecting continued progress on its turnaround blueprint.

Following the Q3 print, Morgan Stanley analyst Erin Wright reiterated a buy rating on UNH stock with a price target of $529. "UNH's beat & raise reinforces turnaround momentum, with improving MA [Medicare Advantage]/Optum Health supporting a higher '26 EPS baseline & upside to '27 consensus," stated Wright.

The five-star analyst added that better-than-expected performance in the UnitedHealthcare and Optum Health businesses supported another upgrade to the tech giant's 2026 adjusted earnings per share outlook to at least $20.50. Wright noted that UNH raised the earnings guidance despite incremental investments planned for the fourth quarter of 2026.

Furthermore, Wright highlighted management's view that the consensus 2027 EPS of $22.63 was too conservative. Reaching even the low end of the organization's 13% to 16% long-term EPS growth target would imply an EPS of $23.17.

Recent findings suggest that wright raised her 2026 EPS estimate to $20.65 from $19.82 and 2027 EPS to $23.24 from $22.54, reflecting the latest upside and an improving 2026 medical loss ratio to 87.4% from 88.1%. Overall, she believes that UNH's operational performance continues to improve, increasing her confidence in its UHC strategy and Optum Health turnaround execution.

Wright ranks No. 264 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. Her ratings have been successful 64% of the time, delivering an average return of 15%. See UnitedHealth Ownership Structure on TipRanks.

It has been revealed that social media giant Meta Platforms has been making headlines since the launch of its Muse AI agent, which is seeing solid traction. Investors look forward to updates on the company's AI strategy when it unveils its third-quarter results on Oct. 21.

Heading into Q3 earnings, Guggenheim analyst Michael Morris maintained a buy rating on Meta stock and increased his price target to $850 from $700, reflecting higher estimates for 2027. He expects Muse usage momentum and engagement levels to shape investor sentiment into the Q3 earnings call.

Recent findings suggest that specifically, Morris highlighted that, according to Apptopia, Muse reached 1.3 million daily active consumers in five weeks versus 300,000 in the first week. Given that Muse's current adoption represents less than 0.05% of Meta's 3.6 billion daily active user base, the analyst expects management to prioritize boosting usage over near-term monetization.

Recent findings suggest that "Over time, we believe Muse monetizes primarily through businesses paying to reach consumers through their agents, consistent with the economics of Meta's core advertising business, rather than consumer wallets," said the five-star analyst. He added that the checkout integrations with Shopify and PayPal reflect this framework.

While there are concerns that a rival could overtake Muse or the recently debuted Muse Wonder and push Meta into a prolonged cycle of overinvestment, Morris remains bullish due to the firm's strong record in scaling WhatsApp and competing strongly with TikTok via Reels as well as free distribution to an extensive user base.

Industry observers note that morris ranks No. 629 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been successful 57% of the time, delivering an average return of 13.2%. See Meta Platforms KPIs on TipRanks.

Next is semiconductor company Marvell Technology. Earlier this month, Marvell held its Investor Day, where it raised its total addressable market estimate to $400 billion by 2030, reflecting solid AI-led demand tailwinds.

After hosting a non-deal roadshow with Marvell's senior management following the Investor Day, Stifel analyst Tore Svanberg reiterated a buy rating on the stock with a price target of $370.

According to recent reports, the five-star analyst said that a major focus of the roadshow was the XPU and XPU Attach mix, as Marvell's Custom business expands toward its FY31 revenue target of $30 billion. In this regard, management reiterated that it expects a balanced mix of XPU and XPU Attach revenue in FY31, though it noted that either segment could grow rapidly enough to shift the mix toward 60/40 or 40/60.

While XPU drove most of the nearly $1.5 billion Custom revenue in FY26, Svanberg expects Marvell's XPU Attach business to grow substantially through the end of the decade, leading to a more balanced mix in this business. At the Investor Day event, the manufacturer raised its FY29 Custom target from more than $10 billion to over $12 billion, mainly driven by strength in the XPU Attach business.

Sources indicate that svanberg stated that another key topic in the roadshow was whether Marvell can secure enough capacity to meet its raised targets. Management said that it met with suppliers ahead of Investor Day to share its five-year goals and received commitments to support these targets. The analyst believes that Marvell's supply chain commitments give it a competitive edge over rivals as customers seek reliable partners for large-scale infrastructure buildouts.

In a recent development, in an earnings preview note on U.S. oil majors, Goldman Sachs analyst Neil Mehta reiterated a buy rating on Chevron with a price target of $241. Recent findings suggest that specifically, Mehta highlighted management's commentary on solid execution in Venezuela, with gross production expected to more than double to nearly 600 kbd (kilo barrels per day) by 2031 via three joint ventures. He also noted a recent oil and gas condensate discovery in offshore Angola and is awaiting commercial updates on the West Qurna 2 and Nasiriyah projects in Iraq.

Furthermore, Mehta expects CVX to report improved productivity and capital efficiency across domestic shale assets. He expects the improvement mainly in the Permian Basin, where Chevron projects advanced chemical treatments to drive about a 10% recovery uplift in new wells and bring down capital spend per barrel by about 25% year-over-year. Overall, Mehta expects Chevron to report Q3 2026 EPS of $4.95, above the consensus of $4.89.

Sources indicate that "While unfavorable timing effects and volatile commodity prices may present quarterly earnings headwinds, we highlight healthy U.S. refining margins and strong asset utilization as partial offsets," stated Mehta.

Industry observers note that mehta ranks No. 381 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 63% of the time, delivering an average return of 12%. See Chevron KPIs on TipRanks.

Recent findings suggest that kinetik Holdings (KNTK) is a fully integrated, pure-play, midstream company operating in the Delaware Basin. Earlier this month, the company declared a dividend of $0.81 per share, payable on October 30, 2026. With an annualized dividend of $3.24 per share, KNTK offers a yield of 5.82%. Kinetik will announce its Q3 earnings on November 4, with a conference call scheduled the next day.

Ahead of Q3 2026 earnings, Goldman Sachs analyst John Mackay reiterated a buy rating on Kinetik stock and slightly raised his price target to $58 from $57. In a recent development, 10 stocks we like better than Lululemon Athletica Inc. ›.

It has been revealed that choosing between a premium apparel leader and a global fast-food titan requires weighing growth potential against steady income. Is lululemon athletica (LULU -2.76%) or McDonald's (MCD +0.33%) the better pick for 2027?

According to recent reports, lululemon athletica focuses on high-end technical gear for active lifestyles, leveraging deep brand loyalty to maintain premium pricing. McDonald's operates a massive real estate and franchising empire, providing consistent cash flow through essential dining. Both companies are titans of the consumer landscape, but they offer vastly different paths for retail investors.

It has been revealed that lululemon athletica sells footwear and accessories alongside its signature yoga and running gear to a loyal customer base. It reaches these guests through more than 800 company-operated stores and a robust e-commerce platform that drives significant engagement. These physical locations often serve as community hubs that offer fitness events to build brand equity and reach more consumers in the apparel stocks category.

In the 12 months ended Aug. 2, 2026, revenue reached nearly $11.1 billion, representing an increase of approximately 1.7% from the prior twelve-month period. Net income for this timeframe was close to $1.4 billion. This growth rate represents a normalization after the rapid expansion seen in previous years as the firm focuses on international markets and men's apparel.

According to recent reports, as of its February 2026 balance sheet, the company maintained a healthy debt-to-equity ratio of roughly 0.4x. The current ratio, which measures short-term assets against liabilities, was approximately 2.3x. In the fiscal year ended Feb. 1, 2026, free cash flow reached nearly $921.7 million, which is the cash left over after paying for operations and capital investments.

McDonald's operates as a global leader in the restaurant industry with a network of over 45,000 locations. Its highly successful franchise model allows the tech giant to collect consistent royalties and rent while shifting most operating costs to independent owners. It also leverages delivery partnerships with platforms like Uber to ensure its products remain accessible to a broad consumer base in over 100 countries.

Sources indicate that in the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, revenue reached approximately $27.8 billion, representing growth of close to 5.8% compared to the prior twelve-month period. Net income during this same timeframe was nearly $9.0 billion. These strong figures highlight the resilience of a business that can effectively raise prices to manage inflationary pressures while maintaining high transaction volumes.

Recent findings suggest that as of its December 2025 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio was roughly -30.6x, indicating that total liabilities exceed shareholder equity. The current ratio, which measures the ability to cover short-term debts, was approximately 1.0x. In the fiscal year ended Dec. 31, 2025, free cash flow was close to $7.2 billion, providing ample capital for dividends and share repurchases.

Industry observers note that lululemon athletica faces intense competition from established athletic brands and potential supply chain disruptions due to its manufacturing concentration in Asia. The firm must also manage the risks of a leadership transition following the departure of its CEO. Brand reputation remains a key vulnerability, as negative publicity or product defects could impact consumer loyalty in the premium segment.

According to recent reports, mcDonald's depends on the financial success of its franchisees and faces stiff competition in the global informal dining market. Operational risks include food safety concerns and commodity price volatility that can impact restaurant profitability. The manufacturer also must invest heavily to protect its digital systems against data security and cybersecurity threats that target its ordering platforms.

Lululemon athletica looks considerably cheaper than McDonald's when comparing their Forward P/E and P/S ratio, which measures market value against sales over the past twelve months.

Valuation metrics include sourcing from Financial Modeling Prep (FMP) and may differ from other data providers.

I'd go with McDonald's. It has built one of the world's best-known restaurant brands, and its franchise model turns that scale into steady cash for shareholders. About 95% of its restaurants are run by franchisees who pay McDonald's rent and royalties, and it has raised its dividend for 50 straight years.

Sources indicate that what I like is how it keeps competing on value. Sales are still growing around the world, and in the U.S., where fewer customers had been walking in, sales turned positive in September after McDonald's pushed harder on value.

It has been revealed that to give lululemon its due, it has a premium brand and a latest CEO working on a turnaround. But sales are shrinking, with North American shoppers buying less at existing stores, and the firm cut its full-year outlook in its latest report.

McDonald's, by contrast, keeps paying shareholders steadily while it grows. For long-term investors, that mix of a trusted brand, steady cash, and a rising dividend makes McDonald's the better buy for 2027.

10 stocks we like better than Alibaba Group ›.

Industry observers note that investors looking for international growth often weigh the dominance of a Chinese tech leader against a global travel giant. Choosing between Alibaba Group (BABA -2.68%) and Booking Holdings (BKNG -1.64%) requires balancing valuation and regional risks.

Alibaba operates a massive ecosystem of e-commerce and cloud services, leveraging its scale in the world's second-largest economy. Booking dominates the online travel industry by connecting millions of travelers with accommodations and services worldwide. While both companies benefit from digital transformation, they face distinct competitive and regulatory landscapes that will shape their paths toward 2027.

Alibaba focuses its strategy on the intersection of artificial intelligence and cloud computing alongside its core consumption platforms. The company serves a vast merchant and consumer base through segments including China e-commerce, international digital commerce, and cloud intelligence. A key part of its strategy involves deepening customer loyalty, with its 88VIP membership base growing to approximately 64 million as of August 2026.

In the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, revenue reached about $160.3 billion, representing growth of approximately 5.5% compared to the prior year. The firm reported net income of roughly $17.6 billion during this same time frame. This growth reflects steady performance in its core commerce operations while it continues to invest in emerging cloud and international initiatives to capture long-term demand. (Alibaba reports in Chinese yuan. Figures have been converted to dollars at the exchange rate around the publication date.).

As of its March 2026 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio was approximately 0.2x, suggesting the company uses a conservative amount of borrowed money relative to its own capital. The current ratio, which measures the ability to pay short-term debts with short-term assets, stood at nearly 1.3x. In the fiscal year ended March 31, 2026, free cash flow was nearly negative $7.6 billion, meaning capital expenditures for the year exceeded the cash generated from operations.

One of the most prominent names among travel and tourism stocks, Booking provides online travel services through brands like Booking.com, Priceline, and Agoda. The tech giant operates a global partner division that maintains commercial relationships with airlines, hotels, and rental car companies across 220 countries. Its primary strategy involves providing a seamless travel experience while leveraging massive consumer traffic derived from search engines and mobile app marketplaces.

Industry observers note that for the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, revenue grew by roughly 8% to reach about $28.1 billion. Net income for the period was approximately $7.2 billion, reflecting the high net margin associated with its asset-light business model. This performance demonstrates the company's ability to capture resilient global travel demand even as it navigates a competitive landscape filled with diverse service providers.

Based on its December 2025 balance sheet, the company had a debt-to-equity ratio of nearly -3.5x. This negative value indicates that total liabilities exceed shareholder equity, a situation that often occurs in companies with significant share repurchases or specific financial structures. The current ratio was approximately 1.3x, while free cash flow reached about $9.1 billion in the fiscal year ended Dec. 31, 2025.

Alibaba faces intense competition from established domestic rivals and emerging low-cost platforms that are challenging its market share in China. The tech giant also operates in a complex regulatory environment that can shift rapidly, potentially affecting its cloud and financial technology interests. Geopolitical tensions may further complicate international expansion efforts and investor sentiment regarding its primary listing as it seeks to grow its global footprint.

It has been revealed that booking faces intense competition from global technology companies and travel providers like Airbnb (ABNB -1.41%) that use artificial intelligence to reach customers directly. The organization is highly dependent on Alphabet Inc. (GOOG -2.59%) for traffic, where changes to search algorithms or new AI features could increase the cost of acquiring customers. Regulatory compliance is also a major risk, particularly with European Union laws that impose operational restrictions and potential penalties on large digital platforms like those operated by Apple Inc. (AAPL -1.90%).

Alibaba trades at a lower valuation than Booking across both sales and future earnings estimates, though it carries different regional and regulatory risks.

Valuation metrics include those sourced from Financial Modeling Prep (FMP) and may differ from those of other data providers.

The P/S ratio measures the stock price against sales over the past twelve months. The Forward P/E ratio compares the current stock price to future earnings estimates for the coming year, helping investors understand how much they are paying for every dollar of projected profit.

Booking Holdings is successfully shifting from an agency model to a primarily merchant model. That means it used to make its money as an agent--connecting travelers to a hotel and collecting a commission while the hotel manages collecting payment from the traveler. In the merchant model, Booking buys capacity from hotels and other providers on its platform and collects payment directly from the traveler. This tends to lead to fatter margins.

In a recent development, the company is also in excellent financial shape. It has $16 billion in cash, which makes its balance sheet investment grade. Another plus for shareholders is the company's $20 billion share buyback program. The brand is increasingly a destination for travelers, which means it is paying less to companies like Google for search engine visibility. Today, two-thirds of Booking.com's visitors are organic, meaning they are direct visitors rather than from paid ad traffic.

According to recent reports, revenue will grow about 9% this year to $29.3 billion. And net income takes a healthier 50% leap to about $8.1 billion.

Alibaba focuses on defending its cash-rich China e-commerce marketplaces, Taobao and Tmall, while funneling capital into higher-growth AI cloud and AI services. Alibaba is the public cloud leader in China and the owner of the Qwen open- and closed-source models. Yet its retail businesses are losing market share to Chinese rivals, which crimps the business's ability to fund money-losing AI model efforts. That means its AI cloud and compute services are the one impressive growth center for the business. It grew 45% year over year in that sector. One metric in its favor is that Alibaba's current valuation is attractive relative to U.S. cloud and AI peers.

Alibaba is forecast to continue growing, but some on the Street are skeptical of the firm's ability to win in the hyper-competitive Chinese market and to expand its fast-growing AI services business beyond the China-dominated region, especially given the capital investment needed for AI.

BABA looks like a value play, but Booking is also priced below the average S&P 500 stock (which trades at a forward P/E of about 19x). And Booking's valuation is well below travel rival Airbnb. Yet the company has robust total sales and good growth, expanding margins, and a pile of cash. It's too good a bargain to pass up at these prices. For 2027, go with Booking Holdings.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Robinhood shares were down around 8% in pre-market trading on Wednesday as investors digested weaker-than-expected third-quarter earnings despite growth in options trading and prediction markets.

Here's how the brokerage performed in its quarter ended Sept. 30, compared with Wall Street estimates, based on a survey of analysts by LSEG:.

Sources indicate that robinhood's net income fell to $468 million, or 51 cents per share, from $556 million, or 61 cents per share, a year ago. Revenue represented a 12% increase from $1.27 billion in the same quarter last year.

Despite that gain, transaction-based revenue of $867 million came in below Wall Street estimates from StreetAccount of $879 million, putting focus on whether Robinhood can sustain momentum across its trading businesses and reduce its reliance on volatile market activity.

Robinhood has been diversifying its business as it tries to expand its brokerage app into a broader financial services platform. Options trading and event contracts have become increasingly vital sources of transaction revenue, while the tech giant has continued to invest in wealth management, subscriptions and other offerings.

It has been revealed that transaction-based revenue grew 19% from the same period last year to $867 million, driven primarily by a more than 500% increase in event contracts revenue. Additionally, options revenue grew 31% to $399 million and equities revenue rose 41% to $121 million.

Those gains were partially offset by cryptocurrency revenue, which fell 55% to $120 million.

Chief Financial Officer Shiv Verma told CNBC event contracts on crypto movements did well in the quarter, offering investors another way to express a view on crypto despite the slump in prices and spot trading.

Sources indicate that net deposits on the Robinhood platform totaled $15.7 billion for the quarter, equal to a 17% annualized growth rate based on total platform assets at the end of Q2 2026. Over the past year, net deposits totaled $71 billion, representing 21% growth compared with total platform assets at the end of Q3 2025.

—With reporting from CNBC's Robert Hum and Kate Rooney.

10 stocks we like better than Coca-Cola ›.

That group includes Brown-Forman (BFB -0.66%) (BFA -0.74%), Coca-Cola (KO +0.94%), Hormel Foods (HRL +2.08%), J.M. Smucker (SJM +1.82%), PepsiCo (PEP +1.11%), and Sysco (SYY +1.32%).

Recent findings suggest that these six beverage and snack stocks serve steady diets of delectable dividends. Image source: Getty Images.

For equity income investors, that's an extensive list from which to choose, and it's reasonable to ponder what these companies have in common besides residence in the consumer staples sector and the food and beverage industry.

The answer is easy and important for dividend seekers: All six are at minimum Dividend Aristocrats®, members of the S&P 500 that have raised payouts for at least 25 consecutive years. (Dividend Aristocrats® is a registered trademark of Standard & Poor's Financial Services LLC.).

Let's examine each one from a dividend perspective.

It has been revealed that typically, the minimum age to open a U.S. brokerage account is 18, though some firms allow 13- to 17-year-olds to open an account with a parent or guardian. This means that younger investors can buy shares of Brown-Forman before they can legally enjoy the company's products, including Jack Daniel's and Woodford Reserve, among other well-known liquor brands.

In a recent development, the company, which also makes Chambord liqueur and Diplomático rum, yields 3%, or nearly triple the S&P 500's dividend, and is on a 42-year run of consecutive annual dividend raises. If recent history is an accurate predictor, November could be the month in which Brown-Forman makes it 43 straight years of boosted payouts, so that's something to keep an eye on over the near term.

In a recent development, something else long-term investors should monitor with Brown-Forman and related stocks is alcohol consumption trends among Gen Zers and millennials. Younger people are consuming slightly less alcohol today than they did during the worst part of the pandemic.

On the more positive side of the ledger for Brown-Forman is evidence suggesting that those consumers are being more selective when they do drink, indicating they are looking to trade up to premium brands, including some from the Brown-Forman stable.

It has been revealed that with payout increase streaks of 65 years and 55 years, respectively, soft drink giants Coca-Cola and PepsiCo are Dividend Kings -- companies that have raised dividends in at least 50 straight years. Yet, while the two share dividend growth, industry, and sector, these stocks' trajectories differ significantly. For the decade ended Nov. 13, Coke returned about 230% while PepsiCo gained 92%.

NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

It has been revealed that this year, Coca-Cola, though a little frothy on valuation, is regularly printing newly introduced all-time highs while beating Pepsi stock by roughly 10 to 1. The latter is being pinched on multiple fronts, including tepid performance in the key North American market and sluggishness in its salty snacks division , a segment to which Coke is less exposed.

It has been revealed that both of these dividends are widely considered safe, but if "safe" is how investors want to play it, Coca-Cola has obvious momentum on its side. At the same time, PepsiCo is a "show me" story that may, in the near term, lack the clarity some market participants demand.

As noted above, there are concerns about the strength of PepsiCo's snacks unit, but those worries aren't uniform across the staples sector.

According to recent reports, just look at J.M. Smucker. In a sign that the fretting about weight-loss drugs hurting snack consumption may be misplaced, shares of this dividend growth star that is the maker of Twinkies are up 41% year to date. That's stellar among packaged-food stocks, and of note to prospective investors is that Smucker raised its full-year earnings guidance in August, saying it's having some success in passing higher costs on to consumers.

Sources indicate that hormel is a different story. While the manufacturer's Spam product found its way into post-Election Day discourse, shares of this Dividend King are slightly in the red this year. But there is hope for the maker of Pepperoni Bites and Planters nuts.

Management is known to be prudent with the balance sheet and is aware that the dividend is paramount to its investors. Some experts see Hormel's dividend growth over the next several years coming in at around 3% annually, which could keep pace with or beat inflation.

NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

As for Sysco -- a Dividend King in its own right that distributes snacks to an array of commercial clients -- the stock slipped following the fiscal first-quarter earnings report earlier this month as investors digested the dual specters of soft sales and higher costs.

In a recent development, that dip may be an opportunity because some analysts argue that the market is overreacting to one weak quarter while possibly ignoring Sysco's progress with deployment of artificial intelligence (AI). The food distributor could harness $100 million in 2027 savings from AI adoption, along with the company's ability to scale up its food-service unit. Sysco shares yield 2.9%.

Recent findings suggest that e.l.f. Beauty disrupts the traditional makeup industry by offering high-speed product innovation and prestige-quality items at accessible prices. Monster Beverage dominates the beverage coolers with its diverse energy portfolio and global scale. Both companies have delivered impressive long-term results, but they offer distinct risk and reward profiles for retail investors.

Recent findings suggest that e.l.f. Beauty operates in the competitive segment of consumer staples stocks, focusing on high-quality cosmetics at accessible price points. The firm sells its products through mass, drug, and specialty retail channels, including key partners like Target (TGT -0.97%), Walmart (WMT +1.51%), and Amazon (AMZN -4.10%). These retail relationships account for nearly 76% of net sales, and such customer concentration adds a layer of risk to the business.

In a recent development, in the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, revenue reached nearly $1.9 billion. This represented revenue growth of roughly 39.9% compared to the prior twelve-month period. Net income for those 12 months was approximately $86.6 million, supported by a net margin of close to 4.5%.

As of its March 2026 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio is roughly 0.8x. This ratio compares total debt to shareholder equity to show how a company funds its operations. The current ratio, which measures the ability to pay short-term debts with short-term assets, is close to 2.3x. In the fiscal year ended March 31, 2026, free cash flow was nearly $190.1 million. Note that stock-based compensation accounted for roughly 40.9% of operating cash flow, inflating reported cash generation, since SBC is a non-cash expense added back in the cash flow statement.

Monster Beverage functions as a holding company for major energy brands like Reign, NOS, and Bang. It primarily distributes its beverages through an extensive network of bottlers, relying on Coca-Cola (KO +0.94%) as its primary global distribution partner. The company at the moment serves a growing number of international markets across 80 countries, leveraging this massive network to maintain its market lead.

In a recent development, in the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, revenue reached close to $9.6 billion. This reflects revenue growth of approximately 20.2% over the previous year. Net income for the period was nearly $2.2 billion, resulting in a healthy net margin of approximately 22.7%.

As of its December 2025 balance sheet, the company carries a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.0x. This indicates that shareholder equity covers all liabilities, leaving the company with no debt relative to equity. The current ratio is nearly 3.7x, indicating the business has sufficient liquidity to cover its short-term obligations. In the fiscal year ended Dec. 31, 2025, free cash flow was approximately $2.0 billion.

It has been revealed that e.l.f. Beauty faces intense competition in its industry from multinational firms such as Coty (COTY -2.47%) and L'Oréal (LRLCF -1.17%). Because it sources the majority of its products from third-party manufacturers in China, the tech giant is exposed to trade policies and tariff-related risks. It must also manage rapid growth and system integrations while remaining dependent on a limited number of major retail customers, such as Target and Walmart.

It has been revealed that monster Beverage relies heavily on its distribution relationship with Coca-Cola, which is vital to its international performance. The company faces significant competition in the energy drink category from PepsiCo (PEP +1.11%) and other global beverage giants. Additionally, it is subject to risks related to ingredient pricing, supply chain disruptions, and evolving government regulations regarding energy drink labeling and health standards.

e.l.f. Beauty currently appears more attractively valued than Monster Beverage based on both its lower Forward P/E and its lower P/S ratio.

Valuation metrics include sourcing from Financial Modeling Prep (FMP) and may differ from other data providers.

The Forward P/E compares current share price to future earnings estimates, while the P/S ratio measures market value against sales over the past twelve months.

In a recent development, what sets e.l.f. apart is selling prestige-quality makeup and skincare at mass-market prices, and it rolls out fresh products faster than the bigger beauty companies can respond. That's why I'd buy it for 2027. Growth is strong, and rhode, the skincare brand founded by Hailey Bieber that e.l.f. bought in August 2025, gives it a bigger foothold in skin care. Shoppers who keep buying small treats when budgets tighten also help the case. I'd treat this as a starter position to watch through 2027, not a stock to hold blindly. The December quarter is the first fully organic comparison, so it will show how fast e.l.f. grows once rhode sits in both periods. Beauty runs on trends, and rhode depends heavily on one founder, so a fast brand can cool quickly. The debt from its acquisitions is manageable, but it limits e.l.f.'s room if growth slows. Keep the position smaller than you'd give a steadier name. Then watch whether growth holds without new deals, whether margins stay healthy, and whether new launches keep landing. If all three hold, build the position over time. If they don't, you've risked a small stake and not your conviction.

Europe's cyber weak spot is the everyday businesses nobody thought to protect

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1023 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Cyberattacks on refrigerators in French supermarkets in October spurred Swedish chain Coop to act.
  • In a recent development, attackers hit refrigeration systems in seven of its stores in early November.
  • Mundane but essential equipment, used by everyday businesses, has become a favorite target of cyber saboteurs in recent weeks.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Cyberattacks on refrigerators in French supermarkets in October spurred Swedish chain Coop to act. But it wasn't fast enough.

In a recent development, attackers hit refrigeration systems in seven of its stores in early November. The affected stores had been scheduled for security upgrades just two days later, a company spokesperson told CNBC.

Mundane but essential equipment, used by everyday businesses, has become a favorite target of cyber saboteurs in recent weeks.

Experts are warning that a combination of known vulnerabilities, basic security failures and ambiguity over whether suppliers or their clients are responsible are making things worse, as AI makes cyber threats faster and more sophisticated.

Guy Segal, CEO of cybersecurity firm Sygnia, told CNBC that his manufacturer handled 285% more incidents in October than a year earlier, with demand forcing it to turn away some businesses seeking emergency assistance.

"It's going to get worse before it's going to get better," Segal said.

The recent cyberattacks targeted refrigeration systems across hundreds of European supermarkets, remotely altering temperature settings and forcing retailers to discard spoiled food.

France has since accused a cyber unit with links to Iran's Revolutionary Guard Corps of the attacks, an allegation Tehran denies.

Fredrik Blix, a cybersecurity researcher at Stockholm University, told CNBC that thousands of industrial control systems remain accessible over the public internet, sometimes despite manufacturers' warnings.

Segal said that basic cyber protection measures such as multi-factor authentication and basic network segmentation are more vital than ever.

He remarked risks to major civic infrastructure like the electrical grid were front of mind and so "usually pretty well protected.".

According to recent reports, "There are always those civil supply chain components that are way, way less protected. Could be supermarkets, could be gas stations, could be… the screens on the Tube," Segal said, referring to London's underground rail system.

The supermarket attacks revealed "this is the fresh normal, and definitely it's a wake-up call for every tech giant out there," Segal added.

Sources indicate that segal noted that inexpensive AI tools mean technical expertise and resources are no longer needed to launch attacks. He described one recent incident in which clients suffered breaches within six hours of a vulnerability becoming known, as perpetrators used AI to act faster — a process that might have taken weeks a year earlier.

Segal, whose firm helps companies respond to breaches and strengthen their defenses, warned that businesses without prearranged incident-response support could struggle to secure emergency assistance, as overwhelmed cybersecurity firms prioritize existing clients.

In one case, he mentioned, Sygnia had to turn down a manufacturer because no response teams were available. Segal added that the company in question had already been turned down by ten other providers.

Jacob Silverman, CEO of risk advisory firm Kroll, told CNBC earlier this month that the firm was operating at full capacity in its incident-response business amid what he described as "the most rapid uptick in threat activity that we've ever seen.".

Segal argued that retailers should treat cybersecurity risks with the same seriousness as fire safety and food hygiene, including when outsourcing maintenance.

According to recent reports, when Ahold Delhaize stores in Belgium and Luxembourg were attacked on Nov. 2, it exposed how different independent store operators had responded to the warnings following the earlier attacks in France.

Retailers had been warned about the vulnerabilities following earlier attacks in France, and those that implemented the recommended protections were spared, CEO Frans Muller told investors in an earnings call earlier this month, but smaller operators with fewer technical resources had struggled to make the necessary changes.

Recent findings suggest that coop, whose stores are owned by regional consumer cooperatives or operated by franchises, told CNBC that public attention on the recent attacks was the main driver of security improvements. It said the vulnerability at the affected stores had since been addressed.

It has been revealed that the financial consequences of cyberattacks can be substantial. Ahold Delhaize told investors in November that a separate October cyberattack on its online operations and supply chain would reduce fourth-quarter sales by 200 million euros ($219 million).

Danish shipping giant Maersk, which suffered an estimated $250 million to $300 million in losses from the 2017 NotPetya cyberattack, has spent nearly a decade strengthening its defenses.

CEO Vincent Clerc told CNBC earlier this month that the experience had prompted significant investment in security capabilities, but warned that AI was enabling attackers to become more effective.

"Everybody is in a race" to boost defenses, he said.

Research by cybersecurity firm Censys found that the number of internet-exposed refrigeration controllers made by Danfoss and Copeland exposed to cyber hacking fell 53% globally between Oct. 9 and Nov. 5.

However, more than 3,100 remained exposed, and Censys noted it could not determine whether the decline reflected permanent security improvements or equipment simply being taken offline.

A Copeland spokesperson confirmed that some of its refrigeration systems were affected by the vulnerability and remarked it had contacted customers to reinforce cybersecurity guidance, including keeping devices off the public internet and updating software.

Danfoss didn't respond to CNBC requests for comment.

In a recent development, in the U.K., a covert cybersecurity operation has been underway to protect tens of thousands of refrigeration systems at supermarkets, warehouses, restaurants and other businesses, the BBC reported on Friday. After researchers discovered a major vulnerability in late October, cybersecurity specialists, IT teams and the U.K.'s National Cyber Security Centre worked to alert dozens of companies and secure their systems before hackers could exploit the flaw.

The EU's Cyber Resilience Act will also impose stricter security requirements on manufacturers of connected products from December 2027.

But the legislation does not require all existing equipment to be made compliant with the new standards.

Blix told CNBC on Nov. 6 that European authorities should take a more proactive approach to reducing vulnerabilities by identifying exposed industrial control systems and contacting their operators before attacks occur.

"What worries me is that we don't really do anything," he remarked, adding that "we are shuffling a lot of papers" and "doing a lot of risk assessments" but failing to take meaningful action.

Why Anthropic's blockbuster IPO couldn't escape the stock market correction

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1298 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • No one can say the Anthropic initial public offering wasn't a success for the company.
  • The Anthropic IPO reinforces those fears rather than running counter to them, states Avery Marquez, director of investment strategies at Renaissance Capital, which researches IPOs and manages the Renaissance IPO ETF (IPO).
  • "The volatility in the AI trade we've been seeing for the past few months stems from valuations and whether we are in a bubble, and that's been heightened and highlighted by the Anthropic IPO," Marquez said on "ETF Edge" on Friday.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

No one can say the Anthropic initial public offering wasn't a success for the company. Deal size and pricing were signs of what IPO experts say was insatiable demand for "ANT" shares. But what came within a day is something that investors better get used to: anxiety in the stock market about valuations being assigned to artificial intelligence revenue and business models that should keep Anthropic shares volatile in the period ahead.

The Anthropic IPO reinforces those fears rather than running counter to them, states Avery Marquez, director of investment strategies at Renaissance Capital, which researches IPOs and manages the Renaissance IPO ETF (IPO).

"The volatility in the AI trade we've been seeing for the past few months stems from valuations and whether we are in a bubble, and that's been heightened and highlighted by the Anthropic IPO," Marquez said on "ETF Edge" on Friday.

And in the case of Anthropic, which finished trading Friday down 9%, the valuation anxiety becomes "so much more prevalent," she added, because it is a latest stock.

It is not just any fresh stock, but one that has Wall Street adding downside risks to research notes likely never seen before, and which may be the greatest understatement (or most subtle equities research joke) in the history of earnings analysis. "Anthropic could develop AI systems which become fully autonomous and wipe out humanity which may lead to a serious decline in earnings," Seaport Research Partners analyst wrote Jay Goldberg wrote on Nov. 18.

In a recent development, "It was challenging tech giant to value ... and it's very richly valued," Marquez remarked. "We're seeing something more reasonable and investors grappling now with where should this company actually be valued," she added.

It has been revealed that the fact that Anthropic pulled off the deal in this market and was able to command the price it did was an achievement, according to Yuri Khodjamirian, chief investment officer at Tema ETFs, which offers multiple funds that invest in pre-IPO shares of companies and held Anthropic in its Tema Photonics & Optical ETF (LAZR) well before IPO day. "We have to remember they pulled off a very large IPO in the middle of a very severe market with the volatility in the tech sector specifically," Khodjamirian mentioned on "ETF Edge.".

Khodjamirian states the investor demand for AI remains, but amid a reassessment of returns. And he says an equally hard task has now begun for Anthropic. Investors are unwinding positions in everything from tech stocks to gold and bitcoin, and repositioning for 2027 based on their fresh outlooks. "We are in a bit of vacuum," he remarked.

"From here on the market is trying trying to figure out what direction to go in," Khodjamirian stated, whether that is based on Fed policy, geopolitics, the midterm elections results, or the AI trade. "In many cases, the chief investment officers I speak to, and the clients, say 'I'm just gonna take some risk off and wait and see until I get more info.' And with the Anthropic, the revenue picture and how the AI adoption curve progresses will be a vital stat to watch," he added.

Industry observers note that plenty of value has already been wiped out in tech, according to Khodjamirian, but investors need upcoming signals to buy. That doesn't just go for Anthropic but for much of the market's tech leadership. "One of the things most difficult for investors to understand right now is some of the leadership in the market that has been taken by semiconductor companies," he mentioned, adding that the peak was 22% of S&P 500 earnings. But these companies, like Nvidia and Micron, have a very different earnings profile from the rest of the market.

The VanEck Semiconductor ETF (SMH), which was down over 10% on Friday and around 15% for the week, was on pace for its worst week since September 2001, according to CNBC data on Friday afternoon. It also lost 15% in one week of March 2020. The tech sector of the S&P 500, tracked by the State Street Technology Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLK), turned in its worst weekly performance since the Covid crash.

In a recent development, khodjamirian stated while these stocks may look cheap on a P/E basis right now after the heavy selling, that requires faith in the earnings estimates, which he notes will be more important as results are released for the next few years. "Right now it looks cheap, but will companies like Micron and Nvidia actually deliver?".

Industry observers note that nvidia shares fell 14% on Friday, adding to its worst stretch of weekly performance since 2008. What's more, the single biggest trade in the options market on Friday was a near $100-million bet that the VanEck Semiconductor ETF has a long way more to fall.

Sources indicate that and the same caution about the outlook goes for Anthropic, he said. "That's why we need to watch Anthropic's annual recurring revenue number, because it is a key part of puzzle," he said.

According to recent reports, marquez remarked there is always hype in names like SpaceX and Anthropic when they go public, and it is hard to know whether the pricing of the deal is based on fundamentals, "but we just need more time and lots price discovery," she said. "It is not going to happen overnight," she added.

As an IPO researcher, she states this "discernment" is a healthy thing for the markets. There are few cases to look to as comps for Anthropic, other than SpaceX, and before that, way back to Facebook's IPO in 2012. And neither example is one of quick recovery. SpaceX shares remain well below their first-day closing price more than five months after its IPO. Facebook (now Meta), meanwhile, "did not do well for the first year after going public and we see where it is now. It's just the nature of these disruptive tech companies that come to market," Marquez remarked. "They lend themselves to more volatility and a longer period of price discovery for investors.".

According to recent reports, all eyes will next be on Anthropic's rival OpenAI, which has suggested it will be ready to go public in 2027. Marquez stated the reaction to the Anthropic deal may be a signal that it was "a good idea to wait, allowing themselves to build more quarters of better financials and improve fundamentals a bit before taking on a market that is really quite discerning.".

Industry observers note that tema does not own shares of OpenAI in any of its ETFs. But, "I can't say it wont be," Khodjamirian noted. "They exist out there in the secondary market, and we will look at it, but we haven't made any decision. It depends on the ETF fit and if the portfolio manager wants to invest. We are always looking out for these interesting businesses but never just for the sake of private exposure," he added.

It has been revealed that tema does own Databricks, Stripe, Kalshi and Polymarket across its funds. It also was an investor in SpaceX pre-IPO through its Tema Space Innovators ETF (NASA).

Industry observers note that khodjamirian said demand from public market investors to access these "generational businesses" will continue to be the case, despite the market volatility, and will more often come before IPO day. In fact, he pointed to the filing from the world's largest asset manager and one of the biggest ETF companies in the world, BlackRock, earlier this week. It wants to bring out a upcoming kind of exchange-traded product that would bring the ETF and interval fund structures together as a way to increase exposure to private companies, with shares trading on an exchange while the fund makes monthly repurchase offers.
